docs.title: FreeXmlToolkit Documentation
docs.text:
Free, open-source desktop app for XML, XSD, XSLT, Schematron and JSON – Windows, macOS and Linux. No registration, no admin rights needed.

🪟 Windows x64 · Windows 10/11

Download .exe installer
  • MSI package – for silent / Group Policy deployment
  • Portable ZIP – no installation, extract and run
  • Scoop – scoop install karlkauc/freexmltoolkit

🍎 macOS Apple Silicon & Intel

Download .dmg (Apple Silicon)
  • Intel .dmg – for Intel-based Macs
  • .pkg installer (Apple Silicon) · .pkg (Intel)
  • Portable ZIP (Apple Silicon) · Portable ZIP (Intel)
  • Homebrew – brew install --cask karlkauc/tap/freexmltoolkit

🐧 Linux x64

Download .deb package
  • .rpm package – Fedora, RHEL, openSUSE
  • .deb is for Ubuntu, Debian and Linux Mint
  • Portable ZIP – any distribution, extract and run

Latest release: see GitHub · All downloads and release notes on GitHub · Licensed under Apache 2.0 · Source code · ♥ Sponsor

docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
FreeXmlToolkit is a free desktop application for working with XML files. It helps you edit, validate, transform, and secure your XML documents - all in one place.

A tour of the main features - click to open it full screen

docs.title: What Can You Do With FreeXmlToolkit?
docs.text:
• Edit XML files with smart auto-completion and syntax highlighting
  • Validate XML against XSD schemas, DTDs and RELAX NG schemas to check for errors
  • Validate JSON against JSON Schemas, auto-detected from the document's $schema member
  • Transform XML into other formats (HTML, PDF, Text)
  • Sign XML documents with digital certificates
  • Create business rules with Schematron validation
  • Generate documentation from your XSD schemas
  • Compare and merge XML files by structure, compare folders, convert XML ↔ JSON ↔ YAML
  • Open huge files (gigabytes) in the Large File Viewer
  • Automate with the command line (fxt-cli) and projects
  • Extend it with plugins — industry plugins for ISO 20022, ebInterface, FinDatEx and XBRL included
  • Work in English or German, accessible, centrally administrable

docs.text:

docs.title: Works On All Platforms
docs.text: FreeXmlToolkit runs on Windows (x64), macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Linux (x64) - as an installer, a native package or a portable ZIP, and via Scoop and Homebrew. The Installation page explains every format and the package managers.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Download FreeXmlToolkit with the buttons above; the Installation guide covers every package format, Scoop and Homebrew.

docs.title: Your First Steps
docs.text:
1. Open a file: The app opens on the Welcome page - use Open File (Ctrl+O), the Explorer activity, or drag files into the window. No file at hand? Click Open an Example on the Welcome page to open a small order document that already has a schema and a stylesheet, or pick a task under What do you want to do? (for example Validate an XML file)
  2. Edit multiple files: The shell handles XML, XSD, XSLT, Schematron and JSON files in tabs, each with Text / Tree / Graphic views - HTML files get a rendered read-only Preview view instead
  3. Start editing: Type < to see auto-completion suggestions
  4. Validate: Use the Validation activity (or the toolbar's Validate button, F8) to check your document for errors
  5. Reach every tool: Pick a tool from the activity bar on the left (Explorer, Search, Favorites, Validation, Transform, Schema, Schema Library, PDF/FOP, Signature, FundsXML, Settings). Help, the documentation and About are in the Help menu (also F1 or the ? button in the header)

Learn more: Unified Shell Guide

docs.title: Sample Files
docs.text:
The application includes example files in the examples/ folder to help you get started:

  • xml/ - Sample XML documents (FundsXML4 instances, valid and deliberately invalid)
  • xsd/ - Sample XSD schemas (including FundsXML 4.2.11)
  • xslt/ - XSLT stylesheets (HTML reports, JSON and CSV export)
  • xsl/ - XSL-FO stylesheets for PDF reports
  • xquery/ - XQuery 3.1 data-quality checks
  • xpath/ - XPath 3.1 snippets for the Query Console
  • xproc/ - XProc 3.0 pipelines (identity, slimming, CSV/JSON export, reports)
  • schematron/ - Schematron business rules
  • catalog/ - OASIS XML catalog example for the Schema Library
  • json/ - JSON Schema validation demos ($schema auto-binding, valid/invalid instances, Draft-07 / 2019-09 / 2020-12 dialects)
  • signature/ - Signed XML document with demo keystore
  • templates/ - XML snippet templates
  • profiles/ - XML generation profiles

docs.title: Security Features
docs.text: This page describes the security measures built into FreeXmlToolkit to protect you from XML-based attacks.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
When working with XML files, there are several potential security risks - especially when processing untrusted documents or stylesheets. FreeXmlToolkit includes built-in protections against these common attack vectors:

Protection What It Prevents XXE Protection Malicious files reading data from your computer XSLT/XQuery Extension Security Untrusted stylesheets running code on your system SSRF Protection Documents accessing your internal network Path Traversal Protection Files accessing restricted system directories XPath Injection Protection Malicious input breaking XPath queries Update Integrity Verification Tampered or man-in-the-middle update downloads

These protections work automatically in the background - you do not need to configure them for normal use.

docs.title: What Is XXE?
docs.text: XXE is a type of attack where a malicious XML document tries to read files from your computer or access network resources. This happens through special "entity" declarations in the XML that reference external files.

docs.title: Example of a Malicious XML
docs.text:
This is what a dangerous XML file might look like (FreeXmlToolkit blocks this):

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE data [
  <!ENTITY steal SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">
]>
<data>&steal;</data>

If processed without protection, this could expose sensitive files from your computer.

docs.title: What FreeXmlToolkit Blocks
docs.text: Attack Type Description Status External file access Reading local files via file:// URIs Blocked External DTD loading Loading DTD definitions from remote servers Blocked, except for DTD validation (see below) Parameter entities Using %entity; to include external content Blocked, except DTD modules during DTD validation Entity expansion bombs "Billion laughs" denial-of-service attacks Limited (see below)

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The parsers that read your documents (the editor's model, validation, transformations) are created with secure settings that: - Disable external general entities - Disable external parameter entities - Disable external DTD loading - Turn on the JAXP secure-processing mode, whose built-in limits cap entity expansion

Secure processing stops a document after 100,000 entity expansions. The same settings apply when XPath, XQuery, XSLT, grid formulas and filters read a document. In the editor, internal entities are kept as references and not expanded. See the threat model for the details and the known limits.

docs.title: What This Means for You
docs.text:
Normal XML files work without issues. You can: - Open and edit any XML file - Validate against XSD schemas - Transform with XSLT stylesheets - Work with XML that contains internal (non-external) entities

External entities are never read. If an XML file relies on external entities (<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "…">) for content, those entities stay unresolved. This is intentional for security.

DTD validation is the one place where DTDs are loaded: a document with a <!DOCTYPE> is validated against its DTD, which — with its parameter-entity modules — is read only from XML catalogs, the Schema Library, local files, or http(s) through the schema cache (proxy settings, internal addresses refused). External general entities stay off and entity expansion stays limited. Settings → Network & Security → Validate documents against their DTD turns it off; administrators can lock it with security.dtd.allowed=false. See Schema Support.

docs.title: What Are XSLT Extensions?
docs.text: XSLT 3.0 and XQuery can include "extension functions" that call Java code directly from your stylesheet. While this is powerful for advanced users, it can be dangerous if you process untrusted stylesheets.

docs.title: Example of a Dangerous Stylesheet
docs.text:
This XSLT tries to execute system commands (FreeXmlToolkit blocks this by default):

<xsl:stylesheet version="2.0"
    xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform"
    xmlns:rt="java:java.lang.Runtime">
    <xsl:template match="/">
        <xsl:variable name="runtime" select="rt:getRuntime()"/>
        <xsl:variable name="proc" select="rt:exec($runtime, 'whoami')"/>
    </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>

docs.title: What Is Blocked by Default
docs.text: Extension Type Description Default Status Java namespace (java:) Direct calls to Java classes Blocked Reflexive extensions Runtime method invocation Blocked External functions Custom extension functions Blocked

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: FreeXmlToolkit uses Saxon for XSLT/XQuery processing. By default, the ALLOW_EXTERNAL_FUNCTIONS feature is disabled, preventing stylesheets from executing arbitrary Java code.

docs.title: Enabling Extensions (Advanced Users)
docs.text:
If you need to use Java extensions in your XSLT transformations:

  1. Open Settings (gear icon at the bottom of the activity bar)
  2. Find the PARSER card (group Schemas & Validation)
  3. Enable Allow XSLT extension functions and click Save Settings

Warning: Only enable this if you trust all XSLT stylesheets you will process. Malicious stylesheets could: - Read files from your computer - Execute system commands - Access network resources - Modify or delete files

The setting is stored as: 

security.xslt.allow.extensions=true

When extensions are enabled, you will see a warning message in the application log.

docs.title: What Is SSRF?
docs.text: SSRF attacks trick an application into making requests to internal network resources. In XML processing, this can happen when schemas or stylesheets reference URLs.

docs.title: What FreeXmlToolkit Blocks
docs.text:
When loading remote schemas (via xs:import or xs:include with HTTP URLs), FreeXmlToolkit blocks access to:

Address Type Examples Why Blocked Localhost 127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1 Prevents access to local services Private networks (Class A) 10.0.0.0 - 10.255.255.255 Blocks internal network access Private networks (Class B) 172.16.0.0 - 172.31.255.255 Blocks internal network access Private networks (Class C) 192.168.0.0 - 192.168.255.255 Blocks internal network access Link-local addresses 169.254.0.0 - 169.254.255.255 Blocks auto-configured addresses Cloud metadata endpoints 169.254.169.254 Blocks AWS/Azure/GCP metadata Multicast addresses Various Blocks broadcast addresses

docs.title: What Is Allowed
docs.text: Address Type Examples Status Public internet URLs https://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema.xsd Allowed Local file URLs file:///path/to/schema.xsd Allowed Only HTTP/HTTPS http://, https:// Other protocols blocked

docs.title: What This Means for You
docs.text:
Public schemas work normally. You can reference standard schemas from W3C and other public sources.

Internal network schemas are blocked. If you need to load schemas from: - Your company's internal server (e.g., http://192.168.1.100/schemas/) - Localhost development servers (e.g., http://localhost:8080/)

You should: 1. Download the schema files to your local machine 2. Reference them using file paths or file:// URLs 3. Place them in the same directory as your XML files for relative references

docs.title: Automatic Import Resolution Is Covered Too
docs.text:
When an imported schema file cannot be found locally or through the Schema Library and XML catalogs, the toolkit can download it from the import's schemaLocation URL or its namespace URL (see Automatic Resolution of Imported Schemas). These downloads go through the same SSRF protection: only public http/https addresses are contacted, and the downloaded content is verified to be a real XML Schema before it is used. Downloaded schemas are cached in ~/.freeXmlToolkit/cache/schemas/. In addition, a downloaded import or include is copied next to the schema that references it, under its original name, so the folder works without the network next time; an existing file is never overwritten and your schema file is never rewritten. Start the application with -Dfxt.schema.localCopies=false to keep downloads in the cache only.

-Dfxt.schema.namespaceFallback=false turns off the namespace-URL fallback and the downloads of the bundled Schema Library entries. It does not stop every download: a schemaLocation URL in a document or an import is still fetched. See Operation without internet for the full list of network connections.

docs.title: What Is Path Traversal?
docs.text: Path traversal attacks use special characters like ../ to access files outside the intended directory. This could allow a malicious document to read or write to sensitive system locations.

docs.title: What FreeXmlToolkit Blocks
docs.text: Protection Description Excessive parent traversals More than 5 levels of ../ are flagged System directory access Writes to /etc, /bin, C:\Windows, etc. Encoded sequences URL-encoded traversals like %2e%2e/ Double-encoded sequences %252e and similar bypass attempts Null byte injection Paths containing \0 characters Symbolic link escapes Following symlinks outside base directories

docs.title: Protected System Directories
docs.text:
Windows: - C:\Windows\ - C:\Program Files\ - C:\ProgramData\

Linux/macOS: - /etc/ - /bin/, /sbin/ - /usr/bin/, /usr/sbin/ - /var/ - /root/ - /boot/

docs.title: Affected Features
docs.text: Path validation applies to: - Schema includes (xs:include, xs:import with relative paths) - Linked file detection (auto-linking in the unified editor) - Export paths (saving output files) - Any relative file references in XML documents

docs.title: What This Means for You
docs.text:
Normal file operations work fine. You can: - Open files anywhere on your computer - Save files to your documents folder - Use relative paths within your project directories

Suspicious paths are blocked. If you see a path traversal warning, check that your schema or stylesheet references do not contain unusual ../ sequences or try to access system directories.

docs.title: What Is XPath Injection?
docs.text: XPath injection is similar to SQL injection - it happens when user input is inserted directly into XPath queries without proper escaping. This could allow malicious input to modify the query's behavior.

docs.title: How FreeXmlToolkit Protects You
docs.text: When you use the XPath/XQuery snippet system with parameters, all parameter values are automatically escaped before being inserted into queries.

docs.title: How Value Escaping Works
docs.text: Input Contains Escape Method No quotes Wrapped in single quotes: 'value' Single quotes only Wrapped in double quotes: "value" Double quotes only Wrapped in single quotes: 'value' Both quote types Uses concat() function for safe combination

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
If you have a snippet with parameter ${searchTerm} and the user enters:

O'Brien "Bob"

The system generates:

concat('O', "'", 'Brien "Bob"')

This prevents the user input from breaking out of the string literal and modifying the query structure.

docs.title: What This Means for You
docs.text: This protection is automatic and transparent. You do not need to do anything special - just use the parameter syntax ${paramName} in your snippets, and values will be properly escaped.

docs.title: What Is This?
docs.text: When FreeXmlToolkit downloads an application update, it verifies that the downloaded file is exactly the one published by the official release - and was not tampered with in transit (for example by a man-in-the-middle on an untrusted network) or swapped on the download server.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. The update package (a ZIP) is downloaded from the official GitHub release over HTTPS.
  2. Before the package is extracted or launched, its SHA-256 checksum is computed locally.
  3. That checksum is compared against the SHA-256 digest that GitHub publishes for the release asset, fetched over a separate TLS-protected connection to the GitHub API.
  4. If the checksums do not match, the update is aborted and the downloaded file is deleted. Nothing is installed.

This means that even if an attacker could intercept or replace the download, the mismatch would be detected and the update refused.

Note: The certificate-validation bypass setting (ssl.trustAllCerts, used only for connection testing) never applies to update downloads. Update traffic always validates TLS certificates.

docs.title: When No Published Checksum Is Available
docs.text:
GitHub only began publishing per-asset digests in 2025, so some older releases may not have one. By default, when no trustworthy digest is available, the update proceeds with a warning written to the application log (preserving compatibility with those releases).

If you prefer a stricter policy, you can require a verified checksum for every update - any update without one will be refused:

update.requireChecksum=true
Behavior update.requireChecksum=false (default) update.requireChecksum=true Checksum present and matches Update proceeds Update proceeds Checksum present but mismatches Update aborted Update aborted No checksum published Update proceeds (logged warning) Update aborted

docs.title: What This Means for You
docs.text: For normal use you do not need to change anything - integrity verification runs automatically. Set update.requireChecksum=true only if your environment requires that no update is ever installed without a cryptographically verified checksum.

docs.title: Finding Security Settings
docs.text:
1. Open FreeXmlToolkit
  2. Open Settings (gear icon at the bottom of the activity bar)
  3. The relevant options are spread over two cards: PARSER (group Schemas & Validation) and SECURITY (group Network & Security). Typing a word such as XSLT or certificates into the search field of the Settings side panel finds them too.

docs.title: Available Settings
docs.text: Card Setting Description Default PARSER Allow XSLT extension functions Enable Java extension functions in XSLT Off (secure) SECURITY Trust all certificates Accept any TLS certificate for HTTPS downloads (schemas, catalogs, FundsXML, telemetry). Never for the update check and update downloads. Leave off unless a corporate proxy re-signs traffic Off (secure)

docs.title: Security Property Reference
docs.text:
For advanced users, security settings are stored in the application properties file (~/.freeXmlToolkit/FreeXmlToolkit.properties; earlier versions kept it in the working directory; it is copied over automatically on the first start):

Property Values Description security.xslt.allow.extensions true / false Enable/disable Java extensions in XSLT update.requireChecksum true / false Require a verified SHA-256 checksum for every update; refuse updates that have no published checksum (default false)

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Keep extensions disabled unless you specifically need them
  2. Only process trusted stylesheets if you enable extensions
  3. Download remote schemas to local files when working with internal network resources
  4. Review XML files before processing if they come from untrusted sources
  5. Check validation errors - they may indicate blocked security threats

docs.title: "External entity not resolved"
docs.text:
Cause: Your XML references an external DTD or entity that was blocked for security.

Solution: If you need the entity definitions, manually include them in your XML file or convert the external DTD to a local file.

docs.title: "URL blocked for security reasons"
docs.text:
Cause: You tried to load a schema from a localhost or private network address.

Solution: Download the schema file to your local machine and reference it as a local file.

docs.title: "XSLT extension function not available"
docs.text:
Cause: Your stylesheet uses Java extension functions, which are disabled by default.

Solution: If you trust the stylesheet, enable XSLT extensions in settings. Otherwise, modify the stylesheet to not use extensions.

docs.title: "Path traversal detected"
docs.text:
Cause: A file reference contains suspicious ../ sequences that would access files outside the expected directory.

Solution: Check your schema imports and includes for unusual paths. Use absolute paths or properly relative paths that stay within your project directory.

docs.title: "Integrity verification failed" during an update
docs.text:
Cause: The downloaded update did not match the checksum published for the release. This usually indicates a corrupted download or interference on the network, and the update was refused.

Solution: Retry the update on a trusted network connection. If it keeps failing, download the latest release manually from the official GitHub releases page.

docs.title: An update was refused with "no published checksum"
docs.text:
Cause: You set update.requireChecksum=true, and the target release does not have a published checksum.

Solution: Either update manually from the official release page, or set update.requireChecksum=false to allow updates that have no published checksum (the default behavior).

docs.title: Technical Reference
docs.text: For developers and security professionals, here are the specific protections implemented:

docs.title: XML Parser Configuration
docs.text: All XML parsers use these security features: - http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl = false (DOCTYPE allowed, but entities disabled) - http://xml.org/sax/features/external-general-entities = false - http://xml.org/sax/features/external-parameter-entities = false - http://apache.org/xml/features/nonvalidating/load-external-dtd = false - javax.xml.XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING = true - Entity reference expansion = disabled

docs.title: XSLT/XQuery Configuration (Saxon)
docs.text:
• Feature.ALLOW_EXTERNAL_FUNCTIONS = false (by default)
  • Configurable via application settings

docs.title: Update Integrity Verification
docs.text:
• Downloaded update artifact is hashed with SHA-256 and compared against the digest GitHub publishes for the release asset (retrieved over TLS from the Releases API).
  • Mismatch aborts the update and deletes the artifact before any extraction or launch.
  • The ssl.trustAllCerts connection-test bypass is never applied to update downloads, which always perform standard certificate validation.
  • update.requireChecksum=true additionally refuses any update that has no published digest.

docs.title: URL Validation
docs.text: Uses Java's InetAddress class to check: - isLoopbackAddress() - blocks localhost - isLinkLocalAddress() - blocks 169.254.x.x - isSiteLocalAddress() - blocks private networks - Special check for 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata)

docs.title: Path Validation
docs.text:
• Canonical path comparison for traversal detection
  • Regex patterns for encoded sequences
  • Blocklist of system directories
  • Symbolic link resolution for escape detection

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text: This page documents the accessibility audit of FreeXmlToolkit (version 2.10, November 2026): what was checked, what was fixed, and what is still open. The reference is WCAG 2.1 level AA, the standard that EN 301 549 applies to the user interface of desktop software.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Area Result Names for screen readers (buttons, input fields) All buttons and input fields of the shell have a name (before: 38 unnamed buttons, 22 unlabelled fields) Text contrast (light and dark theme) All text colours reach 4.5:1 on their backgrounds (before: 10 combinations below) Keyboard Every function of the shell can be reached from the keyboard, except four options of the grid view header Visual views The graphic XSD view and the grid view are drawn on a canvas and are not readable by screen readers; the Text and Tree views show the same content Screen reader support of the platform Windows (Narrator, NVDA, JAWS) and macOS (VoiceOver) through JavaFX; Linux: none (JavaFX has no screen reader bridge on Linux) Interface language English and German (Settings → Language)

The automated checks run with the test suite, so the results stay true for later changes.

docs.title: How it was checked
docs.text:
1. Automated audit of the user interface (AccessibilityAuditTest). The test opens the shell, visits every activity (Explorer, Search, Favorites, Validation, Transform, Schema, Schema Library, PDF / FOP, Signature, FundsXML, Settings), opens an XML document in the Text, Tree and Grid views, and walks the scene graph. It reports:

    • buttons without a name: no text and no accessible text (a tooltip alone is not announced);
    • input fields without a label: no accessible text, no associated label (Label.labelFor) and no prompt text;
    • buttons outside the keyboard tab order;
    • content drawn on a canvas.

    The test fails when a button or field without a name appears, or a control outside the tab order that has no documented keyboard alternative (list below). 2. Contrast of the design tokens (ContrastTest). The test computes the WCAG contrast ratio of every text colour on the backgrounds it is used on, in the light and the dark theme, and requires 4.5:1. 3. Review of the keyboard paths (menu bar, shortcuts, focus indication) and of the views that are drawn rather than built from controls.

The audit did not include a session with a screen reader user or manual testing with NVDA or VoiceOver; that is the recommended next step (see Open points).

docs.title: Names for screen readers
docs.text:
Icon-only buttons (toolbar, side panel headers, favourites stars, Inspector actions) only had a tooltip, so screen readers announced "button". Input fields in the settings and panels had a visible label next to them that was not associated with the field.

  • Every window now names its controls automatically (AccessibleNames): a button without text takes the first line of its tooltip, a card button (Welcome page) the title inside it; an input field is associated with the label right before it (also in the same row of a grid). The names follow the interface language.
  • The few controls without tooltip or label got an explicit name (Validation panel ⋮ menu, the favourites and recent menus of the Transform and Validation panels, the ◀ / ▶ favourites buttons, the language selection, the output method, the proxy test address).

docs.title: Contrast
docs.text: Colour Light theme Dark theme Secondary hints (-fxt-text-muted), e.g. explanations under settings #8a93a0 → #667080 (2.8–3.1:1 → 4.6–5.0:1) #6b7480 → #858f9c (3.3–3.9:1 → 4.8–5.3:1) Primary colour as text (links, selected entries) new token -fxt-primary-text #1068c4 (4.1–4.4:1 → 4.9–5.5:1); the brand colour #1373d9 stays for fills unchanged #4c9bf5 (6.0:1) Text on primary buttons unchanged (4.7:1) new fill -fxt-primary-fill #1f6fd1 behind white text (2.9:1 → 4.9:1) Warning as text new token -fxt-warning-text #a65500 (2.5:1 → 5.0:1); the icon colour #f08c00 stays unchanged #fab005 (9.3:1)

docs.title: Keyboard
docs.text: • The theme switch (Light / Dark) on the Settings page and the FAVORITES / RECENT tabs of the Explorer are now in the tab order.

docs.title: Keyboard access
docs.text:
All commands are in the menu bar, which opens with F10 or Alt (menu titles have access keys: Alt+F File, Alt+E Edit, Alt+V View, Alt+T Tools, Alt+H Help; in German Alt+D Datei, Alt+B Bearbeiten, Alt+A Ansicht, Alt+W Werkzeuge, Alt+H Hilfe) and is navigated with the arrow keys. Frequent commands have shortcuts — see Keyboard Shortcuts. Focused controls show the focus ring of the theme.

Some controls of the window frame are deliberately left out of the tab order, so that a mouse click on them does not take the focus away from the document. Each one has a keyboard alternative:

Control Keyboard alternative Activity Bar buttons (Explorer, Search, …) View → Activities, Ctrl+Shift+D (Favorites) Menu bar titles F10 / Alt Help button (?) F1 Theme button in the header View → Theme, Settings → Appearance Favourites stars (header, Explorer) File → Open Favorite Side panel and Properties toggles Ctrl+L, Ctrl+Shift+P (also in the View menu) View switch (Text / Tree / Graphic) View → Text / Tree / Graphic View Grid zoom buttons Ctrl++, Ctrl+−, Ctrl+0

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Canvas views. The Graphic view of XSD schemas (diagram) and the Grid view of XML and JSON documents are drawn on a canvas. A screen reader cannot read their content. The grid view is fully keyboard-operable (shortcuts), and the Text and Tree views show the same document with standard controls.
  • Grid view header options — Optimal widths, Word wrap, Entry helpers and the ⋮ grid settings menu — can only be used with the mouse.
  • Linux. JavaFX provides no screen reader support on Linux.
  • No high-contrast theme. The application has a light and a dark theme; it does not follow the high-contrast mode of Windows. Text in editors can be enlarged with Ctrl++; the size of the rest of the interface follows the system's display scaling.
  • Interface texts. Most texts are translated into German; some messages built in code are still English (see Settings → Language).

docs.title: Open points
docs.text:
1. Test with screen readers (NVDA and Narrator on Windows, VoiceOver on macOS), ideally with users who rely on them, and fix what the automated checks cannot find (reading order, announcements of status changes such as validation results).
  2. Keyboard access to the grid view header options.
  3. A high-contrast theme, or following the system's high-contrast setting.
  4. An accessible alternative description for the XSD diagram (for example the structure as a navigable tree next to it).

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• AccessibilityAuditTest and ContrastTest (package org.fxt.freexmltoolkit.a11y) fail for regressions; the audit writes its findings to build/a11y-audit.md.
  • Give every icon-only button a tooltip (it becomes its name) or accessibleText; put a Label right before each input field, or set accessibleText / labelFor.
  • Use -fxt-primary-text for text in the primary colour, -fxt-primary-fill for fills behind -fxt-on-primary text, and -fxt-warning-text for warning text.
  • A control that should stay out of the tab order needs a keyboard alternative listed in AccessibilityAuditTest.KEYBOARD_ALTERNATIVES and on this page.

docs.title: Administration and Policies
docs.text:
This page is for administrators who install FreeXmlToolkit on many computers. Two optional files in one folder set the application up for every user on a computer:

File Effect policy.properties Locked settings. Each line overrides the user's own setting. Users cannot change it: the control is greyed out in Settings, and a notice at the top of the Settings page says that the administrator manages it. defaults.properties Defaults. Each line applies until the user changes the setting.

The command line (fxt-cli) reads the same files.

docs.title: Where the files go
docs.text:
System Folder Windows %ProgramData%\FreeXmlToolkit\ (usually C:\ProgramData\FreeXmlToolkit\) macOS /Library/Application Support/FreeXmlToolkit/ Linux /etc/freexmltoolkit/

To keep the files somewhere else, for example on a network share, set the environment variable FXT_POLICY_FILE machine-wide to the full path of the policy file. The Java option -Dfxt.policy.file=<path> does the same. defaults.properties is then read from the same folder.

Users only need read access; only administrators should be able to write. The application reads the files at start, so users have to restart it after a change.

docs.title: File format
docs.text: The files use the format of ~/.freeXmlToolkit/FreeXmlToolkit.properties: one key=value per line, and # starts a comment. Write backslashes in Windows paths twice (C:\\Schemas) or use forward slashes (C:/Schemas). Characters outside Latin-1 have to be written as \uXXXX.

docs.title: Settings you can set
docs.text:
Any key of the user's settings file works. These are the ones most often managed:

Key Values Setting update.allowed false Policy only. No update check, no Check for Updates in the Help menu or the About dialog, no update installs. Use it when software distribution delivers new versions. update.check.enabled true / false Automatic update check at start (Settings → Updates) telemetry.usage.enabled, telemetry.errors.enabled true / false Anonymous usage statistics and error reports (Settings → Privacy) fxt.telemetry.disabled true Telemetry fully off, without the first-start notice (see Privacy & Telemetry) useSystemProxy, manualProxy true / false Proxy mode: system (useSystemProxy=true), manual (manualProxy=true), or none (both false) http.proxy.host, http.proxy.port host, port Manual proxy http.proxy.nonProxyHosts localhost, 127.*, *.corp Addresses reached without the proxy http.proxy.domain, http.proxy.windowsSignOn domain, true / false NTLM proxy: domain; sign on with the Windows account http.connectTimeoutSeconds, http.readTimeoutSeconds seconds Network timeouts ssl.trustAllCerts false Lock "Trust all certificates" off security.xslt.allow.extensions false Lock Java extension calls in stylesheets off security.xproc.unrestricted false Lock the XProc restrictions on: no p:os-exec, p:run, p:http-request, no network (see Threat Model) security.htmlPreview.allowActiveContent false Lock JavaScript and remote content in HTML previews off security.dtd.allowed false No DTD validation and no DTD loading; DOCTYPEs are only checked for well-formedness fundsxml.enabled true / false FundsXML extension ui.language system / en / de Language of the interface (Settings → Appearance → Language) ui.theme light / dark / system Theme (Settings → Appearance → Theme) ui.accent blue / indigo / violet / green / teal / orange / red / graphite or #rrggbb Accent colour (Settings → Appearance → Accent colour), e.g. the company colour plugins.external.allowed false Policy only. Load no plugins from the plugins folder (built-in ones still load) fop.external.allowed false Policy only. Only the bundled Apache FOP renders PDFs; external XSL-FO processors are hidden and refused (panel, scenarios, fxt-cli fop) fop.processors JSON list The external XSL-FO processors (as written by Settings → XSL-FO Processors); in defaults.properties a starting list, in policy.properties a fixed one fop.processor.default builtin or an id The default XSL-FO processor xmlenc.allowed false Policy only. No XML encryption or decryption (page, editor menu and fxt-cli) xmlenc.legacyAlgorithms.allowed false Policy only. Block the legacy XML encryption algorithms (RSA-1_5, TripleDES, CBC modes, finite-field DH) for encryption and decryption plugin.<id>.enabled true / false A plugin on or off (Settings → Plugins), e.g. plugin.fundsxml.enabled schemaLibrary.autoBind.enabled true / false Bind schemas from the Schema Library automatically xml.parser.type XERCES / SAXON XSD validator (XSD 1.1 schemas always use Xerces) memory.max.mb megabytes, 0 = automatic Maximum memory (Settings → Memory) templates.directory folder Shared template folder useSystemTempFolder, customTempFolder true / false, folder Folder for temporary files log.cleanup.enabled, log.cleanup.maxAgeDays, log.cleanup.maxSizeMb Log file cleanup xml.indent.spaces, json.indent.spaces number Indentation when formatting

Keys that start with fxt. are Java options rather than settings: they replace the -D… options from Operation without Internet and are the only way to set them on macOS, where the launcher configuration cannot be changed. Those in policy.properties always apply. Those in defaults.properties apply unless the option is given on the command line.

Key Effect fxt.telemetry.disabled=true No telemetry at all fxt.schema.namespaceFallback=false Never download a schema by its namespace URL; bundled Schema Library entries only from the cache fxt.schema.localCopies=false Never write downloaded schemas next to the schema that imports them fxt.locale=de Language of the interface, whatever the setting says (en, de) fxt.plugins.dir=<folder> Load plugins from this folder instead of ~/.freeXmlToolkit/plugins

No passwords in these files

Every user can read the files. Do not put a proxy password into them. Use the system proxy or the Windows sign-on (http.proxy.windowsSignOn=true) instead.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
A computer without internet access, on which users cannot switch anything back on:

# C:\ProgramData\FreeXmlToolkit\policy.properties
update.allowed=false
fxt.telemetry.disabled=true
telemetry.usage.enabled=false
telemetry.errors.enabled=false
fundsxml.enabled=false
fxt.schema.namespaceFallback=false
ssl.trustAllCerts=false
security.xslt.allow.extensions=false
security.xproc.unrestricted=false
security.htmlPreview.allowActiveContent=false

A company proxy that users can still change, with a shared template folder:

# /etc/freexmltoolkit/defaults.properties
useSystemProxy=false
manualProxy=true
http.proxy.host=proxy.example.com
http.proxy.port=8080
http.proxy.nonProxyHosts=localhost, 127.*, *.example.com
templates.directory=/srv/shared/fxt-templates

docs.title: Silent installation
docs.text:
System Command Windows (MSI) msiexec /i FreeXmlToolkit-x64-<version>.msi /qn /l*v fxt-install.log (optionally INSTALLDIR="D:\Apps\FreeXmlToolkit") macOS (PKG) sudo installer -pkg FreeXmlToolkit-arm64-<version>.pkg -target / (Intel: FreeXmlToolkit-x64-…) Debian / Ubuntu sudo apt-get install -y ./freexmltoolkit-x64_<version>_amd64.deb Fedora / RHEL / openSUSE sudo rpm -i freexmltoolkit-x64-<version>-1.x86_64.rpm

Distribute policy.properties (and defaults.properties) with the same tool, for example with group policy preferences (Computer Configuration → Preferences → Windows Settings → Files), Intune, Jamf or a configuration-management system. An update of the application does not touch these files.

With update.allowed=false, new versions only arrive through your distribution. Each release publishes SHA-256 checksums and an SBOM (see Licenses).

docs.title: Checking what applies
docs.text:
• The Settings page shows the notice, with the path of the policy file, when anything is locked. Locked controls are greyed out.
  • At start, the log names the folder and the number of locked settings and defaults.
  • The user's own file (~/.freeXmlToolkit/FreeXmlToolkit.properties) keeps only the user's own values. Removing a key from the policy brings the user's previous value back.

See also the Threat Model and Operation without Internet.

docs.title: Our Pledge
docs.text:
We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

docs.title: Our Standards
docs.text:
Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our community include:

  • Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
  • Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
  • Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
  • Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience
  • Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

  • The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
  • Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
  • Public or private harassment
  • Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission
  • Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

docs.title: Enforcement Responsibilities
docs.text:
Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces. Examples of representing our community include using an official e-mail address, posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the community leaders responsible for enforcement at karl.kauc@gmail.com. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.

All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

docs.title: Enforcement Guidelines
docs.text: Community leaders will follow these Community Impact Guidelines in determining the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of Conduct:

docs.title: 1. Correction
docs.text:
Community Impact: Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.

Consequence: A private, written warning from community leaders, providing clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.

docs.title: 2. Warning
docs.text:
Community Impact: A violation through a single incident or series of actions.

Consequence: A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This includes avoiding interactions in community spaces as well as external channels like social media. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.

docs.title: 3. Temporary Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: A serious violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior.

Consequence: A temporary ban from any sort of interaction or public communication with the community for a specified period of time. No public or private interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, is allowed during this period. Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban.

docs.title: 4. Permanent Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: Demonstrating a pattern of violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior, harassment of an individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of classes of individuals.

Consequence: A permanent ban from any sort of public interaction within the community.

docs.title: Attribution
docs.text:
This Code of Conduct is adapted from the Contributor Covenant, version 2.1, available at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html.

Community Impact Guidelines were inspired by Mozilla's code of conduct enforcement ladder.

For answers to common questions about this code of conduct, see the FAQ at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/faq. Translations are available at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/translations.

docs.title: Code signing policy
docs.text: Free code signing for Windows is provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation.

docs.title: What is signed
docs.text:
Only release artifacts that are built by the project's public GitHub Actions workflow (build-packages-on-new-release.yml) from the tagged source code of this repository are signed:

  • the Windows installers FreeXmlToolkit-x64-<version>.msi and FreeXmlToolkit-x64-<version>.exe
  • the portable Windows package FreeXmlToolkit-windows-x64-app-image-<version>.zip
  • inside these packages: the application launcher FreeXmlToolkit.exe, the update helper fxt-update-helper.exe and the executables and libraries of the bundled Java runtime

Nothing is signed from a developer's machine. Builds from forks, pull requests or manual workflow runs are not signed.

Third-party components bundled in the packages (the Java runtime, JavaFX and the Java libraries listed in build.gradle.kts) are open source and are signed as part of the FreeXmlToolkit distribution only.

docs.title: Team roles
docs.text:
Role Members Committers and reviewers Karl Kauc Approvers Karl Kauc

Every signing request is approved manually by an approver. All team members use multi-factor authentication for GitHub and SignPath.

docs.title: Privacy policy
docs.text:
FreeXmlToolkit connects to other systems only for the following purposes:

  • Anonymous usage statistics and error reports — on by default and can be switched off in Settings → Privacy → USAGE STATISTICS. Nothing is sent before the one-time notice was shown after the first start. No file contents, file names, paths or personal data are transmitted. Details: Privacy & Anonymous Telemetry.
  • Update check — asks the GitHub Releases API for the latest version at startup (switch off with Check for updates on startup in the settings). Updates are only downloaded and installed when the user confirms them.
  • FundsXML extension — off by default; when enabled, downloads and updates the FundsXML schemas, samples and rules from GitHub.
  • Schemas and stylesheets referenced by documents the user opens (e.g. xs:import, schemaLocation, catalogs) are downloaded from the locations given in those documents.

Apart from these, the program does not transfer any information to other networked systems unless specifically requested by the user.

docs.title: Reporting problems
docs.text: If you notice a signed file that was not produced by this project, or a signature you do not trust, please open an issue at https://github.com/karlkauc/FreeXmlToolkit/issues or contact the maintainer via the e-mail address on the GitHub profile.

docs.title: Command Line (fxt-cli)
docs.text:
fxt-cli runs FreeXmlToolkit's validators, transformation engines, XPath/XQuery/JSONPath queries, XML comparison and merge, schema documentation, XML/JSON/YAML conversion, PDF output, XML signatures and XML encryption without the user interface: in build pipelines, scripts and scheduled jobs. It uses the same engines and the same security defaults as the application, and it is installed with it.

fxt-cli validate --xsd schema/order.xsd data/
fxt-cli transform -s report.xsl -p year=2026 data/order.xml -o report.html
fxt-cli query -e 'count(//item)' data/order.xml
fxt-cli xsd-doc schema/order.xsd -o site/
fxt-cli fop -i data/order.xml -s order2fo.xsl -o order.pdf
fxt-cli compare old/order.xml new/order.xml
fxt-cli xspec tests/price.xspec -r junit.xml
fxt-cli merge base.xml mine.xml theirs.xml -o merged.xml
fxt-cli convert data/order.xml -o order.json
fxt-cli convert -t yaml data/config.json
fxt-cli sign order.xml --keystore me.p12 --storepass-env KS_PW
fxt-cli encrypt order.xml -x //payment --cert partner.pem

docs.title: Where it is
docs.text:
Installation Program Windows (installer or ZIP) fxt-cli.exe next to FreeXmlToolkit.exe in the installation folder macOS FreeXmlToolkit.app/Contents/MacOS/fxt-cli Linux .deb / .rpm /opt/freexmltoolkit/bin/fxt-cli Linux ZIP bin/fxt-cli in the extracted folder

The installers do not add it to the PATH. Add the folder, or link the program, for example sudo ln -s /opt/freexmltoolkit/bin/fxt-cli /usr/local/bin/fxt-cli on Linux. It brings its own Java runtime; nothing else needs to be installed.

From a source checkout: ./gradlew runCli --args="validate src/test/resources".

fxt-cli --help lists the commands with a one-line summary each, and fxt-cli --version prints the version. fxt-cli <command> --help (or -h, or fxt-cli help <command>) shows one command: what it does, its parameters, its options grouped by topic with their allowed values and defaults, and a few examples to copy. -q / --quiet and --verbose work with every command.

docs.title: validate
docs.text:
Checks XML files against an XML Schema (1.0 or 1.1) and/or a Schematron, and JSON files against a JSON Schema, with the validators of the Validation Panel.

fxt-cli validate [options] FILE|FOLDER...
Option Meaning -x, --xsd, --schema SCHEMA Schema for all XML files: XML Schema (.xsd), DTD (.dtd) or RELAX NG (.rng, .rnc) -s, --schematron SCH Schematron, checked in addition to the schema -j, --json-schema SCHEMA JSON Schema for all JSON files (.json, .json5) --no-schema-lookup Do not use the schema a file declares (see below) --include GLOB,... File names to validate inside folders; default *.xml,*.json -f, --report-format FORMAT text (default), json, junit, sarif -r, --report FILE Write the report to a file; the text summary still goes to standard output -p, --project FXTPROJ Use a project's bindings (schema, Schematron, JSON Schema) and catalogs --fail-on-warning Warnings make a file invalid too

Which schema is used. With --xsd / --schema, that schema (or DTD, or RELAX NG schema) for every XML file. With --project, the schema the project binds to the file (first matching pattern), and the Schematron it binds (unless --schematron is given); JSON files get the JSON Schema the project binds to them (unless --json-schema is given). Otherwise each file is checked against the schema it declares itself, found the same way as when the file is opened in the editor: xsi:schemaLocation / xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation (relative to the file, remote schemas downloaded and cached), redirected by the Schema Library and XML catalogs, else the Schema Library entry for the root namespace or element. A file with a <!DOCTYPE> or a RELAX NG <?xml-model?> is validated against that DTD or RELAX NG schema. A file that names no schema is checked for well-formedness. --no-schema-lookup skips the lookup.

Large files. XML files of 64 MB or more are validated while they are read, as a stream: memory stays flat whatever the size (a 1 GB file needs less than 20 MB). This applies to XML Schema and well-formedness checks; with --schematron the file is read into memory as usual. After 10,000 problems the file's report stops.

Folders are searched recursively for the --include patterns; hidden folders (such as .git) are skipped. Files named directly are always validated; .json and .json5 files are treated as JSON, everything else as XML.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
The text format prints one line per problem, in the form compilers use, and a summary:

data/bad.xml:2:11: error: [XSD] cvc-datatype-valid.1.2.1: 'x' is not a valid value for 'integer'.
data/broken.xml:2:1: error: [Well-formed] XML document structures must start and end within the same entity.
data/order.xml:14: warning: [Schematron] Delivery date lies in the past (at /order/delivery)
4 files, 2 invalid, 2 error(s), 1 warning(s) (485 ms)
Format For json Scripts: summary plus every file with its findings (severity, source, line, column, message, rule, context) junit Test reports of CI servers (Jenkins, GitLab, Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions reporters): one test case per file, a failure per invalid file sarif SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning (GitHub, Azure DevOps, GitLab): one result per problem with rule (xsd, well-formed, schematron, json, json-schema, not-run), level and position

Paths in reports are relative to the working directory when the files lie below it.

docs.title: transform
docs.text:
Runs an XSLT 3.0 stylesheet, an XQuery 3.1 or an XProc 3.0 pipeline.

fxt-cli transform -s STYLESHEET [options] [INPUT...]
Option Meaning -s, --stylesheet FILE .xsl/.xslt (XSLT), .xq/.xquery/.xqy/.xql/.xqm (XQuery), .xpl (XProc) -l, --language LANG xslt, xquery, xproc, for other file extensions -p, --param NAME=VALUE Stylesheet parameter or external XQuery variable (string); repeatable -m, --method METHOD Output method xml, html, xhtml, text, json; default: the stylesheet's xsl:output, else xml -o, --output FILE Output file (one input) -d, --output-dir DIR Output folder for several inputs; each result is named after its input with the extension of the output method --profile REPORT XSLT with one input, or XQuery with at most one: profile the run and write the report, as JSON when REPORT ends in .json, else as text (- for standard error) --warmup N With --profile: runs before the measured one (default 1), so Java's JIT compiler has warmed up

Without -o and -d the result goes to standard output. xsl:message output goes to standard error. XSLT needs an input document; XQuery and XProc can run without one. Relative xsl:import, xsl:include and doc() references resolve against the stylesheet's and the input's folder. As in the application, stylesheets cannot call Java, and doc(), document() and unparsed-text() refuse remote URLs (see Threat Model); XProc pipelines may not run programs (p:os-exec), run computed pipelines (p:run), send HTTP requests or load documents from the network, unless security.xproc.unrestricted=true is set in the settings (see Threat Model).

docs.title: query
docs.text:
Evaluates an XPath 3.1, XQuery 3.1 or JSONPath expression against files, like the Query Console of the application. Made for scripts: one result per input, and an exit code like grep.

fxt-cli query -e EXPR [options] [FILE|FOLDER|-]...
fxt-cli query --query-file QUERY.xq [options] [FILE|FOLDER|-]...
Option Meaning -e, --expression EXPR The expression --query-file FILE Read the expression from a file instead (.xq, .xquery, .xqy, .xql, .xqm: XQuery) -l, --language LANG xpath, xquery or jsonpath. Default: from --query-file's extension, jsonpath when all inputs are .json, else xpath --var NAME=VALUE An external XQuery variable (string value); repeatable --include GLOB,... File names to query inside folders; default *.xml,*.json --[no-]with-filename Prefix each result line with its file; default: when there is more than one input -f, --format FORMAT text (default) or json: one object per input with file, result, error -o, --output FILE Write the results to FILE

- as input reads standard input. An XQuery may run without input. XPath and XQuery run with Saxon (the map:, array: and math: prefixes are declared) under the application's security defaults: no Java calls, no remote doc().

The exit code is 0 when at least one result is not empty, 1 when all results are empty, 3 when the expression fails or an input cannot be read or is not well-formed (the other inputs still run, the errors go to standard error).

fxt-cli query -e 'count(//Position)' fund.xml                                   # 27
fxt-cli query -e '//Position[xs:decimal(TotalPercentage) gt 10]/Identifiers/ISIN/string()' data/
fxt-cli query --query-file report.xq --var year=2026 orders.xml
fxt-cli query -l xquery -e 'current-date()'
fxt-cli query -e '$.items[*].name' data.json
curl -s https://example.org/feed.xml | fxt-cli query -e '//title/string()' -
if fxt-cli query -e '//error' log.xml > /dev/null; then echo "errors found"; fi

docs.title: xsd-doc
docs.text:
Generates the documentation of an XML Schema, like Generate Documentation in the application, with the same options (and a few more for PDF).

fxt-cli xsd-doc SCHEMA -o OUTPUT [options]
fxt-cli xsd-doc SCHEMA --list-languages

-o is a folder for the HTML site and a file for PDF and Word. Without -f the format follows the extension of -o (.pdf, .docx, otherwise HTML). Options that are on by default are switched off with their --no- form (--no-toc). An option of another format than the chosen one (--watermark for an HTML site) is ignored with a warning, so one script can share its options between formats. --verbose prints the generation steps.

Option Meaning Default -o, --output PATH Output folder (HTML) or file (PDF, Word) — -f, --format FORMAT html, pdf or docx from the extension --list-languages Print the documentation languages (xml:lang) of the schema and exit; default stands for documentation without a language

Content

Option Meaning Default --language LANG,… Only documentation in these languages; documentation without a language is always kept all --fallback-language LANG Language the HTML site shows when the reader's language is missing --markdown MODE Render documentation as Markdown: all, marked (only where xs:appinfo sets markdown="true") or off all --[no-]type-definitions Type definitions in the source-code views on --dedupe-data-dictionary One data-dictionary row per type instead of per usage off --[no-]parallel Process the schema on several threads on

Diagrams

Option Meaning Default --image-format FORMAT svg, png or jpg; in a PDF, svg keeps vector diagrams svg --diagram-docs Documentation texts inside the diagrams off --[no-]diagram-constraints Identity constraints and assertions on diagram cards on --root-constraints Also the constraints of the root card off --constraint-targets Mark the fields identity constraints point at off

HTML site

Option Meaning Default --[no-]svg-overview Page with the diagram of the whole schema on --[no-]metadata Generator, date and schema metadata on --favicon FILE Favicon of the site (.ico, .png, .svg)

PDF and Word

Option Meaning Default --page-size SIZE a4, letter, legal, a3 (A3: PDF only, Word uses A4) a4 --landscape Landscape pages portrait --cover-page Cover page off --[no-]toc Table of contents on --[no-]data-dictionary Data dictionary of all elements and attributes on --[no-]schema-diagram Diagram of the whole schema on --[no-]element-diagrams A diagram per element on --element-reference SCOPE Element sections: declarations, all (every occurrence) or off declarations --source-code XSD source of each component off

PDF only

Option Values Default --color-scheme blue, green, purple, grayscale, professional blue --watermark none, draft, confidential, internal none --[no-]page-numbers, --page-number-position left, center, right on, center --[no-]bookmarks PDF outline on --margins narrow (15 mm), normal (20 mm), wide (30 mm) normal --font, --font-size helvetica, times, courier; 9 to 12 points helvetica, 11 --heading-style blue, black, underlined blue --line-spacing compact, normal, relaxed normal --header-style, --footer-style standard, minimal, none standard --table-style bordered, zebra, minimal, grid bordered --[no-]schema-overview, --[no-]complex-types, --[no-]simple-types Chapters on --raster-scale Scale of png/jpg diagrams, 0.5 to 4 1 --title, --author, --subject, --keywords Document properties schema name, user name

Word only

Option Values Default --word-header-style professional, minimal, colorful professional

Examples:

# HTML site with the German and English documentation, German as fallback
fxt-cli xsd-doc order.xsd -o site --language de,en --fallback-language de

# PDF in landscape with a draft watermark and the green colour scheme
fxt-cli xsd-doc order.xsd -o order.pdf --landscape --watermark draft --color-scheme green

# Word document without diagrams, with a cover page
fxt-cli xsd-doc order.xsd -o order.docx --cover-page --no-schema-diagram --no-element-diagrams

docs.title: xspec
docs.text:
Runs XSpec tests for XSLT, XQuery and Schematron.

fxt-cli xspec [options] XSPEC...
Option Meaning -r, --report FILE Write a report for the (single) XSpec file -f, --report-format FORMAT junit (default, for CI servers), html (XSpec's report) or xml (XSpec's XML report)

Every failed test is printed with its scenario, the expected and the actual result; -q leaves out the passed and pending ones. The exit code is 0 when all tests pass, 1 when a test fails and 3 when the tests cannot run (the XSpec file or the code it tests does not compile).

docs.title: scenario
docs.text:
Runs the transformation scenarios of a project file — the ones saved from the Transform panel.

fxt-cli scenario [options] PROJECT [NAME...]
Option Meaning -l, --list List the scenarios (name, stylesheet, input, output) instead of running them -i, --input FILE... Run for these files or folders: the scenario runs once per file --include GLOB,... File names to use inside --input folders; default *.xml --check Compare each result with the scenario's expected result instead of only running it --accept Like --check, then write each differing or missing expected file from the result (placeholders of the old file are kept) -f, --report-format FORMAT Check report: text (default), junit (JUnit XML) or json -r, --report FILE Write the check report to FILE; the summary still goes to standard output

Without names, all scenarios run in the order of the project file. A scenario with an output file writes its result there; the others print it to standard output. The exit code is 1 when a scenario fails (the others still run) and 2 for an unknown scenario name.

With --input, each file fills the scenario's ${file} (and an empty input); ${name} and ${dir} in the output name the result after it. Without scenario names, each file runs the scenario the project binds to it:

fxt-cli scenario orders.fxtproj Report --input data/      # Report for every XML file in data/
fxt-cli scenario orders.fxtproj -i data/a.xml data/b.xml  # each file's bound scenario

A file without a bound scenario, or one whose output an earlier file already wrote (no ${name} in the output), counts as failed.

Regression checks. --check runs the scenarios that name an expected result (or the named ones) and compares each result with it: XML by structure with the scenario's compare settings (ignore XPaths, placeholders, tolerance), text line by line. A ${file} scenario without --input is checked for each file the project binds to it. One line per check (passed, FAILED with the differences, MISSING when the expected file does not exist yet, ERROR), then a summary. Exit code 0 when all match, 1 when one differs or fails, 3 when an expected file is missing.

fxt-cli scenario orders.fxtproj --check -f junit -r build/scenarios.xml   # for CI
fxt-cli scenario orders.fxtproj Report --accept                            # new results are right

docs.title: compare
docs.text:
Compares two XML files by structure, or two folders file by file, like Compare with File… in XML mode and Compare Folders… in the application (see Compare & Merge). Formatting, attribute order and namespace prefixes do not count.

fxt-cli compare [options] LEFT RIGHT
Option Meaning --exact-whitespace Whitespace in text counts (default: trimmed, runs collapsed, whitespace between elements ignored) --ignore-comments Do not compare comments --ignore-order Pair elements regardless of their position --prefixes Also report changed namespace prefixes -k, --key ATTR,... Attributes that identify an element among same-named siblings, e.g. -k id --ignore XPATH Leave out the nodes or attributes this XPath 1.0 selects, on both sides, e.g. --ignore '//@created'; repeatable --tolerance N Numbers in text or attribute values that differ by at most N are equal (default: exact) --[no-]placeholders Evaluate XMLUnit placeholders in LEFT: ${xmlunit.ignore}, ${xmlunit.isNumber}, ${xmlunit.isDateTime}, ${xmlunit.matchesRegex(REGEX)} (default: on) --bytes Folders: compare XML files by their bytes only -f, --format FORMAT text (default) or json

LEFT is the expected document. With placeholders it can describe a result whose values change from run to run (an ID, a date): see Comparing as XML.

For two files, the text report has one line per difference in the form left.xml:LINE: Attribute 'qty' changed: "1" → "2" (/order[1]/item[1]/@qty) and a summary; differences XMLUnit rates similar (a moved element, CDATA instead of text) are marked [similar] (JSON: "similar": true) and still count. For two folders it lists every file that differs or exists on one side only, then the counts. The exit code is 0 when the files are equivalent or the folders match, 1 when they differ, 3 when a file is not well-formed XML.

docs.title: merge
docs.text:
Three-way merge of a base and two changed versions, like Tools → Merge Files… (see Merging three files). Conflicts are written with Git's markers.

fxt-cli merge [options] BASE LEFT RIGHT
Option Meaning -o, --output FILE Result file (may be LEFT); without it the result goes to standard output -L, --label NAME Names in the conflict markers, up to three in the order LEFT, BASE, RIGHT --no-base Leave the base part (|||||||) out of conflict blocks --exact-whitespace For XML: changes that differ only in whitespace are a conflict too

The exit code is 0 without conflicts and 1 with conflicts (the result then contains the markers). A merge without conflicts whose XML is not well-formed gives a warning on standard error.

As a Git merge driver for XML files, in .git/config or ~/.gitconfig:

[merge "fxt"]
    name = FreeXmlToolkit XML merge
    driver = fxt-cli merge -q -L ours -L base -L theirs %O %A %B -o %A

and in .gitattributes: *.xml merge=fxt.

docs.title: convert
docs.text:
Converts between XML, JSON and YAML, like Tools → Convert to JSON… / XML… / YAML… in the application. The mappings are described in the JSON Editor chapter.

fxt-cli convert [options] INPUT...
Option Meaning -t, --to FORMAT json, xml or yaml; default: json for XML input, xml for JSON and YAML input --from FORMAT xml, json, yaml; default: by extension (.json/.jsonc/.json5, .yaml/.yml, everything else XML) -m, --mapping MAPPING structured (default) or w3c (XPath 3.1 fn:json-to-xml vocabulary, lossless) --typed XML to JSON or YAML: numbers and true/false become numbers and booleans --root NAME JSON to XML: root element when the JSON does not name one; default json --indent N Spaces per indentation level, 0 for compact output; default 2 -o, --output FILE Output file (one input) -d, --output-dir DIR Output folder for several inputs; each result is named after its input with the new extension

Without -o and -d the result goes to standard output. A file that cannot be converted (not well-formed, not valid JSON or YAML, not in the W3C vocabulary with -m w3c) is reported on standard error and gives exit code 1; the other files are still converted.

docs.title: fop
docs.text:
Renders a PDF with Apache FOP or an external XSL-FO processor, like the PDF Generator.

fxt-cli fop -i XML -s XSL -o OUT.pdf [options]
fxt-cli fop --fo DOCUMENT.fo -o OUT.pdf [options]
fxt-cli fop --list-processors
Option Meaning -i, --input XML / -s, --stylesheet XSL XML and the stylesheet that turns it into XSL-FO --fo FO A finished XSL-FO document instead -o, --output PDF The PDF to write --title, --author, --subject PDF metadata --pdfa Produce PDF/A-1b --page-size, --orientation Passed to the stylesheet as the parameters page-size and page-orientation -p, --processor NAME builtin (the bundled Apache FOP) or the name or id of an external processor from Settings → XSL-FO Processors. Default: the default processor of the settings --list-processors Lists the processors (* marks the default) and exits

The external processor's warnings and errors are printed to standard error; a failed run gives exit code 1.

docs.title: sign
docs.text:
Signs an XML document (XML digital signature), like Sign & Encrypt → Sign.

fxt-cli sign INPUT --keystore FILE [--alias ALIAS] (--storepass[=PW] | --storepass-env VAR) [options]
Option Meaning --keystore FILE JKS or PKCS#12 keystore with the signing key --alias ALIAS The key's alias (default: the keystore's only key) --storepass, --storepass-env VAR The keystore password: prompted when --storepass has no value, or read from an environment variable (preferred in scripts) --keypass, --keypass-env VAR The key entry's password (default: the keystore password) --type TYPE enveloped (default), enveloping or detached --signature-alg ALG rsa-sha256 (default for RSA keys), rsa-sha384, rsa-sha512, rsa-pss-sha256/384/512, ecdsa-sha256 (default for EC keys), ecdsa-sha384, ecdsa-sha512 --digest-alg ALG sha256 (default), sha384, sha512 --c14n METHOD exclusive (default), exclusive-comments, inclusive, inclusive-comments, inclusive-11 -o FILE Output (default: INPUT.signed.xml, detached: INPUT.sig.xml)

docs.title: verify
docs.text:
Checks XML signatures; with a trust store also the signer's certificate chain (PKIX).

fxt-cli verify INPUT... [--trust-store FILE (--storepass… ) | --trust-cacerts] [--revocation] [-f text|json]

Exit code 0 when every file is valid (and trusted), 1 when one is not, 3 on errors.

docs.title: encrypt
docs.text:
Encrypts XML according to W3C XML Encryption 1.1, like Sign & Encrypt → Encrypt.

fxt-cli encrypt INPUT [-x XPATH]... [--content | --binary] RECIPIENTS... [options]
Option Meaning -x, --xpath XPATH Elements to encrypt (repeatable; default: the document element) --ns PREFIX=URI Namespace prefixes for --xpath (the document element's are known) --content Encrypt only the content of the elements --binary, --mime-type TYPE Encrypt INPUT as binary data (any file) --data-alg ALG Data algorithm (default aes256-gcm) --cert FILE A recipient certificate, PEM or DER (repeatable) --public-key FILE A recipient public key, PEM (repeatable) --keystore FILE --alias ALIAS Recipient certificates from a keystore (--alias repeatable; --storepass…) --key-file FILE, --key-name NAME A shared symmetric key (hex, Base64 or raw) and its KeyName --key-wrap ALG Key wrap for key files, passwords and key agreement; none uses the key file as data key --password, --password-env VAR A password recipient (PBKDF2); --iterations N, --prf sha256|sha384|sha512 --key-transport ALG, --oaep-digest, --mgf RSA: rsa-oaep (default), rsa-oaep-mgf1p, rsa-1_5; OAEP digest and MGF --kdf concatkdf|hkdf, --kdf-digest Key derivation after ECDH-ES / X25519 / X448 --x509 KIND How a certificate is named: issuer-serial (default), certificate, ski, subject, none --recipient-name NAME, --property NAME=VALUE Recipient attribute; EncryptionProperties (repeatable) --keys-outside EncryptedKeys next to the data with a ReferenceList --list-algorithms List all algorithms with their URIs -o FILE Output (default: INPUT.encrypted.xml)

Legacy algorithms (RSA-1_5, TripleDES, CBC modes) work but print a warning.

docs.title: decrypt
docs.text:
Decrypts every EncryptedData the given keys open (also several layers), or describes an encrypted document without a key.

fxt-cli decrypt INPUT (--keystore FILE … | --private-key FILE | --key-file FILE | --password) [--id ID]... [-o FILE]
fxt-cli decrypt --inspect [-f text|json] INPUT
Option Meaning --keystore FILE, --alias, --storepass…, --keypass… Your private key from a keystore --private-key FILE Your private key as PEM (--keypass for an encrypted one; repeatable) --key-file FILE, --key-name NAME A shared symmetric key (repeatable) --password, --password-env VAR The document's password --id ID Only the EncryptedData with this Id (repeatable) --inspect, -f text|json Describe the encryption instead of decrypting -o FILE Output (default: INPUT.decrypted.xml; binary data INPUT.decrypted.bin)

Exit code 0 when everything selected was decrypted, 1 when no key fits or data stays encrypted, 3 on errors.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success; all documents valid 1 Problems found (an invalid document, a difference), or a transformation, conversion, documentation or PDF run failed 2 Invalid command line, or an input file does not exist 3 A validation or comparison could not run: the schema or Schematron does not load, a file is unreadable or not well-formed

docs.title: Output, logging and settings
docs.text:
• Standard output carries only results and reports, so it can be piped or redirected. Messages, progress (Wrote …) and log output go to standard error. -q / --quiet leaves only problems and requested reports; --verbose adds the processing log.
  • Settings are read from the same file as the application (~/.freeXmlToolkit/FreeXmlToolkit.properties, or -Dfxt.properties.file): the proxy, the Schema Library and its catalogs, and the XSD validator (Xerces or Saxon; XSD 1.1 schemas always use Xerces).
  • Network: only what the files ask for (declared schemas, imports); see Operation without Internet. The command line sends no telemetry and does not check for updates.
  • Java options (for example -Xmx8g for very large files) go into the environment variable JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, or into fxt-cli.cfg next to the application's own launcher configuration.

docs.title: In a CI pipeline
docs.text:
GitHub Actions, uploading the SARIF report to code scanning:

- name: Validate XML
  run: /opt/freexmltoolkit/bin/fxt-cli validate --xsd schema/order.xsd -f sarif -r fxt.sarif data/
- uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
  if: always()
  with:
    sarif_file: fxt.sarif

GitLab CI with a JUnit report:

validate:
  script:
    - fxt-cli validate --xsd schema/order.xsd -f junit -r fxt-junit.xml data/
  artifacts:
    when: always
    reports:
      junit: fxt-junit.xml

docs.title: Where the Others Offer More
docs.text:
FreeXmlToolkit focuses on XML, XSD, XSLT and XQuery development. It edits DTD and RELAX NG schemas as text only (with validation and auto-completion for documents that use them), and it does not edit files larger than its memory limit (the Large File Viewer is read-only). The other products cover areas that FreeXmlToolkit does not:

  • Oxygen XML Editor:
    • authoring and publishing for DITA, DocBook and TEI;
    • a visual (CSS-based) author mode with change tracking;
    • connections to XML databases, content management systems and WebDAV;
    • an Eclipse plugin and a web-based editor (separate product);
    • an AI assistant (paid add-on).
  • XMLSpy:
    • database connections;
    • code generation for Java, C# and C++;
    • a WSDL editor and a SOAP client;
    • an XBRL taxonomy editor;
    • Authentic view;
    • charts from XML data;
    • Visual Studio and Eclipse integration;
    • an AI chat (separate subscription).
  • XMLBlueprint:
    • refactoring (rename or split elements, rename namespace prefixes);
    • editing files on FTPS, SFTP and WebDAV servers;
    • CSV and Excel to XML conversion;
    • a user interface in 21 languages.
