Comments, unquoted keys, single quotes and trailing commas are not part of the document model behind the tree and grid views. Editing in the grid (or through the Properties inspector) therefore rewrites the file as standard JSON on the first edit - the grid warns you once when it opens such a file. Edit in the Text view to keep them.

docs.title: JSONC syntax (JSON with Comments)
docs.text:
{
  // This is a single-line comment
  "name": "John",
  /* This is a
     multi-line comment */
  "age": 30
}

docs.title: JSON5 syntax
docs.text:
{
  // Unquoted keys
  name: 'John',
  // Single quotes
  city: 'New York',
  // Trailing commas allowed
  items: [1, 2, 3,],
}

docs.title: Converting between XML, JSON and YAML
docs.text:
The Tools menu converts the active document:

Command From Convert to JSON… XML, YAML Convert to XML… JSON, YAML Convert to YAML… XML, JSON

When XML is involved, a dialog asks for the mapping (below) and remembers your choice; between JSON and YAML there is nothing to choose. The result opens in a new, unsaved tab named after the document (order.xml → order.json). The converter reads the text of the editor, including changes that are not saved yet. The indentation follows Settings (XML for XML output, JSON for JSON and YAML output).

YAML files (.yaml, .yml) open in the editor as text. They are read as YAML 1.2 (core schema: yes and on stay strings); a file with several documents (---) becomes an array. YAML is written in block style. Strings that would otherwise read back as a number, boolean or null are quoted ('007', 'true'), so a conversion to YAML and back returns the same data. XML goes to YAML through its JSON form, with the same mapping. Comments and anchors of a YAML file are not kept.

docs.title: Structured mapping
docs.text:
The default. It works for any XML and gives JSON that reads naturally:

XML JSON <order>…</order> (the root) {"order": …} <name>Ada</name> "name": "Ada" <item sku="A">Apple</item> "item": {"@sku": "A", "#text": "Apple"} two or more <item> siblings "item": [ … ] <empty/> "empty": "" xmlns:p="urn:p" "@xmlns:p": "urn:p" comments, processing instructions dropped

Element text is kept as it is, as a string. With Numbers and true/false as JSON numbers and booleans, text that is a JSON number (42, 1.5, -3e2, but not 007) or true/false becomes a number or boolean.

From JSON to XML the same rules apply in reverse. A top-level object with exactly one property names the root element; anything else (several properties, an array, a single value) is wrapped in the root element set in the dialog (default json). An array repeats its element; an array inside an array becomes <item> elements. null becomes an empty element. A property name that is not an XML name is adapted: invalid characters become _, and a name that starts with a digit gets a leading _ ("first name" → first_name, "1st" → _1st). A prefix like p: stays when the object declares it with "@xmlns:p".

What the structured mapping cannot keep: the order of differently named siblings (<a/><b/><a/> becomes "a": [ … ], "b": …), text between child elements in mixed content (it is joined into one #text), the difference between one element and an array of one, and empty arrays. Characters that XML 1.0 cannot hold (control characters such as \u0001) stop the conversion to XML; the W3C mapping replaces them.

docs.title: W3C mapping (XPath 3.1)
docs.text:
The XML representation of JSON defined for XPath 3.1, as written by fn:json-to-xml and read by fn:xml-to-json (Saxon). It converts any JSON to XML and back without loss:

<map xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-functions">
   <array key="items">
      <number>1</number>
      <string>two</string>
   </array>
   <boolean key="active">true</boolean>
</map>

Use it when the XML is processed further with XSLT or XQuery, or when the JSON must come back unchanged. Converting XML to JSON with this mapping needs a document in that vocabulary; other XML is refused with a message.

On the command line: fxt-cli convert.

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
JSON files use the shell's single-row editor toolbar. Related actions sit in split buttons with a visible ▾ arrow menu; see Unified Shell - Toolbar for the full reference.

With a JSON file active, the relevant actions are:

Button Description New Open the guided New File dialog (includes JSON) Open Open an existing file Save ▾ Save the current document; the arrow menu holds Save As… and Save All Undo / Redo Undo or redo changes (icon buttons) Format ▾ Pretty-print the JSON; the arrow menu holds Minify (compress by removing whitespace) Query Console Toggle the bottom query console - for JSON documents it runs JSONPath queries (icon button, Ctrl+Shift+X) Validate Check the JSON syntax (F8)

Actions that do not apply to JSON (e.g. Run or the XSLT transform) are greyed out. The Tree and Graphic (grid) views are switched with the Text/Tree/Graphic view switch at the right end of the toolbar.

docs.title: Tree View Icons
docs.text: Icon Type { } Object (blue) [ ] Array (green) " " String (gray) # Number (orange) Toggle Boolean (cyan) - Null (gray, italic) // Comment (green, italic)

docs.title: Tips and Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use the Tree View for navigating large JSON documents, and the Grid View to edit arrays of objects like a table
  2. Enable Auto-Format after pasting JSON from external sources
  3. Use JSONPath to quickly extract specific data
  4. Validate against Schema to ensure data quality
  5. Drag and Drop files for quick access

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• XML Editor - Edit XML files with similar features
  • XSLT Developer - Transform JSON to other formats

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text:
All shortcuts of the Unified Shell in one place. The same list is available in the application under Help → Keyboard Shortcuts, and every menu item shows its shortcut next to it.

macOS

On macOS use Cmd instead of Ctrl for the shortcuts below (see Menu Bar → macOS). Because Cmd+H hides the application, Find and Replace is Alt+Cmd+F; full screen is Ctrl+Cmd+F (F11 works too).

docs.title: Files and Tabs
docs.text: Shortcut Action Ctrl+N New file (opens the guided New File dialog) Ctrl+O Open file Ctrl+S Save current tab Ctrl+Shift+S Save As (the Save ▾ menu also offers Save All) Ctrl+W (Windows/Linux also Ctrl+F4) Close the active tab (asks to save unsaved changes) Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab Next / previous tab Ctrl+, Open the Settings page Ctrl+Q Quit FreeXmlToolkit (Cmd+Q on macOS; Alt+F4 on Windows works as usual). With unsaved documents one dialog lists them and offers Save All / Don't Save / Cancel - the same when the window is closed

docs.title: Editing and Search
docs.text:
Shortcut Action Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y (or Ctrl+Shift+Z) Undo / Redo (works from the Text, Tree and Graphic views) Ctrl+F Find (in the active document, in every view mode - see below) Ctrl+H Find and Replace (in the active document); Alt+Cmd+F on macOS Ctrl+Shift+F Find in Files - opens the Search panel, prefilled with the editor selection Ctrl+Shift+H Replace in Files - opens the Search panel with the replace row expanded Shift+Alt+F Format (pretty-print) the active document Ctrl+Space Auto-completion (IntelliSense); also in the Query Console Ctrl+T Insert Template… (needs an open document) Alt+Enter / Ctrl+. Changed shortcut

Ctrl+Shift+F no longer formats the document. Following the VS Code convention, it now opens Search (Find in Files), and Ctrl+Shift+H opens Replace in Files. Format Document moved to Shift+Alt+F - the toolbar's Format button works unchanged. The in-editor find/replace stays on Ctrl+F / Ctrl+H.

docs.title: Search in Every View
docs.text: Pressing Ctrl+F opens an inline search bar with up/down chevron arrows for Find Previous / Find Next (Enter / Shift+Enter work too). The search works in the Text, Tree and Graphic views. In the structured views it searches the nodes themselves — for XSD schemas that is element/attribute/type names, documentation and appinfo, type references, fixed/default values, enumeration and facet values, and comments; for XML instances in the Graphic grid it is element names, attribute names, and values (also inside embedded table cells); for JSON documents (Tree and Graphic) it is keys and values. A match hidden inside a collapsed branch is revealed automatically (ancestors expand), selected, and scrolled into view; matches wrap around when you reach the end. Switching the view mode or tab while the bar is open re-targets the search to the active view. Replace is available in the Text view only — in Tree/Graphic views the replace toggle is disabled. In an HTML document's Preview, Ctrl+F searches the underlying markup text, not the rendered page. See XML Editor Features for details.

docs.title: Large File Viewer
docs.text: The Large File Viewer shows text and XML files of any size, read-only: a 1 GB file opens in a few seconds and needs only a few megabytes of memory. It reads the file from disk as you scroll, instead of loading it into the editor. Use it for files that are too large for the editor, or when you only want to look at, search or copy from a large file.

docs.title: Opening a file in the viewer
docs.text:
• Opening a large file: a file of 50 MB or more asks how to open it: Open in Viewer, Open in Editor or Cancel. A file too large for the editor's memory limit (see Memory and large files) offers only the viewer.
  • File → Open in Large File Viewer… opens any file in the viewer, whatever its size.

The tab is named <file> (viewer). While the file is read for the first time, a progress bar shows how far it is (a 1 GB file takes a few seconds on an SSD); Cancel stops it. The bar above the text shows the size, the number of lines and the encoding.

docs.title: Working in the viewer
docs.text:
Action How Scroll Mouse wheel, scroll bar, Page Up / Page Down, Home / End Go to a line Type the number into Line (or press Ctrl+G) and press Enter Select Click a row; Shift+click or Shift+arrow keys extend the selection Copy Ctrl+C copies the selected rows (up to 100,000) Find Type into Find (or press Ctrl+F) and press Enter; Regex and Match case refine the search Next / previous match F3 / Shift+F3, or click a match in the list below the text

The search runs in the background over the whole file and lists up to 10,000 matches with their line numbers; clicking one shows its line. The status bar shows the line and the byte offset of the selection.

XML is coloured line by line (tags, attributes, values, comments). A line longer than 4 KB, such as a minified document on one line, is shown as several rows; the continuation rows are marked with ↪ instead of a line number. A match that spans two such rows is not found.

docs.title: Structure (XML)
docs.text:
For an XML file, the Structure tab shows the elements without reading the whole file:

  • Tree (left): the root element; expanding an element lists its children, 1,000 at a time. Load more… at the end of a list reads the next 1,000. Each element shows its name, its first attribute and, for an element with only text, the text.
  • Table (right): the children of the selected element as records, one row per child. The columns are the children's attributes (@id, …) and the texts of their simple child elements (elements that contain only text, such as <amount>), so a file of records reads like a spreadsheet. Load More adds the next 1,000 children.

Double-click a row, or choose Show in Text in the context menu, to see the element in the Text tab. Open as New Document opens the element (up to 50 MB) as a new, unsaved document in the editor, where it can be edited, validated or transformed like any other file. Copy XPath copies the element's path, such as /orders[1]/order[42].

The structure is read from the bytes of the file on demand, so the first 1,000 children of the root of a 1 GB file appear in well under a second. Reading assumes a well-formed document; DTD declarations are skipped, entities other than the predefined ones are not expanded.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Validate in the toolbar checks the whole file while reading it as a stream, so memory stays flat whatever its size (a 1 GB file: well-formedness in about 10 seconds, XML Schema validation in about 25 seconds, with less than 20 MB of memory):

Item Checks Against the Declared Schema The schema the document names (xsi:schemaLocation / xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation, resolved as in the editor, also through the Schema Library); the menu shows its file name, or "(none)" Against a Schema… An XML Schema (.xsd, 1.0 or 1.1) you choose Well-Formedness Only That the document is well-formed XML

The Problems tab lists severity, line, column and message; double-click a problem to see its line in the Text tab. The check stops after 1,000 problems, and at the first error that makes the document not well-formed. A progress bar shows how far it is; Cancel stops it. Schematron is not available for large files.

fxt-cli validate validates XML files of 64 MB or more the same way (without Schematron), see Command Line.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• The viewer is read-only. To change a large file, open it in the editor (if it fits the memory limit), or open the element you need as a new document from the Structure tab.
  • UTF-8, ASCII and single-byte encodings such as ISO-8859-1 are supported; UTF-16 and UTF-32 files are not.
  • The file is read where it is: if it changes on disk while it is open, close and reopen the viewer.

docs.title: Third-Party Libraries and Licenses
docs.text: FreeXmlToolkit itself is licensed under the Apache License 2.0. It is built on third-party libraries and ships with its own Java runtime. The tables below list the libraries the project uses directly; the SBOM of each release lists every library in the installation, including the ones these pull in. Two parts need more than a table row: the Xerces build for XSD 1.1 and the bundled Java runtime with JavaFX. This page explains the license situation; it is not legal advice.

docs.title: License Texts in the Installation
docs.text:
Every library jar carries its own license and notice files (META-INF/), in the installation's app folder. The Java runtime keeps its license texts in a legal folder, one subfolder per module:

Installation Java runtime license texts Windows runtime\legal\ in the installation folder macOS FreeXmlToolkit.app/Contents/runtime/Contents/Home/legal/ Linux .deb / .rpm /opt/freexmltoolkit/lib/runtime/legal/ Linux ZIP lib/runtime/legal/ in the extracted folder

docs.title: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
docs.text:
From version 2.11 on, every GitHub release carries a machine-readable SBOM in the CycloneDX 1.6 format: FreeXmlToolkit-<version>-sbom.cdx.json and FreeXmlToolkit-<version>-sbom.cdx.xml. It lists every library the application ships (the runtime classpath, not test or build tools) with its version, license, package URL and hashes, and it is covered by the release's SHA256SUMS.txt. Security and compliance tools such as Dependency-Track, Trivy or Grype read it directly.

To create it from the sources: ./gradlew cyclonedxDirectBom writes build/reports/cyclonedx-direct/bom.json and bom.xml.

docs.title: XML Validation (XSD 1.1 Support)
docs.text:
Library Version License Apache Xerces, XSD 1.1 build (org.exist-db.thirdparty.xerces:xercesImpl, classifier xml-schema-1.1) 2.12.2 Apache License 2.0 Eclipse WST XPath 2.0 Processor "PsychoPath" (org.exist-db.thirdparty.org.eclipse.wst.xml:xpath2) 1.2.0 Eclipse Public License 1.0 Java CUP Runtime (edu.princeton.cup:java-cup) 10k CUP License (permissive, similar to the Standard ML of New Jersey license) Jing (org.relaxng:jing, RELAX NG validation) 20241231 BSD 3-Clause License Trang (org.relaxng:trang, DTD / RELAX NG to XSD for IntelliSense) 20241231 BSD 3-Clause License ISO RELAX (isorelax:isorelax, used by Jing) 20030108 MIT License XML Commons External (xml-apis:xml-apis, xml-apis:xml-apis-ext) 1.4.01, 1.3.04 Apache License 2.0; contains the SAX (public domain) and W3C DOM interfaces (W3C Software License)

Why a Xerces from eXist-db. XSD 1.1 validation (assertions, conditional types, open content) comes from Apache Xerces-J. The Apache project builds Xerces-J 2.12.2 in two variants: the XSD 1.0 build, which is the one on Maven Central as xerces:xercesImpl, and the XSD 1.1 build, which Apache only offers as a download on xerces.apache.org. The eXist-db project publishes the XSD 1.1 build to Maven Central under its own group id org.exist-db.thirdparty.xerces, so that build tools can use it. FreeXmlToolkit uses that artifact:

  • It is Apache code under the Apache License 2.0, not an eXist-db product under eXist-db's license (LGPL). The jar reports itself as Xerces-J 2.12.2-xml-schema-1.1 from the Apache Software Foundation and contains Apache's LICENSE and NOTICE. "Fork" only means a different place of publication.
  • The matching sources are on Maven Central next to the jar (xercesImpl-2.12.2-xml-schema-1.1-sources.jar); the Apache sources are the release tag Xerces-J_2_12_2 in the Apache Xerces repository.
  • For assertions, Xerces needs the XPath 2.0 processor from the Eclipse Web Tools Platform and the CUP parser runtime. eXist-db publishes both in the same way. The XPath 2.0 processor is under the Eclipse Public License 1.0 (a weak copyleft for the library itself, without effect on FreeXmlToolkit's code); it is distributed unchanged, and its sources are on Maven Central (xpath2-1.2.0-sources.jar).
  • Xerces depends on the old XML Commons interface jars (xml-apis), and the Xerces jar contains copies of them. They are inert on Java 25: the classes of the javax.xml, org.w3c.dom and org.xml.sax packages always come from the Java runtime's own java.xml module.
  • The XSD 1.1 build is used for XSD 1.0 schemas as well unless Settings → Schemas & Validation → XML parser is set to Saxon; XSD 1.1 schemas always use it.

docs.title: Bundled Java Runtime and JavaFX
docs.text:
FreeXmlToolkit does not need an installed Java. Each installer and ZIP contains a Java 25 runtime, made with jlink from the BellSoft Liberica Full JDK. "Full" means the JDK includes OpenJFX (JavaFX), the UI toolkit; FreeXmlToolkit does not download or ship JavaFX jars of its own.

  • What is in it. Only the modules the application needs (java.base, java.desktop, java.xml, java.net.http, …, and javafx.base, javafx.controls, javafx.fxml, javafx.graphics, javafx.media, javafx.swing, javafx.web). The modules are not modified; jlink only leaves out the other modules, debug information and the command line tools. The release file in the runtime folder names the exact version.
  • License. OpenJDK and OpenJFX are under the GNU General Public License version 2 with the Classpath Exception. The Classpath Exception allows an application to run on and link with the runtime under its own license; FreeXmlToolkit's code stays under the Apache License 2.0, and the runtime stays under GPLv2+CE. Some native parts carry their own licenses: WebKit in javafx.web (used for the HTML preview and the help pages) and GStreamer/GLib in javafx.media are mostly under the LGPL 2.1, and libraries such as ICU, libxml2, libxslt, FreeType, HarfBuzz, libjpeg and libpng under permissive licenses. Every one of them is listed with its full license text in the module's legal subfolder (see License Texts in the Installation).
  • Sources. The runtime is the unmodified Liberica build. Its sources are published by BellSoft (Liberica source packages, github.com/bell-sw) and by the OpenJDK projects (openjdk/jdk, openjdk/jfx).
  • Updates. The runtime is replaced with every FreeXmlToolkit release, which picks up the latest Liberica 25 update at build time. Java security fixes therefore arrive with FreeXmlToolkit updates, not through a separately installed Java.
  • The TestFX/Monocle jar in the test dependencies below is only used to run the tests headless; it is not part of the installation.

docs.title: Operation without Internet
docs.text: FreeXmlToolkit works without an internet connection. Editing, validation against local schemas, transformations, debugging, documentation generation, PDF output and signatures all run locally. This page lists every feature that can contact the network, so administrators can run the application on air-gapped machines or behind a restrictive firewall, and pre-seed what it would otherwise download.

docs.title: Network connections
docs.text:
All connections use the proxy from Settings → Network & Security → HTTP PROXY (system, manual or none, with authentication). Without a connection, each feature fails quietly or falls back to its cache; the application is never blocked.

only after the first-start notice On FXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1 (machine-wide), Settings → Privacy, see Privacy & Telemetry Queued locally (at most 5000 events / 14 days), retried with growing pauses Error report telemetry.status20.net Only when you click Send – As telemetry Error shown in the dialog FundsXML extension api.github.com, codeload.github.com (repositories fundsxml/schema, fundsxml/examples) 5 s after start when enabled; the status bar shows the schema as unresolved Imported / included schemas (xs:import, xs:include) The schemaLocation URL When a schema is loaded or used for validation On Map the URL to a local file Cached copy, else the import is reported as unresolved Namespace-URL fallback The namespace URI of an import without a usable location When an import cannot be resolved otherwise On -Dfxt.schema.namespaceFallback=false Not resolved Bundled Schema Library entries w3.org, oasis-open.org, xbrl.org, web3d.org, schemas.xmlsoap.org, raw.githubusercontent.com On first use of the schema, then cached On -Dfxt.schema.namespaceFallback=false, or disable single entries in the Schema Library The cached copy is used JSON Schema $schema / $ref The referenced URL When a JSON document is validated or bound On Use local $refs Not resolved XProc p:http-request and remote hrefs The URL in the pipeline When the pipeline runs, only with Run XProc pipelines without restrictions on – Blocked by default Pipeline error HTML preview Remote images, scripts and styles the page refers to When the preview is shown – – Missing resources Open from URL, proxy test The URL you enter On your action – – Error message

Not on this list because they never connect: XSLT, XQuery and XPath (also in the Query Console, grid formulas and filters: doc(), document() and unparsed-text() refuse remote URLs), XSL-FO/PDF output (remote resources are refused), XSD documentation (all assets are bundled), the user interface's icons and fonts.

The command line (fxt-cli) connects only for what the files ask for (the schema rows above); it sends no telemetry, does not check for updates and does not start the FundsXML extension.

docs.title: Schemas without the internet
docs.text:
Give the application a local copy of every schema your documents and schemas refer to:

  1. Schema Library (activity bar → Schema Library): add a namespace → local file mapping, or import an OASIS XML catalog whose system, uri, rewriteSystem or rewriteURI entries point http(s) locations to file: paths. The library is asked before any download, also inside imported schemas. See Schema Library.
  2. Pre-seed the cache: run the application once on a connected machine with the same schemas, then copy ~/.freeXmlToolkit/cache/ and ~/.freeXmlToolkit/schema-library.json to the offline machines.
  3. Downloaded imports are also copied next to the schema that references them (under their original name, never overwriting a file). A folder prepared this way works offline. Start with -Dfxt.schema.localCopies=false to keep downloads in the cache only.

docs.title: Files and folders
docs.text:
Path Content ~/.freeXmlToolkit/FreeXmlToolkit.properties All settings (another file: -Dfxt.properties.file=<path>) ~/.freeXmlToolkit/schema-library.json Schema Library mappings and catalogs ~/.freeXmlToolkit/cache/schemas/ Downloaded schemas (cache-index.json lists them) ~/.freeXmlToolkit/cache/<id>/ Schemas from xsi:schemaLocation and JSON Schemas ~/.freeXmlToolkit/fundsxml/ FundsXML schemas, examples and Schematron ~/.freeXmlToolkit/telemetry-queue.jsonl Telemetry events waiting to be sent

~ is the user's home folder (%USERPROFILE% on Windows).

docs.title: Settings for an offline machine
docs.text:
Put these into FreeXmlToolkit.properties (or a central copy, see below):

update.check.enabled=false
telemetry.usage.enabled=false
telemetry.errors.enabled=false
fundsxml.enabled=false

and set the environment variable FXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 machine-wide (it also suppresses the first-start notice; see Privacy & Telemetry).

For every user of a computer, and without users being able to switch them back, put these lines into the machine-wide policy file instead (with update.allowed=false, fxt.telemetry.disabled=true and the fxt.schema.… options below), see Administration & Policies.

docs.title: Java options for an installed application
docs.text:
Options written as -D… on this page are Java options. In an installed application they go into the launcher configuration in the installation's app folder, FreeXmlToolkit.cfg (on Linux under lib/app/), as lines in the [JavaOptions] section:

[JavaOptions]
java-options=-Dfxt.schema.namespaceFallback=false
java-options=-Dfxt.properties.file=\\server\share\fxt\FreeXmlToolkit.properties

An update replaces this file, so software distribution should write it again after each update. On macOS the file is part of the signed application bundle: changing it breaks the signature, so use the policy file (fxt.… keys) or the environment variables there instead.

See also the Threat Model for the security side of these connections.

docs.title: PDF Generator (FOP)
docs.text: Create professional PDF documents from your XML files using Apache FOP (Formatting Objects Processor).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The PDF Generator combines your XML data with an XSL-FO stylesheet to create formatted PDF documents.

The PDF / FOP panel with the input files, metadata, and options set

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
XML Data + XSL-FO Stylesheet = PDF Document
  1. XML File - Your data (the content you want in the PDF)
  2. XSL-FO Stylesheet - A template defining layout and formatting
  3. PDF Output - The generated document

docs.title: The PDF / FOP Panel
docs.text:
In the Unified Shell, open the PDF / FOP activity from the activity bar. The panel is organized into these sections plus the primary action:

Section Contents TOOLS Debug stylesheet… runs the XSL-FO stylesheet in the XSLT debugger; Render PDF from FO… renders the FO of the latest run (e.g. of a debug run) to a PDF INPUT The XML (follows the active editor; Change fixes it to a file) and the XSL-FO stylesheet. Each slot shows the file name on its own line (full path as tooltip); an empty slot shows a hint such as "No stylesheet — choose or drop a file" and works like Change when clicked METADATA PDF Title, Author (pre-filled from your user name), Subject OPTIONS PDF/A-1b compliant toggle and the Page size dropdown (A4/Letter · Portrait/Landscape) Generate PDF Asks for the output file and renders off the UI thread (XSLT → XSL-FO → PDF) RESULT Preview PDF, Open PDF, Show intermediate FO (the XSL-FO the stylesheet produced, as an editor tab) and Messages & events (n) (the stylesheet's xsl:message output and every event Apache FOP raised, in the OUTPUT panel)

docs.title: Step 1: Select Your Files
docs.text:
1. Open your XML data file in the editor (or pick one via the INPUT section's Change, or drop an .xml file from your file manager onto the XML row)
  2. Click Change on the stylesheet row to select your XSL-FO stylesheet - or drop an .xsl / .xslt file onto the row

You can also drag and drop files directly into the application.

docs.title: Step 2: Set PDF Metadata (Optional)
docs.text:
Add metadata to your PDF document in the METADATA section:

Field Description Title Document title Author Your name or organization (pre-filled from the configured user name) Subject What the document is about

docs.title: Step 3: Options (Optional)
docs.text:
• PDF/A-1b compliant - produces an archival-grade PDF. The stylesheet must use embeddable system fonts (e.g. Liberation Sans); the PDF base-14 fonts (Helvetica, Times, Courier) cannot be embedded and FOP will report exactly that.
  • Page size - a dropdown whose value is passed to the stylesheet as the XSLT parameters page-size (A4/Letter) and page-orientation (Portrait/Landscape). As the hint below the dropdown says, it only applies if the stylesheet uses these parameters - stylesheets that declare them can switch their fo:simple-page-master accordingly; others ignore the setting.
  • Processor - which program renders the XSL-FO: the bundled Apache FOP or an external XSL-FO processor you configured. Manage processors… opens the list. With an external processor, the metadata fields and PDF/A are only available when its arguments pass them on (${title}, ${pdfa} …).

docs.title: Step 4: Generate the PDF
docs.text: Click Generate PDF. You are asked where to save the output file, and the PDF is rendered in the background - the application stays responsive throughout.

docs.title: Step 5: Preview
docs.text:
The generated PDF opens in the built-in PDF preview, a tab next to your documents. You can: - Page through the document with the arrow buttons in its toolbar (Page 1 / 2) - Scroll within a page; it is fitted to the tab's width - Review the layout and formatting without leaving the app

The Preview PDF and Open PDF buttons re-open the last result at any time.

The generated factsheet in the preview tab; the RESULT section lists the follow-up actions

docs.title: Step 6: Understand what FOP did
docs.text:
Every generation keeps the intermediate XSL-FO and the messages of both stages:

  • Show intermediate FO opens the FO document the stylesheet produced as an editor tab - the quickest way to see whether a layout problem comes from the stylesheet (wrong FO) or from FOP (right FO, unexpected rendering).
  • Messages & events (n) shows the stylesheet's xsl:message output and every event FOP raised while rendering - a substituted font, content that overflows its area, an unknown property - in the OUTPUT panel. The status line after a successful run counts the FOP warnings, so a Generated: report.pdf · 2 FOP warnings is worth a look.
  • A failed generation puts the stylesheet error (with its line in the .xsl file) or FOP's reason into OUTPUT as well.

docs.title: Debugging the stylesheet
docs.text: TOOLS → Debug stylesheet… runs the XSL-FO stylesheet in the interactive XSLT debugger: set breakpoints in the stylesheet's gutter, step through templates, watch variables and the context node, read xsl:message output live. The page-size and orientation parameters are passed on. When the debug run finishes, its FO is in the OUTPUT panel and in the panel's result, so Show intermediate FO and Render PDF from FO… work right away - the latter renders exactly the FO you just debugged to a PDF of your choice.

docs.title: Favorites Integration
docs.text:
Save frequently used XML and XSL-FO files for quick access:

  • Both INPUT rows carry a star menu next to their Change link - XML favorites for the input, XSLT favorites for the stylesheet - so you can pick a favorited file in one click.
  • Ctrl+D (or the Favorites panel's Add current) stars the active document.
  • The Favorites activity (star icon in the activity bar) lists all your saved files.

Learn more: Favorites System

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Description Drag & Drop Drop an .xml file onto the XML row or an .xsl / .xslt file onto the stylesheet row; like a favorite pick, the file is also loaded into the editor Built-in Viewer Preview PDFs without leaving the app PDF Metadata Add title, author, and subject PDF/A-1b Optional archival-grade output Background Rendering Generation runs off the UI thread Favorites Quick access to frequently used files

docs.title: XSL-FO Basics
docs.text: XSL-FO (Extensible Stylesheet Language Formatting Objects) defines how your XML content should be formatted in the PDF.

docs.title: Simple Example
docs.text:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="1.0"
    xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform"
    xmlns:fo="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Format">

  <xsl:template match="/">
    <fo:root>
      <fo:layout-master-set>
        <fo:simple-page-master master-name="A4"
            page-height="29.7cm" page-width="21cm"
            margin="2cm">
          <fo:region-body/>
        </fo:simple-page-master>
      </fo:layout-master-set>

      <fo:page-sequence master-reference="A4">
        <fo:flow flow-name="xsl-region-body">
          <fo:block font-size="24pt" font-weight="bold">
            <xsl:value-of select="/document/title"/>
          </fo:block>
          <fo:block font-size="12pt">
            <xsl:value-of select="/document/content"/>
          </fo:block>
        </fo:flow>
      </fo:page-sequence>
    </fo:root>
  </xsl:template>

</xsl:stylesheet>

docs.title: Common FO Elements
docs.text: Element Description fo:block Paragraph or block of text fo:inline Inline text formatting fo:table Tables with rows and cells fo:external-graphic Images fo:page-number Current page number fo:leader Dots, lines, or space (for TOC)

docs.title: External XSL-FO Processors
docs.text:
Instead of the bundled Apache FOP, the PDF can be rendered by any formatter that has a command line: Antenna House Formatter (AHFCmd), RenderX XEP (xep), a separately installed Apache FOP (another version, your own fop.xconf with fonts), or a script of your own. The XSLT stage (XML → XSL-FO) still runs inside FreeXmlToolkit with Saxon, so Show intermediate FO, the stylesheet's messages and the debugger work the same; only the rendering is handed to the external program.

Set one up: Settings → Extensions → XSL-FO Processors (or Manage processors… in the PDF/FOP panel) → Add…

Field Meaning Preset Fills the arguments for Apache FOP, Antenna House, XEP or Custom Name Shown in the panel; also used by scenarios and fxt-cli fop --processor Program The executable or script. Empty: the preset's program is looked up on the PATH (Find on PATH shows it) Arguments The argument template (below) Working folder Where the program runs. Empty: the stylesheet's folder Time limit The program is stopped after this many seconds (default 300)

Test renders a one-page document with the current settings and shows the program's output - use it before saving. Use as Default makes a processor the default for the panel, PDF scenarios and the command line.

docs.title: Argument template
docs.text:
Arguments are separated by spaces; an argument with spaces goes in double quotes. The program is started directly, never through a shell. Placeholders:

Placeholder Value ${fo} The XSL-FO file to render (required) ${pdf} / ${out} The PDF to write (required) ${xml}, ${xsl} The XML input and the stylesheet (empty when rendering a finished FO) ${baseDir} The stylesheet's folder ${title}, ${author}, ${subject} The PDF metadata from the panel ${pdfa} Present when PDF/A was asked for; expands to nothing

Arguments in square brackets are an optional group, left out when one of its placeholders is empty: [-title ${title}] passes the title only when there is one, and [-pdfprofile PDF/A-1b ${pdfa}] adds the flag only for PDF/A.

The presets start with:

Preset Program Arguments Apache FOP (external) fop -fo ${fo} -pdf ${pdf} [-pdfprofile PDF/A-1b ${pdfa}] Antenna House Formatter AHFCmd -d ${fo} -o ${pdf} RenderX XEP xep -fo ${fo} -pdf ${pdf}

Check your formatter's manual for further options (configuration file, PDF version, fonts) and add them to the template, e.g. -c /etc/fop/fop.xconf for Apache FOP.

docs.title: How a run works
docs.text:
1. The XSL-FO is written to a temporary file in the stylesheet's folder (.fxt-render-….fo, deleted afterwards), so relative image and font references resolve as they would next to the stylesheet. If that folder is not writable, the temp folder is used.
  2. The program runs with the expanded arguments in the working folder.
  3. It succeeded when it exits with code 0 and wrote the PDF (an old PDF of the same name is removed first, so it never passes for a new one).
  4. Its console output appears under Messages & events: lines with error, fatal or severe count as errors, lines with warn / warning as warnings.

Cancel in the panel stops the program (and the processes it started).

An administrator can turn external processors off with fop.external.allowed=false in the policy, or hand out a processor list with fop.processors - see Administration.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Validate first - Ensure your XML and XSL-FO files are valid before generating
  • Check error messages - If generation fails, read the error details
  • Use the preview - Review the PDF in the built-in viewer
  • Save to favorites - Quick access to frequently used files
  • PDF/A and fonts - For PDF/A-1b output, use embeddable system fonts in your stylesheet (the PDF base-14 fonts like Helvetica cannot be embedded)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution No output Check the INPUT section shows both the XML and the XSL-FO stylesheet Font issues (PDF/A) Use embeddable system fonts in the stylesheet - see the PDF/A-1b note above Image not showing Check image path is correct and accessible Generation fails The status shows a short reason; the OUTPUT panel has the stylesheet error with its line, or FOP's reason. Show intermediate FO tells you whether the FO itself is what you expect PDF looks wrong (fonts, overflow) Open Messages & events - FOP reports substituted fonts and overflowing content there External processor: "program not found" Set Program to the full path, or use Find on PATH; on Windows choose the .exe or .bat External processor: images missing Relative paths resolve against the stylesheet's folder - set Working folder or pass the base folder to the program (${baseDir}) A template does not fire / wrong values TOOLS → Debug stylesheet… and step through it - see Debugging the stylesheet

docs.title: Writing Plugins
docs.text:
This guide explains how FreeXmlToolkit plugins work and how to write, test, package and ship your own. For installing and managing plugins as a user, see Plugins.

A complete, buildable example is in the repository: examples/plugin-sample — a plugin for "order" documents with an activity, a menu item, a validator, a hint bar and a stylesheet. The built-in plugins are larger references: FundsXML (controls/shell/editor/FundsXmlPlugin), ISO 20022, ebInterface, FinDatEx and XBRL (org.fxt.freexmltoolkit.plugins.*).

docs.title: How plugins work
docs.text:
start of FreeXmlToolkit (also fxt-cli)
   │
   ├─ PluginManager.loadAll()
   │    ├─ ServiceLoader: built-in plugins (application class path)
   │    └─ every *.jar in the plugins folder, each in its own class loader
   │         (skipped when the policy plugins.external.allowed=false)
   │
   ├─ for each plugin:  id unique?  switched on (plugin.<id>.enabled / enabledByDefault())?
   │    └─ plugin.register(context)          ← your code: declare contributions, nothing else
   │         ok      → contributions are kept
   │         throws  → plugin listed as "failed", contributes nothing
   │
   └─ the window opens: activities, menus, stylesheets, schemas are in place
        ├─ activity shown the first time  → your panel factory runs (JavaFX thread)
        ├─ menu item clicked             → your action runs (JavaFX thread)
        ├─ document opened               → your document listeners run (JavaFX thread)
        ├─ any XML validation            → your validators run (background thread)
        └─ ~5 s after start              → your startup tasks run (background thread)
  • Discovery uses java.util.ServiceLoader: a plugin jar lists its plugin class in META-INF/services/org.fxt.freexmltoolkit.plugin.FxtPlugin. A jar can contain several plugins.
  • Isolation: each external jar gets its own URLClassLoader whose parent is the application. Your plugin sees the whole application API and its libraries (JavaFX, Saxon, Xerces, Gson, …); libraries you need beyond that go into your jar (shade/relocate them if they could clash).
  • Failures are contained: an exception in register disables only that plugin; a panel factory that throws shows an error in the side panel; a validator that throws becomes one error in the results; a startup task that throws is logged.
  • Changes take effect at the next start: switching a plugin on or off, adding or removing a jar.

docs.title: Your first plugin
docs.text:
package com.example.orders;

public final class OrdersPlugin implements FxtPlugin {

    @Override public String id() { return "com.example.orders"; }   // unique, stable
    @Override public String name() { return "Orders"; }             // shown in Settings → Plugins
    @Override public String version() { return "1.0.0"; }
    @Override public String description() { return "Checks order documents."; }

    @Override
    public void register(PluginContext context) {
        context.addActivity(new PluginActivity("orders", "Orders", "bi-cart",
                ui -> new VBox(new Label("Order tools"))));
    }
}

src/main/resources/META-INF/services/org.fxt.freexmltoolkit.plugin.FxtPlugin:

com.example.orders.OrdersPlugin

Build it against the FreeXmlToolkit jar (see Building and packaging), copy the jar into the plugins folder and restart.

docs.title: The plugin interface
docs.text: Method Purpose String id() Unique, stable id (com.example.orders). Also the settings key plugin.<id>.enabled. A second plugin with the same id is not loaded. String name() Name in Settings → Plugins String version() Shown next to the name (optional) String description() One sentence in Settings → Plugins (optional) boolean enabledByDefault() false: the plugin stays off until the user switches it on (optional industry plugins do this) void register(PluginContext context) Declares the contributions. Runs once at start, before the window exists — also in fxt-cli. Do not block, do not create UI here.

docs.title: Contributions
docs.text:
Everything a plugin adds goes through the PluginContext passed to register:

Method Adds addActivity(PluginActivity) An Activity Bar button (above Settings), a View → Activities entry and a side panel addMenuItem(PluginMenuItem) An item at the end of Tools, or in Help (and the header's Help popup) addValidator(DocumentValidator) Checks that run with every XML validation (Validation panel, F8, fxt-cli validate) addStartupTask(Runnable) A background task a few seconds after start (update checks, cache refresh) addDocumentListener(DocumentListener) A callback when a document has been opened in the editor addDocumentBadge(DocumentBadge) A small mark in the status bar while the active document is one your plugin recognises addStylesheet(String url) A CSS file added to the window, for your panels addSchema(PluginSchema) An XML Schema in the Schema Library (source Plugin) while the plugin is on service(Class<T>) An application service (see Application services) pluginId() Your id

docs.title: Activities
docs.text:
context.addActivity(new PluginActivity(
        "orders",                       // id: node id activity-orders; must not clash with other activities
        "Orders",                       // label and tooltip
        "bi-cart",                      // Bootstrap icon (https://icons.getbootstrap.com)
        Workflow.VALIDATION,            // colour family of the button and panel (optional)
        ui -> new OrdersPanel(ui),      // the side panel, created once, on the JavaFX thread
        () -> settings.isEnabled()));   // visible now? asked again on ui.refreshContributions()

The short constructor new PluginActivity(id, label, icon, panelFactory) uses the neutral colour and is always visible. Keep the panel factory cheap; load data in the background (see Threads).

docs.title: Menu items
docs.text:
context.addMenuItem(new PluginMenuItem(PluginMenuItem.Menu.TOOLS, "orders-report", "Orders Report…",
        "bi-table", ui -> ui.showActivity("orders"), null /* always visible */));

Tools items get the node id menu-tools-<id>, Help items menu-help-<id>. The visibility supplier is asked each time the menu opens.

docs.title: Validators
docs.text:
context.addValidator(new DocumentValidator() {
    @Override public String name() { return "Order rules"; }        // "source" column of the problems

    @Override public boolean accepts(String content, String documentName) {
        // cheap: look at the root element or namespace only
        return XmlScan.rootOf(content).map(root -> root[0].equals("order")).orElse(false);
    }

    @Override public List<Problem> validate(String content, String documentName) {
        return List.of(new Problem("warning", 12, "The order total is zero."));   // severity, line, message
    }
});
  • Validators run on a background thread after XSD / DTD / RELAX NG and Schematron, only for well-formed documents, and in fxt-cli validate too.
  • severity is error, warning or info; line is 1-based (0 when unknown).
  • XmlScan.of(content) reads the document once into a flat list of elements (path, text, line, attributes) — usually all a validator needs. It is securely configured (no DTDs, no external entities).

docs.title: Document listeners and editor bars
docs.text:
context.addDocumentListener((ui, path, content) -> {
    if (looksLikeAnOrder(content)) {
        ui.showEditorBar(new OrderHintBar(ui));     // one bar at a time, above the editor
    }
});

path is null for unsaved documents. Call ui.hideEditorBar() to remove the bar.

docs.title: Document badges
docs.text:
context.addDocumentBadge((path, content) -> looksLikeAnOrder(content)
        ? new DocumentBadge.Badge("Order", "bi-receipt", "Recognised as an order; the order checks apply.",
                Workflow.VALIDATION, ui -> ui.showActivity("orders"))
        : null);

The status bar asks every badge when another document becomes active, a document has been loaded or the settings were saved; return null when the document is not yours. It runs on the JavaFX thread, so look at the text only (no I/O). The chip uses the colours of the given Workflow; the click action and the icon are optional. FundsXML uses it to show that a document was recognised.

docs.title: Startup tasks
docs.text:
context.addStartupTask(() -> refreshCodeListsFromServer());   // background thread, once

Use service(ConnectionService.class) for network access so the proxy settings apply.

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text:
context.addSchema(new PluginSchema("urn:example:orders:1",
        "https://example.com/schemas/orders-1.xsd", "Orders 1.0", null));

Documents in that namespace get the schema bound automatically. Remote schemas are downloaded once and cached; the user's own Schema Library entries for the same namespace win.

docs.title: Stylesheets
docs.text:
context.addStylesheet(OrdersPlugin.class.getResource("orders.css").toExternalForm());

Your CSS can use the design tokens of the application (-fxt-text-primary, -fxt-bg-surface, -fxt-primary-text, …), so it follows the light and dark theme. See STYLE_GUIDE.jsonc in the repository.

docs.title: The application window: PluginUi
docs.text:
Panels, menu actions and document listeners receive a PluginUi (JavaFX thread only):

Method editorHost() The editor area: getActiveDocument(), getActiveText(), openFile(path), openGeneratedDocument(text, type, name), activeTabProperty(), schema binding … window() The main window (owner for dialogs and file choosers) openFile(Path) Opens a file in the editor showActivity(String id) Shows an activity (built-in ids: explorer, search, favorites, validation, transform, schema, schema-library, pdf, signature, settings) refreshContributions() Asks every plugin activity and menu item again whether it is visible showEditorBar(Node) / hideEditorBar() A bar above the editor

docs.title: Application services
docs.text:
context.service(Type.class) returns the application's instances:

Service Use PropertiesService Read and write settings — use keys starting with your plugin id (com.example.orders.serverUrl) ConnectionService HTTP(S) requests that respect the proxy settings and the administrator policy FavoritesService Add files to the user's favourites XmlService Parse, validate, format XML SchemaLibraryService Look up schemas and catalogs

Snippets and templates have their own stores: XPathSnippetRepository.getInstance() (XPath / XQuery snippets in the Query Console) and TemplateRepository.getInstance() (templates for New); the FundsXML plugin adds its snippets and sample templates there.

Classes of the application outside org.fxt.freexmltoolkit.plugin can change between versions; the plugin package is the stable API.

docs.title: Threads
docs.text:
Runs on Your code Start, before the window register JavaFX application thread panel factories, menu actions, document listeners, everything in PluginUi Background threads validators, startup tasks

Never block the JavaFX thread: do file and network work with org.fxt.freexmltoolkit.FxtGui.executorService.submit(...) (or your own executor) and update the UI with Platform.runLater(...). Validators may run concurrently for different documents; keep them stateless.

docs.title: Translations
docs.text:
The application's interface is English and German (Settings → Appearance → Language). Plugins bring their own texts. A simple way is a ResourceBundle in your jar that follows the application language:

ResourceBundle texts = ResourceBundle.getBundle("com.example.orders.messages",
        org.fxt.freexmltoolkit.i18n.I18n.locale(), OrdersPlugin.class.getClassLoader());

with messages.properties (English) and messages_de.properties (German) next to your classes.

docs.title: Settings of your plugin
docs.text: There is no settings page per plugin yet. Store settings with PropertiesService under keys that start with your id, and offer them in your side panel (for example a "Settings…" action that opens a dialog). Administrators can then pre-set or lock them in policy.properties like every other key (see Administration). The on/off switch plugin.<id>.enabled is managed by the application.

docs.title: Building and packaging
docs.text:
Compile against the FreeXmlToolkit jar — from an installation (FreeXmlToolkit.jar in its app folder) or from a source build (./gradlew jar → build/libs/FreeXmlToolkit-<version>.jar) — with Java 25 and --enable-preview. A Gradle build (see examples/plugin-sample/build.gradle.kts):

plugins { java }
java { toolchain { languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(25) } }
repositories { mavenCentral() }

dependencies {
    compileOnly(files(property("fxtJar") as String))      // provided at run time
    compileOnly("org.openjfx:javafx-controls:25:linux")   // ditto (any platform classifier)
}

tasks.withType<JavaCompile> { options.compilerArgs.add("--enable-preview") }

gradle jar -PfxtJar=/opt/freexmltoolkit/lib/app/FreeXmlToolkit.jar
cp build/libs/orders-plugin.jar ~/.freeXmlToolkit/plugins/

The jar contains your classes, META-INF/services/org.fxt.freexmltoolkit.plugin.FxtPlugin, resources (CSS, bundles, sample files) and libraries the application does not provide.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Unit-test validators directly. To test registration, register the plugin as if it had been found:

@Test
void registersItsContributions() {
    PluginManager manager = PluginManager.getInstance();
    manager.registerForTesting(new OrdersPlugin());
    assertTrue(manager.activities().stream().anyMatch(a -> a.id().equals("orders")));
}

UI tests can use TestFX like the application's own tests; PluginShellTest in the repository shows a plugin activity, menu item and editor bar inside the real shell.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• Start the application with -Dfxt.plugins.dir=/path/to/your/build/libs to load the plugin straight from your build folder.
  • The log (~/.freeXmlToolkit/logs, also Settings → Files & Cache → Open log folder) lists every plugin and its state at start (Plugins: [fundsxml=ACTIVE, com.example.orders=FAILED]) and the stack trace of a failed register, panel or validator.
  • Settings → Extensions → PLUGINS shows why a plugin failed.

docs.title: Security and administration
docs.text:
A plugin is code with the full rights of the application. Keep that in mind when you write one:

  • Use ConnectionService for network access (proxy settings, administrator policy).
  • Parse untrusted XML with XmlScan or the factories in SecureXmlFactory (no external entities).
  • Do not run external programs without the user's explicit choice (the XBRL plugin runs Arelle only from a command the user chose or installed).

Administrators control plugins with plugins.external.allowed=false (no jars from the plugins folder) and plugin.<id>.enabled=false (a single plugin), and can move the plugins folder with fxt.plugins.dir; see Plugins → Administration.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
FreeXmlToolkit has no update channel for plugins: users replace the jar in the plugins folder and restart. Settings → Extensions → PLUGINS shows version(), so raise it with every release.

Data that changes more often than your plugin can be fetched at run time, as the FundsXML plugin does:

  • Use a startup task (addStartupTask) and ConnectionService; the latter applies the proxy and certificate settings.
  • Cache the data under the user's folder.
  • Offer a setting to turn the check off.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: The API in org.fxt.freexmltoolkit.plugin is kept compatible within a major version; new contribution types are added as new methods. Build against the oldest FreeXmlToolkit version you want to support and state it in your plugin's description or README.

docs.title: ebInterface (Austrian e-invoice)
docs.text:
ebInterface is the Austrian XML standard for electronic invoices, accepted by the federal e-invoicing portal (e-Rechnung.gv.at) and many companies. The ebInterface plugin binds its schemas automatically, recalculates the invoice — line amounts, taxes, totals, payable amount — checks VAT ids and bank details and gives you a sample invoice to start from.

It is one of the industry plugins and off by default.

docs.title: Switching it on
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Extensions → PLUGINS.
  2. Tick ebInterface (Austrian e-invoice) and save the settings.
  3. Restart FreeXmlToolkit.

A receipt icon (ebInterface) then appears in the Activity Bar. Administrators can keep the plugin off with plugin.ebinterface.enabled=false (see Administration).

docs.title: Which documents it handles
docs.text: XML documents whose root element is Invoice in a namespace http://www.ebinterface.at/schema/<version>/, for example http://www.ebinterface.at/schema/6p1/. The version is taken from the namespace (6p1 → 6.1). All document types share the root Invoice — the DocumentType attribute says whether it is an invoice, credit memo, final settlement and so on.

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text: While the plugin is on, the Schema Library contains entries (source Plugin) for the versions 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 5.0, 6.0 and 6.1. Opening an invoice binds the schema of its version by namespace. The schemas are downloaded from the standard's repository on GitHub (austriapro/ebinterface-standards, file schemas/ebInterface<version>/Invoice.xsd) the first time they are needed and cached; the schemas they import (e.g. XML Signature) are resolved the same way.

docs.title: The side panel
docs.text:
ABOUT — what the plugin checks.

ACTIVE DOCUMENT — a summary of the open invoice:

ebInterface 6.1 · Invoice 2026-0042 of 2026-11-08
Biller: Beispiel Handels GmbH · 2 lines · payable 147.50 EUR
  • version, document type (DocumentType), invoice number and date;
  • the biller's name (Biller/Address/Name);
  • the number of invoice lines (ListLineItem);
  • the payable amount (PayableAmount) in the invoice currency (InvoiceCurrency).

Check Active Document runs the checks below on the editor's text (saving is not needed). The result shows the number of problems and the first ten with their line; Show All Problems opens the complete list as a text document.

New ebInterface 6.1 Invoice opens a schema-valid sample invoice as a new document: a biller and a recipient, two lines at 20 % and 10 % VAT, the tax summary, totals and payment by SEPA credit transfer. Replace parties, items and accounts with your own data.

CHECK AN IDENTIFIER — choose Austrian VAT id (UID), IBAN or BIC and paste a value:

  • UID: ATU and eight digits, the last one a check digit after the algorithm of the Austrian tax administration (✗ "ATU1234567" is not an Austrian VAT id (ATU and 8 digits).);
  • IBAN: length of the country and check digits; BIC: form after ISO 9362.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text: The checks follow the rules of the ebInterface 6.1 specification. They run from the side panel and with every validation of an ebInterface invoice — the Validation panel, F8 and fxt-cli validate — with the source ebInterface, next to the schema's problems.

docs.title: Identifiers
docs.text: Check Severity Example message every VATIdentificationNumber starting with ATU: format and check digit. ATU00000000 (the recipient has no UID) is accepted; ids of other countries are not checked error "ATU1358562" is not an Austrian VAT id (ATU and 8 digits). every IBAN: country length and check digits error IBAN AT611904300234573202 has wrong check digits. every BIC error "BKAUATW" is not a BIC (8 or 11 characters: bank, country, location, optional branch).

docs.title: Amounts
docs.text:
Check Severity When it is skipped Line amount: LineItemAmount = Quantity × UnitPrice (÷ the BaseQuantity attribute of UnitPrice, e.g. a price per 100 pieces) warning lines with a surcharge, reduction or other VAT-able tax (any element in the line whose name contains Reduction, Surcharge or OtherVATableTax) Tax amount: TaxAmount = TaxableAmount × TaxPercent ÷ 100, for every TaxItem (in lines and in the tax summary) and OtherVATableTax warning — Tax summary against the lines: the taxable amounts of Invoice/Tax/TaxItem add up to the line amounts warning invoices with surcharges or reductions on invoice level (ReductionAndSurchargeDetails) Gross total: TotalGrossAmount = taxable amounts + taxes of the tax summary warning invoice-level surcharges or reductions, OtherTax Payable amount: PayableAmount = TotalGrossAmount − PrepaidAmount + RoundingAmount error invoices with below-the-line items (BelowTheLineItem) Due date: PaymentConditions/DueDate is not before InvoiceDate warning dates not in the form YYYY-MM-DD

The first four allow a difference of one cent for rounding; the payable amount must match exactly. Every message names the expected value, for example:

LineItemAmount 120.00 is not quantity × unit price (3 × 50.00 = 150.00).
TaxAmount 25.00 is not 20 % of 100.00 (20.00).
The tax summary's taxable amounts add up to 125.00, the lines to 150.00.
TotalGrossAmount 147.00 is not taxable amounts plus taxes of the tax summary (147.50).
PayableAmount 140.00 is not TotalGrossAmount − PrepaidAmount + RoundingAmount (147.50).
The due date 2026-11-01 is before the invoice date 2026-11-08.

docs.title: Typical workflow
docs.text:
1. New ebInterface 6.1 Invoice — or open an invoice your ERP system produced.
  2. Edit it in the Text, Tree or Grid view; the schema provides auto-completion.
  3. Press F8: schema errors and the arithmetic checks appear together; click a problem to jump to it.
  4. Before uploading to e-Rechnung.gv.at, check the saved file in a script:
fxt-cli validate invoices/2026-0042.xml

docs.title: What is not checked
docs.text:
• The business rules of the e-Rechnung.gv.at portal that go beyond the specification (e.g. the order reference of the federal government, the supplier id).
  • VAT ids of other countries, and whether a UID is registered (only its check digit; use the EU VIES service for that).
  • Calculations in lines with surcharges or reductions, and totals with invoice-level surcharges, reductions or other taxes — they are skipped rather than reported wrongly.
  • Older versions are checked with the same 6.1 rules; elements that do not exist there are simply not found.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution No schema is bound Only versions 4.1–6.1 are registered, and GitHub must be reachable once for the download (proxy in Settings → Network & Security). A warning about a line amount although the invoice is right The line probably uses a price unit (BaseQuantity) or a discount that is not written as surcharge/reduction. Warnings do not make the document invalid. The check button is disabled The root is not Invoice in an http://www.ebinterface.at/schema/… namespace.

docs.title: FinDatEx Templates (EMT, EET, EPT, TPT)
docs.text:
FinDatEx (Financial Data Exchange Templates) publishes the data templates with which fund manufacturers pass product data to distributors and insurers. The FinDatEx plugin checks such template files against the field definitions of the official specifications, opens Excel template files and creates new, empty template files.

It is one of the industry plugins and off by default.

docs.title: Supported templates
docs.text:
Template Version Purpose Fields EMT — European MiFID Template V4.3 target market and costs under MiFID II 114 EET — European ESG Template V1.1.3 sustainability data under SFDR and MiFID 614 EPT — European PRIIPs Template V2.1 (version value V21 or V21UK) data for the PRIIPs KID 144 TPT — Solvency II Tripartite Template V7.0 and V8.0 look-through of fund holdings for insurers 152 / 154

FinDatEx publishes no XML Schema: the templates are exchanged as CSV or Excel files. The plugin carries, for every field, its code, definition, codification, the flag M(andatory) / O(ptional) / C(onditional) / I(ndicative) / N(o longer maintained) and — for TPT — the CIC categories the field applies to. The definitions are part of the application and are updated with it.

TPT V7 and V8: TPT V7 is required for the production of December 2026, V8 becomes mandatory for the end-March 2027 production, and both may be used in the transition. The plugin checks a file against the version its 1000_TPT_Version field names (V7.0 or V8.0). A file naming another version is checked against V8, and the version is reported.

docs.title: Switching it on
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Extensions → PLUGINS.
  2. Tick FinDatEx Templates (EMT, EET, EPT, TPT) and save the settings.
  3. Restart FreeXmlToolkit.

A table icon (FinDatEx) then appears in the Activity Bar. Administrators can keep it off with plugin.findatex.enabled=false.

docs.title: Opening a file
docs.text:
CSV files open like any other file (File → Open, Explorer, drag & drop). The plugin recognises a template file by its version field anywhere in the first 200 000 characters:

Template Version field EMT 00001_EMT_Version EET 00010_EET_Version EPT 00001_EPT_Version TPT 1000_TPT_Version

Excel files (.xlsx, .xls): click Open Excel Template File… in the side panel. The first sheet opens as a new, semicolon-separated text document with the same name and .csv:

  • dates become YYYY-MM-DD, date and time YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss;
  • numbers are written without formatting (no thousands separator, decimal point);
  • Excel booleans become Y / N; formulas are replaced by their last computed value;
  • values containing ;, quotes or line breaks are quoted.

Save the result if you want to keep it as CSV; the Excel file itself is not changed.

docs.title: Layouts
docs.text:
Both layouts used in practice are recognised automatically:

One instrument per row under a header row of field codes:

00001_EMT_Version;00002_EMT_Producer_Name;00010_Financial_Instrument_Identifying_Data;…
V4.3;Example Asset Management;AT0000A0XYZ1;…
V4.3;Example Asset Management;AT0000A0XYZ2;…

One field per row (transposed), the field code in the first column and one instrument per column:

1000_TPT_Version;V8.0;V8.0
1_Portfolio_identifying_data;AT0000A0ABC1;AT0000A0ABC1
12_CIC_code_of_the_instrument;DE31;XT72
14_Identification_code_of_the_instrument;DE0001102341;…

A file counts as "one instrument per row" when its first row contains at least two known field codes. The separator — ;, ,, | or tab — is taken from the first non-empty line (the one that occurs most often). Quoted values (RFC 4180) may contain separators, line breaks and doubled quotes. Empty rows (or empty columns in the transposed layout) are skipped.

docs.title: The side panel
docs.text:
ACTIVE DOCUMENT — what the file is:

TPT V8.0 file · 2 instruments · 154 of 154 fields · one instrument per column

the template and the version in the file, the number of instruments, how many of the file's columns are known fields of the template, and the layout when it is transposed.

Check Active Document runs the checks below. The result shows the number of problems and the first ten; Show All Problems opens the full list as a text document.

Actions:

Action What it does Open Excel Template File… Converts the first sheet of an Excel file to CSV text and opens it (see above) New EMT V4.3 File A new file with the header row of all EMT fields and one row with the version and the current date and time (UTC) filled in New EET V1.1.3 File, New EPT V21 File, New TPT V7.0 File, New TPT V8.0 File The same for the other templates

CHECK AN IDENTIFIER — ISIN (ISO 6166: form and check digit) and LEI (ISO 17442).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text: FinDatEx files are checked from the side panel (Check Active Document); they are no XML and therefore not part of the Validation panel or fxt-cli validate.

docs.title: Columns and version
docs.text: Check Severity Example message a column appears twice error The field 12_CIC_code_of_the_instrument appears twice. a column is no field of the template (typo, other version, own additions) warning 12_CIC_Code is no field of TPT V8.0. a generally mandatory field is missing as a column warning Mandatory fields 6_Valuation_date, 7_Reporting_date are missing. the file has no instruments warning The file has no instruments. the template version in the file is not the one the checks follow warning Row 1 (…): 00001_EMT_Version "V4.2": the checks follow V4.3; other versions may differ.

docs.title: Values
docs.text:
Every filled value is checked against the type of its field:

Field type Expected Example message date YYYY-MM-DD expected a date like 2026-01-31 date and time YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss expected a date and time like 2026-01-31 14:30:00 number a number with decimal point, optional exponent; percentages as fractions expected a number (decimal point, 5% = 0.05) whole number an integer within the field's range expected a number from 1 to 7 closed code list one of the listed values: Y / N, Y / N / Neutral, R / P / B / N, TPT lists such as Fixed / Floating / Variable / Inflation_linked … expected one of Y, N currency three capital letters (ISO 4217) expected an ISO 4217 currency code like EUR country ISO 3166 alpha-2 code expected an ISO 3166 country code like DE LEI form and check digits not a valid LEI CIC code (TPT) country of listing or XL (not listed) / XT (not tradable), category 0–9 / A–F, subcategory expected a CIC code like DE31 (country or XL/XT, category 0-9 or A-F, subcategory) identifier when its identification type field is 1: a valid ISIN — in TPT the issuer (47_…) and issuer group (50_…) identifiers must then be a valid LEI not a valid ISIN (identification type 1) text not longer than the field's maximum length longer than 255 characters

Value problems are errors and name the row (or, in the transposed layout, the instrument), the instrument's identifier and the field, and they jump to the line:

Row 3 (AT0000A0XYZ2): 00045_Financial_Instrument_Performance_Fee "yes": expected one of Y, N.
Instrument 2 (DE0001102341): 12_CIC_code_of_the_instrument "D31": expected a CIC code like DE31 (…).

The instrument's identifier is the identifying-data field of the template; in TPT 14_Identification_code_of_the_instrument.

docs.title: Mandatory fields
docs.text:
Empty mandatory fields are warnings:

  • EMT, EET, EPT: the fields flagged M in the general sections — data set information and instrument or manufacturer information. In the other sections, whether a field is mandatory depends on the reporting flags and on the product, so they are not checked.
  • TPT: the fields flagged M for the instrument's CIC category, the third character of 12_CIC_code_of_the_instrument. Example: 47_Issuer_identification_code is mandatory for categories 0–8 and A–F, but not for 9 (property).
Row 2 (XS1234567890): 47_Issuer_identification_code: the field is mandatory for CIC category 2 and empty.

Conditional fields (C) are not checked in any template.

At most 500 value problems are listed per file; after that the check stops with "More than 500 value problems; the rest is not listed."

docs.title: Typical workflow
docs.text:
1. Open Excel Template File… with the TPT your fund administrator delivered, or open the CSV.
  2. Check Active Document. Typical findings: dates in DD.MM.YYYY, percentages as 5 instead of 0.05, decimal commas, typos in code lists, missing issuer LEIs.
  3. Correct the values in the text editor (or open the CSV in a spreadsheet) and check again.
  4. To start a new file, use New … File — the header row is complete and in the official order.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution "The active document is not one this plugin checks." The version field (e.g. 1000_TPT_Version) is missing or spelled differently. Check the header row / the first column. Many "is no field of" warnings The file uses another version's field codes, or a header with descriptions instead of codes. All values of a row are shifted The separator was detected wrongly — the first line must contain the separator that the file uses (e.g. no single-column title line above the header). Excel dates show as numbers The cells are not formatted as dates in Excel; format them as dates, or correct the values in the CSV.

docs.title: ISO 20022 Payments (SEPA)
docs.text:
The ISO 20022 plugin helps with payment messages of the ISO 20022 standard — payment initiations (pain), interbank messages (pacs) and account reports (camt). It binds the official XML Schemas automatically, checks what a schema cannot check (check digits, control sums, the SEPA rules of the European Payments Council) and gives you SEPA sample messages to start from.

It is one of the industry plugins and off by default.

docs.title: Switching it on
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Extensions → PLUGINS.
  2. Tick ISO 20022 Payments (SEPA) and save the settings.
  3. Restart FreeXmlToolkit.

A bank icon (ISO 20022) then appears in the Activity Bar, above Settings. Administrators can keep the plugin off for everyone with plugin.iso20022.enabled=false in policy.properties (see Administration).

docs.title: Which documents it handles
docs.text:
Every XML document whose root element is in a namespace starting with urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd: — the rest of the namespace is the message id, for example urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pain.001.001.09. The plugin knows the names of these message families:

Family Name pain.001 Customer Credit Transfer Initiation pain.002 Customer Payment Status Report pain.007 Customer Payment Reversal pain.008 Customer Direct Debit Initiation pacs.002 FI To FI Payment Status Report pacs.004 Payment Return pacs.008 FI To FI Customer Credit Transfer camt.052 Bank To Customer Account Report camt.053 Bank To Customer Statement camt.054 Bank To Customer Debit Credit Notification camt.056 FI To FI Payment Cancellation Request

Other ISO 20022 messages (e.g. acmt, reda) are recognised as well; the identifier checks below run on them, the control-sum and SEPA checks do not.

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text:
While the plugin is on, the Schema Library contains an entry (source Plugin) for each of these message versions:

Area Versions pain pain.001.001.03, pain.001.001.09, pain.001.001.12, pain.002.001.03, pain.002.001.10, pain.007.001.09, pain.008.001.02, pain.008.001.08, pain.008.001.11 pacs pacs.002.001.10, pacs.004.001.09, pacs.008.001.08, pacs.008.001.13 camt camt.052.001.08, camt.053.001.02, camt.053.001.08, camt.054.001.02, camt.054.001.08, camt.056.001.08

When you open a message of one of these versions, its schema is bound by namespace — no xsi:schemaLocation needed. The schema is downloaded from iso20022.org (https://www.iso20022.org/sites/default/files/documents/messages/<area>/schemas/<message>.xsd) the first time it is needed and cached; afterwards it works offline. You get validation, auto-completion and the schema facts in the Inspector as with any other schema.

For other versions add the schema to the Schema Library yourself (namespace → file). The entries of the plugin are never written to your own library; they disappear when the plugin is switched off.

docs.title: The side panel
docs.text:
The panel has four parts.

ABOUT — a short description of what the plugin checks.

ACTIVE DOCUMENT — what the open document is, updated when you switch tabs:

pain.001.001.09 · Customer Credit Transfer Initiation
1 payment group · 2 transactions · 1234.50 EUR · SEPA
  • the message id and its name;
  • the number of payment groups (PmtInf) and of transactions — counted from the instructed amounts (InstdAmt) or interbank settlement amounts (IntrBkSttlmAmt);
  • the total of all amounts, when they all have the same currency;
  • SEPA when a service level SvcLvl/Cd is SEPA;
  • "(not well-formed)" when the XML cannot be read.

A document that is no ISO 20022 message shows "The active document is not one this plugin checks." and the check button is disabled.

Check Active Document runs the checks below on the editor's text — also on an unsaved document — in the background. The result lists the number of problems and the first ten with their line. With more than ten, Show All Problems opens the full list as a text document (severity, line, message per row).

Actions:

Action What it does New SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001) Opens a sample pain.001.001.09 message (SEPA credit transfer, schema-valid, after the EPC guidelines 2025) as a new, unsaved document New SEPA Direct Debit (pain.008) Opens a sample pain.008.001.08 message (SEPA Core direct debit with mandate) as a new, unsaved document

Change the names, IBANs and amounts and save it under a name of your choice.

CHECK AN IDENTIFIER — pick IBAN, BIC or LEI, paste a value and see at once whether it is valid (✓ Valid IBAN) or why not (✗ IBAN AT61 1904 3002 3457 3202 has wrong check digits.). Spaces in an IBAN are allowed.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text: The checks run from the side panel and with every validation of an ISO 20022 message: the Validation panel, F8 in the editor and fxt-cli validate. Their problems have the source ISO 20022 and appear next to the schema's problems. All of them are errors.

docs.title: All messages
docs.text: Check Example message IBAN values: country code, length of that country, check digits (ISO 13616) IBAN DE89370400440532013001 has wrong check digits. BICFI, BIC, AnyBIC, BICOrBEI values: 8 or 11 characters, bank code, country, location (ISO 9362) "DEUTDEF" is not a BIC (8 or 11 characters: bank, country, location, optional branch). LEI values: 20 characters and check digits (ISO 17442) LEI 5299000J2N45DDNE4Y29 has wrong check digits. every Ccy attribute is three capital letters (ISO 4217 form) "eur" is not an ISO 4217 currency code. the message is well-formed The message is not well-formed: …

docs.title: Control counts and sums
docs.text:
For pain.001 (credit transfer initiation), pain.008 (direct debit initiation) and pacs.008 (interbank credit transfer):

Check Example message GrpHdr/NbOfTxs is the number of transactions in the message NbOfTxs of the message is 3, but it has 2 transactions. GrpHdr/CtrlSum is the sum of their amounts CtrlSum of the message is 1300.00, but its transactions add up to 1234.50. PmtInf/NbOfTxs and PmtInf/CtrlSum match the transactions of that payment group (pain only) CtrlSum of payment group PMT-2026-0001 is 1000, but its transactions add up to 1234.50.

Transactions are CdtTrfTxInf (amount Amt/InstdAmt, in pacs.008 IntrBkSttlmAmt) and DrctDbtTxInf (amount InstdAmt). If a transaction has its amount in another form (e.g. an equivalent amount), the sum is not compared. Missing NbOfTxs/CtrlSum elements are not reported — the schema says whether they are required.

docs.title: SEPA rules
docs.text:
For every payment group of a pain.001 or pain.008 whose service level (PmtTpInf/SvcLvl/Cd, in the group or a transaction) is SEPA, after the EPC implementation guidelines 2025 for SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Direct Debit Core (customer-to-PSP):

Check Example message amounts are in EUR SEPA: payments are in EUR only, not CHF. amounts are between 0.01 and 999 999 999.99 SEPA: the amount must be between 0.01 and 999999999.99, not 0.00. amounts have at most two decimals SEPA: amounts have at most 2 decimals (10.005). MsgId, PmtInfId, InstrId, EndToEndId, MndtId use only the SEPA character set: a-z A-Z 0-9 / - ? : ( ) . , ' + and space SEPA: EndToEndId "Rechnung Nr. 4711 – März" uses characters outside the SEPA character set … these references do not start or end with / and contain no // SEPA: InstrId "/INV-1" must not start or end with / or contain //. the charge bearer ChrgBr is SLEV SEPA: the charge bearer is SLEV, not SHAR.

The references of the group header (MsgId) are checked with every SEPA group.

docs.title: Typical workflow
docs.text:
1. Click New SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001) — the sample opens with its schema bound.
  2. Fill in debtor, creditors and amounts. Auto-completion offers the elements the schema allows.
  3. Press F8 (or Check Active Document): schema errors and the plugin's checks appear together; a click on a problem jumps to the line.
  4. Correct NbOfTxs and CtrlSum when you add or remove transactions — the check tells you the right values.
  5. Save the file and check it again from the command line before sending it to the bank:
fxt-cli validate payments/2025-11-salaries.xml

fxt-cli validate loads the switched-on plugins, so the same checks run there (exit code 1 on errors, see Command Line).

docs.title: What is not checked
docs.text:
• Bank-specific rules beyond the EPC guidelines (e.g. national variants, cut-off times, the maximum number of transactions a bank accepts).
  • Whether an IBAN or BIC exists — only its form and check digits.
  • Rules of SEPA Instant, SDD B2B or other schemes; the SEPA rules apply to groups with service level SEPA in pain.001/pain.008 only.
  • Business rules of camt and pacs.002/pacs.004 messages besides identifiers and currencies.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution No schema is bound to my message Check the version in the namespace: only the versions listed above are bound. Add others in the Schema Library. The schema cannot be loaded when it is first needed iso20022.org must be reachable once (proxy settings in Settings → Network & Security). Afterwards the cached copy is used. See Operation without Internet for prepared machines. The ISO 20022 activity is missing The plugin is off, or your administrator disabled it. Check Settings → Extensions → PLUGINS. The check button is disabled The active document is not an ISO 20022 message (root namespace not urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:…).

docs.title: XBRL (with Arelle)
docs.text:
XBRL (eXtensible Business Reporting Language) is the XML standard for financial and regulatory reports — annual reports in ESEF, supervisory reports (COREP, FINREP, Solvency II QRTs) and many more.
