The XBRL plugin recognises XBRL instances and inline XBRL reports, shows what they contain and validates them with Arelle, the open-source XBRL processor.

It is one of the industry plugins and off by default.

docs.title: Why Arelle?
docs.text: An XBRL document is only meaningful together with its taxonomy: the schemas and linkbases it references, which define the concepts, the dimensions and the calculation and formula rules. Validating XBRL means XBRL 2.1, XBRL Dimensions, calculation linkbases and XBRL Formula — exactly what Arelle does, and what a plain XML Schema validation cannot do. FreeXmlToolkit therefore runs Arelle as a separate program. Arelle is not bundled; you install it once.

docs.title: Setting it up
docs.text:
1. Switch the plugin on: Settings → Extensions → PLUGINS, tick XBRL (with Arelle), save, restart. A chart icon (XBRL) appears in the Activity Bar.

  2. Install Arelle (Python 3.11 or later):

    pip install arelle-release

    This puts the command arelleCmdLine on the PATH (Windows: arelleCmdLine.exe in Python's Scripts folder). With a virtual environment or pipx install arelle-release it lands in that environment's bin / Scripts folder instead.

  3. Tell FreeXmlToolkit where it is, if it is not on the PATH: click Choose Arelle Command… in the XBRL side panel and pick the arelleCmdLine program. The choice is stored in the setting plugin.xbrl.arelleCommand; leave it empty to search the PATH again. On Windows .exe, .cmd and plain names are searched.

The side panel shows which Arelle is used (Arelle: /home/me/.local/bin/arelleCmdLine) or "Arelle not found — install it or choose its command."

docs.title: Which documents it handles
docs.text: Kind Recognised by XBRL instance (.xbrl, .xml) root element xbrl in the namespace http://www.xbrl.org/2003/instance Inline XBRL report (.xhtml, .html) root element html and the inline XBRL namespace http://www.xbrl.org/2013/inlineXBRL in the document

docs.title: The side panel
docs.text:
ACTIVE DOCUMENT — what the document contains:

XBRL instance · 248 facts · 12 contexts · 3 units
Arelle: /usr/local/bin/arelleCmdLine
  • facts: in an instance, the elements with a contextRef that are not part of the XBRL structure itself; in inline XBRL, the ix:nonFraction (numbers) and ix:nonNumeric (texts) elements;
  • contexts (xbrli:context) and units (xbrli:unit);
  • which Arelle is used.

Check Active Document runs Arelle on the saved file: Arelle reads the file from disk and resolves the taxonomy references relative to it. Save the document first — for an unsaved document the check reports "Save the document first: Arelle reads the file and its taxonomy references." Unsaved changes in the editor are not seen by Arelle.

The command run is

arelleCmdLine -f <file> -v --logFile <temporary file>.json --logFileMode w --logFormat "%(message)s"

Arelle writes its messages as JSON into the temporary file, which is read and deleted afterwards.

-v validates the instance against its taxonomy: XBRL 2.1, dimensions, calculations and the taxonomy's formulas. The result shows Arelle's errors and warnings with their code and line, for example

Line 57: [xbrl.4.6.2:numericUnit] Fact eu:Assets of context C1 must have a unit
Line 112: [xbrldie:PrimaryItemDimensionallyInvalidError] …

Information messages (timings, loading progress) are left out. Inconsistencies and fatal messages count as errors. Lines are given when Arelle names a place in the checked file; problems in the taxonomy have no line. Show All Problems opens the full list as a text document.

A run stops after 10 minutes ("Arelle did not finish within 10 minutes."). Large taxonomies take a while on the first run because Arelle downloads them; later runs use Arelle's cache.

docs.title: Taxonomies and network
docs.text: Arelle loads the taxonomies the document references (link:schemaRef) from the internet and caches them, with its own network settings. The proxy settings of FreeXmlToolkit do not apply to it; configure a proxy for Arelle with its --proxy option in a wrapper script, or through the HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY environment variables. For offline machines, prepare Arelle's cache or taxonomy packages (--packages) and point the plugin to a wrapper script that adds these options.

docs.title: In scripts
docs.text:
XBRL documents are not checked by the Validation panel or fxt-cli validate (those see them as plain XML). Run Arelle directly in scripts and pipelines:

arelleCmdLine -f report.xbrl -v --logFile report-log.json

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution "Arelle was not found." Install it with pip install arelle-release, or choose arelleCmdLine with Choose Arelle Command…. A configured path that no longer exists also counts as not found. "Save the document first …" Save the file; Arelle reads it from disk. "Arelle wrote no log (exit code …)" Arelle could not start or crashed. Run the command above in a terminal to see its output (e.g. a missing Python package). The file name contains characters that cmd.exe would interpret On Windows a .cmd/.bat launcher cannot safely receive names with & | < > ^ % ! or quotes. Rename the file or choose arelleCmdLine.exe instead of a script. Taxonomy cannot be loaded Arelle needs the internet (or a taxonomy package) — see Taxonomies and network. The check takes long The first run downloads the taxonomy; later runs are faster.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
FreeXmlToolkit can be extended with plugins: jar files that add an activity with its own side panel, menu items, validation checks, tasks at start and reactions to opened documents. The FundsXML extension is built as such a plugin and serves as the reference implementation.

Plugins are programs

A plugin runs inside FreeXmlToolkit with the same rights as the application: it can read and write your files and reach the network. Install plugins only from sources you trust. Administrators can switch external plugins off (see Administration).

docs.title: Installing a plugin
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Extensions → PLUGINS and click Open Plugins Folder (~/.freeXmlToolkit/plugins, on Windows %USERPROFILE%\.freeXmlToolkit\plugins).
  2. Copy the plugin's .jar file into that folder.
  3. Restart FreeXmlToolkit.

The PLUGINS card lists every plugin found at start — built-in ones and the jars in the folder — with its version and description. Untick a plugin and save the settings to switch it off; this takes effect at the next start. A plugin that could not be loaded is listed with the reason (e.g. a jar without plugin, or an error while it registered); the others still load.

docs.title: What a plugin can contribute
docs.text:
Contribution Where it appears Activity A button in the Activity Bar (above Settings) and an entry in View → Activities; its side panel is created the first time it is shown. A plugin can hide the activity while it is not in use (FundsXML: while the extension is off). Menu item At the end of the Tools menu, or in the Help menu (also in the header's Help popup) Validator Its problems appear with every XML validation — the Validation panel, F8, and fxt-cli validate — with the validator's name as source Startup task Runs once in the background a few seconds after start (FundsXML: checks for new schema versions) Document listener Is told when a document has been opened; it can show a bar above the editor (FundsXML: the hint bar) Stylesheet Added to the window, for the plugin's own panels Schema A Schema Library entry (source Plugin) while the plugin is on; never saved to the user's library

Application services — settings, favorites, XPath snippets, templates, the Schema Library — are available to a plugin through PluginContext.service(…).

docs.title: Writing a plugin
docs.text: A plugin is a class implementing org.fxt.freexmltoolkit.plugin.FxtPlugin, listed in META-INF/services/org.fxt.freexmltoolkit.plugin.FxtPlugin of its jar. The full guide — how plugins are loaded, every contribution type, threads, translations, building, testing and debugging — is Writing Plugins; a complete example project is in examples/plugin-sample.

docs.title: Built-in plugins
docs.text:
Plugin On by default FundsXML yes (its activity appears once the extension is enabled) FundsXML Extensions ISO 20022 Payments (SEPA) no ISO 20022 Payments ebInterface (Austrian e-invoice) no ebInterface FinDatEx Templates (EMT, EET, EPT, TPT) no FinDatEx Templates XBRL (with Arelle) no XBRL

A plugin can say it is off until the user switches it on (enabledByDefault()), and it can add XML Schemas to the Schema Library (context.addSchema(new PluginSchema(namespace, url, description, null))).

docs.title: Updating plugins
docs.text:
Plugins have no update channel of their own. What keeps each part current:

Part How it stays current Built-in plugins (FundsXML, ISO 20022, ebInterface, FinDatEx, XBRL) and their data (FinDatEx field definitions, ISO 20022 schemas) With the application: Help → Check for Updates… or the automatic update check, see Installation FundsXML schemas, samples, Schematron rules and snippets In addition, the FundsXML plugin checks GitHub once a day and installs a new release in the background, see FundsXML Extensions (fundsxml.update.check.enabled=false turns it off) Plugins from the plugins folder (.jar) By hand: put the new jar into the folder, remove the old one, restart. Settings → Extensions → PLUGINS shows the version that is loaded. Arelle (used by the XBRL plugin) It is a separate program: pip install -U arelle-release

With the policy update.allowed=false, application updates, and with them the built-in plugins and their data, arrive only through your software distribution. The FundsXML content check is not affected by this policy; switch it off with fundsxml.update.check.enabled=false, or switch the plugin off with plugin.fundsxml.enabled=false.

docs.title: The FundsXML plugin
docs.text: FundsXmlPlugin (built in, in controls/shell/editor/) is the reference: it contributes the FundsXML activity (visible while the extension is enabled), the FundsXML Website and FundsXML Schema Docs Help items, the startup task that keeps the schema content up to date, and a document listener that offers the extension once when a FundsXML document is opened. Switching the plugin off in Settings → PLUGINS removes all of these.

docs.title: Administration
docs.text:
Key (in policy.properties) Effect plugins.external.allowed=false No plugins are loaded from the plugins folder; built-in ones still load plugin.<id>.enabled=false The plugin is not loaded and cannot be switched on (e.g. plugin.fundsxml.enabled=false)

The plugins folder can be moved with the Java option -Dfxt.plugins.dir=<folder> (or fxt.plugins.dir in policy.properties / defaults.properties), for example to a read-only folder that software distribution fills. See Administration & Policies.

docs.title: Profiled XML Generation
docs.text: Generate customized sample XML from an XSD schema. The Generate Sample XML (Advanced)… dialog lists every element and attribute path of your schema, lets you pick a generation strategy per path, saves those settings as reusable profiles, and can write a whole batch of files in one go.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The basic Generate Sample XML action (see XSD Tools) invents generic values from the element types. The advanced dialog adds:

  • Per-XPath rules -- choose one of 11 strategies for any element or attribute (fixed value, sequence, template, omit, ...).
  • Profiles -- save the rules and options under a name and load them again later.
  • Batch generation -- write many files at once, with sequence counters that continue from file to file.

Without any rules (all rows left on Auto) the dialog produces exactly what the basic generator produces, using the same Only mandatory elements and Max. repetitions options.

docs.title: Opening the Dialog
docs.text:
1. Open your XSD in the Unified Shell so it is the active document. A new, never-saved schema works too -- the current editor text is used. For a schema file with unsaved changes you are asked first whether to save them (see step 3).
  2. Open the Schema activity in the activity bar.
  3. In the panel's TOOLS section (at the top of the panel - click its header to expand it if it is collapsed), click Sample XML with Options… (the sliders icon), which opens the Generate Sample XML (Advanced) dialog. If the schema has unsaved changes, you are first asked "Save changes to first?" - Save and Continue, Use Saved Version (generate from the file as last saved) or Cancel.

FreeXmlToolkit first scans the schema in the background and then shows the dialog with one row per element and attribute path. If the active document is not an XSD you get the message Open an XSD schema first.; if no paths can be extracted, Could not extract any XPaths from the schema.

docs.title: The Dialog
docs.text:
The advanced dialog with its per-XPath rules table

The modal dialog Generate Sample XML (Advanced) is resizable and has, from top to bottom:

Area Contents Profile bar Profile: drop-down of saved profiles, Load, Save As… Per-XPath generation rules Table with the columns XPath, Type, Strategy, Value / Pattern Hint line A one-line reminder of what the Value / Pattern cell means per strategy Options Only mandatory elements, Max. repetitions, Batch count, File name pattern Buttons OK (generate) and Cancel

There is no preview inside the dialog: the result opens as a new editor tab (single document) or is written to a folder you choose (batch) once you press OK -- see What Happens After OK.

docs.title: The Rules Table
docs.text:
The table is pre-filled from the schema; you cannot add or remove rows. Each row is one element or attribute path in schema order:

Column Editable Description XPath no The path of the element (/order/customer/name) or attribute (/order/@id). Compositor groups (xs:sequence, xs:choice, xs:all) do not appear in the path. Type no The XSD type of the element or attribute (xs:string, CustomerType, ...). Strategy yes Drop-down with the 11 strategies below. Default: Auto. Value / Pattern yes One free-text cell whose meaning depends on the strategy (fixed value, pattern, list, or reference). Double-click to edit, press Enter to commit.

Only rows whose strategy is not Auto become rules. Everything else is generated as usual.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
Strategy What it does Value / Pattern cell Auto Standard type-based generation (the default). ignored Fixed Value Always writes the literal you enter. the value, e.g. EUR Omit Leaves the element or attribute out entirely, even if the schema requires it. ignored Empty Writes the element/attribute with no content. ignored XSD Example Picks one of the example values found in the element's XSD annotations. If the schema has none, the value is empty. ignored Enum Cycle Walks through the enumeration values of the element's type in order (A, B, C, A, ...). Empty if the type has no enumeration. ignored Sequence Auto-incrementing number, starting at 1 in steps of 1. pattern with {seq:N} (zero-padded to N digits) or {seq} (no padding), e.g. ORD-{seq:4} gives ORD-0001, ORD-0002, ... A pattern without a placeholder yields just the number. XPath Reference Copies the value that was already generated for another path in the same document. the source XPath, e.g. /order/@id Random from List Picks a random entry from your list on every occurrence. comma-separated values, e.g. Mueller,Schmidt,Huber Template Builds the value from a string with placeholders (see below). the template, e.g. INV-{seq:4}-{date:yyyy} Null (xsi:nil) Writes the element as <name xsi:nil="true"/>. Only valid for nillable elements. ignored

Every strategy applies to attributes as well as elements.

docs.title: Template Placeholders
docs.text:
Placeholder Result Example {seq:N} / {seq} Auto-incrementing number, zero-padded to N digits (or unpadded) {seq:4} -> 0001 {date:format} Current date/time in a Java DateTimeFormatter pattern (default yyyy-MM-dd) {date:yyyy} -> 2026 {random:N} Random number with N digits (default 4, max 18) {random:4} -> 7283 {ref:xpath} Value already generated for another path in the same document {ref:/order/@id} {file:N} Number of the current batch file (1-based), zero-padded to N digits {file:2} -> 01

Example: INV-{seq:4}-{date:yyyy} produces INV-0001-2026, INV-0002-2026, ...

docs.title: Notes on Individual Strategies
docs.text:
• Sequence and Enum Cycle keep one counter per XPath. Repeating elements therefore get consecutive values, and the counters continue across batch files.
  • XPath Reference and {ref:...} only find values that were generated earlier in the same document (document order); otherwise the result is empty. The lookup uses the generator's internal path, so it is reliable for elements and attributes directly under the root element (such as /order/@id); paths nested inside xs:sequence/xs:choice groups may not resolve.
  • Omit, Empty, Null and Fixed Value are applied literally -- they can produce XML that does not validate (missing mandatory element, empty number, xsi:nil on a non-nillable element).
  • Rules inside an xs:choice steer the choice: if one option of a choice has a non-Auto rule somewhere in its subtree, the generator picks that option instead of a random one.
  • Elements with a fixed or default value in the schema keep that value under Auto.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Effect Only mandatory elements off Optional elements and attributes are skipped. Exception: an optional element or attribute that has a rule, or whose descendants have a rule, is still generated so the rule can take effect. Max. repetitions 2 (1..50) Upper bound for elements and choices with maxOccurs greater than 1 or unbounded. Batch count 1 (1..1000) Number of documents to generate. 1 opens a single document in the editor; anything above 1 switches to batch generation. File name pattern sample_{seq:3}.xml Names of the batch files; {seq:N} is replaced by the zero-padded file number. Only used when Batch count is greater than 1.

docs.title: What Happens After OK
docs.text:
Batch count = 1

The document is generated in the background, pretty-printed like Format Document (Shift+Alt+F), and opened as a new editor tab named Sample.xml, already bound to the schema it was generated from, so Run Validation reports Valid (or the actual problems) right away — not just Well-formed. From there you can edit it and save it wherever you like. If generation fails you get an error dialog instead.

The root element carries an xsi:schemaLocation / xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation that names the XSD by file name (for example xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="FundsXML4.xsd") — never an absolute file: path of your machine, so the sample stays valid when it is shared or moved. When you save the sample for the first time into a folder other than the schema's, that reference is rewritten to a relative path (for example ../xsd/FundsXML4.xsd), so the file keeps validating from where it lands — in FreeXmlToolkit after a restart and in other tools alike.

Batch count > 1

A folder chooser titled Choose output folder for N files appears. After you pick a folder, all files are generated and written there in the background, and a message reports how many files were written (for example Wrote 5 of 5 files to: …). Cancelling the folder chooser aborts without generating anything. The files reference the schema relative to that output folder.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text: A profile stores the current rules (all non-Auto rows with their Value / Pattern), plus the four options. Profiles are not tied to a particular schema file.

docs.title: Save As…
docs.text:
1. Set up rules and options.
  2. Click Save As…, enter a name in the Save Profile prompt and confirm.
  3. The profile appears in the Profile drop-down and is selected.

Saving under an existing name overwrites that profile. The file name is derived from the profile name; characters other than letters, digits, _ and - are replaced with _, so My Profile and My_Profile refer to the same file.

docs.title: Load
docs.text: Select a profile in the drop-down and click Load. Every row is first reset to Auto; then each rule of the profile whose XPath matches a row sets that row's strategy and value. Rules for paths that do not exist in the current schema are ignored (and are dropped when you press OK or save again). The options are restored as well.

docs.title: Where Profiles Are Stored
docs.text:
Profiles are JSON files in generation-profiles inside your FreeXmlToolkit user folder:

  • Windows: C:\Users\<your-name>\.freeXmlToolkit\generation-profiles\
  • macOS: /Users/<your-name>/.freeXmlToolkit/generation-profiles/
  • Linux: /home/<your-name>/.freeXmlToolkit/generation-profiles/

The dialog has no delete, rename, export or import function. To remove a profile, delete its .json file; to share one, copy the file into the same folder on the other machine -- it shows up in the drop-down the next time the dialog opens.

docs.title: Batch Generation
docs.text:
1. Configure rules and options as usual.
  2. Set Batch count to the number of files (up to 1000).
  3. Adjust the File name pattern if needed, for example order_{seq:3}.xml.
  4. Click OK and choose the output folder.

docs.title: File Names
docs.text:
{seq:N} in the pattern is replaced by the file number starting at 1, zero-padded to N digits; {seq} gives the unpadded number:

Pattern Files sample_{seq:3}.xml sample_001.xml, sample_002.xml, ... test_{seq}.xml test_1.xml, test_2.xml, ...

A pattern without a placeholder names every file the same, so each file overwrites the previous one -- keep the {seq:N} placeholder. An empty pattern falls back to example_1.xml, example_2.xml, ...

docs.title: How Strategies Behave Across Files
docs.text:
Strategy Across files Sequence, {seq} Counters continue: file 1 has 0001-0002, file 2 continues with 0003. Enum Cycle Cycling continues where the previous file stopped. XPath Reference, {ref} Resolved within each file; references never cross files. {file:N} The number of the current file. Random from List, Auto, {random} Fresh picks in every file. Fixed Value The same value in every file.

If every row is left on Auto, each batch file is produced by the basic generator with the given options.

docs.title: Sequential IDs
docs.text:
1. Find the ID row (for example /order/@id) and set its strategy to Sequence.
  2. Enter ORD-{seq:6} in Value / Pattern.
  3. Click OK -- the new tab contains ORD-000001, ORD-000002, ...

docs.title: Realistic Names and Fixed Codes
docs.text:
1. Set the name row to Random from List with Smith,Johnson,Williams,Brown.
  2. Set the country row to Fixed Value with US.
  3. Set the e-mail row to Template with user{seq:3}@example.com.
  4. Click OK.

docs.title: Many Files for Load Testing
docs.text:
1. Configure the rules, then set Batch count to 100 and the pattern to test_{seq:4}.xml.
  2. Click OK and pick a folder -- you get test_0001.xml to test_0100.xml.

docs.title: Minimal Documents
docs.text: Check Only mandatory elements, or set specific optional rows to Omit.

docs.title: Tips and FAQ
docs.text:
The generated XML fails validation. Check for Omit on mandatory paths, Fixed Value entries that do not match the type, Empty on numeric or date types, and Null on elements that are not nillable.

An XPath Reference stays empty. The referenced path must be generated before the referencing one (document order), and nested paths inside compositor groups may not resolve -- see Notes on Individual Strategies. Use Fixed Value or Template if you only need identical literals.

The sequence restarts at 1. Counters live only for one run (single document or one batch). Every click on OK starts again at 1; the start value and step cannot be changed in the dialog.

A saved profile loads with fewer rules than I saved. Rules are matched to table rows by their exact XPath. If the schema changed (renamed or removed paths), those rules have nothing to attach to and are skipped.

Can I generate two files with the same name? No -- the files are written into one folder, so a later file with the same name replaces the earlier one. Keep {seq:N} in the pattern.

Where is the Validate button? Not in the dialog: open the generated tab and use the Validate action of the shell (see XSD Validation).

docs.title: Projects and Transformation Scenarios
docs.text:
A project keeps the settings that belong to a set of files in one file next to them:

  • which schema, which Schematron and which transformation scenario belong to which files;
  • which XML catalogs resolve schema references;
  • named transformation scenarios: stylesheet, query or pipeline, input, parameters, output.

Commit the project file with your files. Everyone who opens it gets the same bindings and scenarios, in the application and on the command line.

docs.title: Creating and opening a project
docs.text:
File → Project holds every project action:

Menu item What it does New Project… Asks where to save the project file (.fxtproj) and opens the new, empty project Open Project… Opens a project file; the project open before is closed Open Recent Project The last eight projects; Clear List empties it Close Project Closes the project; its bindings and catalogs no longer apply Project Settings… Edits name, folders, bindings, scenarios and catalogs (see below) Validate Project Validates every file of the project that has a schema or Schematron bound Bind in Project… Binds a schema, Schematron or scenario to files of the project Add Catalog to Project… Adds an OASIS XML catalog Edit Project File Opens the project file in the editor (it is JSON)

Other ways to open a project:

  • Welcome page: it lists the recent projects under Projects; a click opens one.
  • Explorer: it shows project files with a briefcase icon. A double click opens the project; on the open project's own file, a double click opens the file in the editor.

Only one project is open at a time. It opens again at the next start, as long as its file is still there.

While a project is open, the Explorer shows the project's folders as its workspace, titled PROJECT · NAME. A project with several folders shows each one at the top level. Closing the project keeps the first folder open.

The project follows changes to its file within a few seconds: saving it in the editor, a git pull, or another program. If the changed file is no valid project file, the project keeps its previous settings.

docs.title: Bindings
docs.text:
A binding assigns things to the files whose path matches a pattern:

  • Files: a path or pattern relative to the project folder. * matches within a folder, ** across folders: data/**/*.xml matches data/a.xml and data/2026/b.xml.
  • Schema: an XSD, DTD or RELAX NG schema (.rng, .rnc). JSON files get a JSON Schema here.
  • Schematron: checked in addition to the schema.
  • Scenario: the transformation scenario of these files (see below).

Each of the three is optional, but at least one is needed. The dialog shows how many files of the project the pattern matches.

Which binding applies. For each file, schema, Schematron and scenario are taken separately, each from the first binding that matches the file and names one. A broad binding at the end can therefore add a Schematron to every file, while narrower ones before it choose the schemas:

Files Schema Schematron Scenario data/special.xml schemas/special.xsd data/**/*.xml schemas/order.xsd Report **/*.xml rules/common.sch

Here data/special.xml gets special.xsd, common.sch and the Report scenario.

What a binding does:

  • Schema: it comes before the schema a file declares (xsi:schemaLocation). The status bar shows it as … (project).
  • Schematron: Validate (F8), the Validation panel and Quick Fixes use it, unless you chose another Schematron for the document.
  • Scenario: the Transform panel chooses it when the file becomes the active document, and the Explorer offers it first under Run Scenario.

Where to bind:

  • File → Project → Bind in Project… starts with the active document: its binding, or its path and schema.
  • In the Explorer: select files, then right-click → Bind in Project…. The pattern starts as the file's path; several files of one folder become folder/*.xml.
  • Project Settings → Bindings lists all bindings. There you can edit them, remove them and change their order.

The Explorer's tooltip on a file says what the project assigns to it.

docs.title: Project Settings
docs.text:
File → Project → Project Settings… (also in the Explorer's context menu) edits the project without touching the JSON:

Tab What you can do General The project's name and its folders. The first folder is the Explorer workspace. Bindings The table of bindings: add, edit (double click), remove, move up or down. Order matters, see above. Scenarios Every scenario with all its fields: add, edit, duplicate, remove, reorder. Renaming a scenario renames it in the bindings too. Removing one removes it from the bindings. Catalogs The project's XML catalogs.

Nothing is saved until you press OK.

docs.title: Transformation scenarios
docs.text:
A scenario names a stylesheet (XSLT), an XQuery (.xq, .xquery, …) or an XProc pipeline (.xpl), together with:

  • Input: a fixed file, or ${file}, the file the scenario is run for. An empty input of an XSLT scenario means the same as ${file}. XQuery and XProc scenarios may have no input.
  • Parameters, one name=value per line. ${file} in a value is the file the scenario runs for.
  • Output method: XML, HTML, XHTML, TEXT, JSON or PDF, or Auto (from xsl:output). For PDF, the stylesheet produces XSL-FO and FOP renders it to the output file.
  • Output file: optional, except for PDF. ${name} is the input file's name without extension, ${dir} its folder: out/${dir}/${name}.html. The output must stay inside the project folder.
  • Expected result: optional, for regression checks: the file the result must match, e.g. expected/${name}.xml.

docs.title: In the Transform panel
docs.text:
While a project is open, the Transform Panel shows a SCENARIO section below OPTIONS & TOOLS.

Choosing and running a scenario:

  • Choose a scenario to fill the panel with its stylesheet, input file, parameters and output method. Run Transform and Debug then work as usual.
  • When the active document has a bound scenario, the panel chooses it by itself. A scenario you chose yourself stays chosen.
  • Run Scenario runs the chosen scenario from the files on disk and shows the result in the OUTPUT panel. A ${file} scenario runs for the active (saved) document.
  • When the scenario names an output file, the result is also written there (folders are created).
  • A PDF opens in the PDF preview.
  • Save open stylesheets first: Run Scenario does not read unsaved editor text.

Saving and removing scenarios:

  • The disk button saves the panel's current settings as a scenario: stylesheet, input, parameters and output method, plus a name and an optional output file. Tick Runs for the file it is started for to store ${file} instead of the current input. Saving under an existing name replaces that scenario.
  • The trash button removes the chosen scenario from the project.

docs.title: Regression checks
docs.text:
A scenario with an expected result can be checked: it runs as usual, and its result is compared with the expected file ("golden file"). XML results are compared by structure, like Comparing as XML — formatting and attribute order do not count. Other results (text, JSON) are compared line by line.

Values that change from run to run — a creation date, an ID — go into the expected file as XMLUnit placeholders, or are left out with an ignore XPath:

<summary created="${xmlunit.isDateTime}" run="${xmlunit.ignore}">
  <count>${xmlunit.isNumber}</count>
  <total>12.5</total>
</summary>
Setting (Edit Scenario dialog) Effect Expected result The expected file; ${name}, ${dir}, ${file} as in the output Ignore (XPath) One XPath 1.0 expression per line; the selected nodes and attributes are left out on both sides Tolerance Numbers that differ by at most this much count as equal Ignore element order, Key attributes As in the Compare view's XML Options

Checking:

  • Transform panel: choose the scenario and press the Check button (next to Run Scenario). The result shows in the OUTPUT panel and the section says ✓ or ✗ with the first differences. After a ✗, Differences opens the expected result (left) next to the actual one (right) in the Compare view, compared with the scenario's settings; Accept makes the actual result the expected one.
  • File → Project → Check Scenarios checks every scenario with an expected result; a ${file} scenario is checked for each file bound to it. A summary lists the outcome; Show Differences opens the failed ones.
  • Command line: fxt-cli scenario orders.fxtproj --check (see below).

A ready-to-run example is in the examples/regression/ folder of the installation.

Accepting writes the actual result to the expected file. Placeholders of the old expected file stay where the same element is still there, so a date stays ${xmlunit.isDateTime}. A new expected file is written as it is: put placeholders into it for values that change.

docs.title: For several files
docs.text:
Select files in the Explorer and choose Run Scenario ▸ in the context menu. The scenario bound to the first file is listed first. The scenario runs once per file:

  • One file without an output file: the result opens in a new tab.
  • Otherwise, a summary lists what was written and what failed.
  • A second file that would overwrite the output of the first fails. Use ${name} in the output so that each file gets its own.

docs.title: Validate Project
docs.text:
File → Project → Validate Project (also in the Explorer's context menu) collects every file of the project's folders that a binding gives a schema or Schematron. It skips hidden folders such as .git. It then validates each file in the background with its own schema and Schematron.

Files without a bound schema use the schema they declare. JSON files are checked against their bound JSON Schema.

The result appears in the Validation panel's batch view. There is one row per file (the tooltip shows its path), plus a text report. At most 10,000 files are checked.

docs.title: Catalogs
docs.text: The project's catalogs are used in addition to the catalogs of the Schema Library, and before them, while the project is open. They are not added to the Schema Library's own list.

docs.title: The project file
docs.text:
All paths are relative to the folder of the project file, so the project can be moved or checked out elsewhere. The file can be edited by hand; the open project picks up the change when the file is saved.

{
  "name": "Orders",
  "folders": ["."],
  "schemaBindings": [
    { "files": "data/**/*.xml", "schema": "schemas/order.xsd", "scenario": "Report" },
    { "files": "**/*.xml", "schematron": "rules/common.sch" },
    { "files": "**/*.json", "schema": "schemas/order.schema.json" }
  ],
  "catalogs": ["schemas/catalog.xml"],
  "scenarios": [
    {
      "name": "Report",
      "stylesheet": "xsl/report.xsl",
      "input": "${file}",
      "parameters": { "year": "2026" },
      "outputFormat": "HTML",
      "output": "out/${name}.html"
    },
    {
      "name": "Invoice PDF",
      "stylesheet": "xsl/invoice-fo.xsl",
      "input": "${file}",
      "outputFormat": "PDF",
      "output": "pdf/${name}.pdf"
    }
  ]
}
Field Meaning name Shown in the Explorer and the Transform panel; default: the file name folders The project's folders; the first one is the Explorer workspace (default .) schemaBindings files (pattern) → schema, schematron, scenario (each optional); first match per part catalogs OASIS XML catalogs scenarios name, stylesheet, optional input (${file} = the file it runs for), parameters, outputFormat (XML, HTML, XHTML, TEXT, JSON, PDF; default from xsl:output), output (${name}, ${dir}), processor (PDF only: builtin or the name of an external XSL-FO processor from the settings; default: the default processor), expected (like output), compare (optional: ignore list of XPaths, tolerance, ignoreOrder, keys, placeholders, ignoreComments, exactWhitespace)

Project files from before these additions keep working unchanged.

docs.title: On the command line
docs.text:
fxt-cli scenario orders.fxtproj                      # run all scenarios
fxt-cli scenario orders.fxtproj Report               # run one
fxt-cli scenario orders.fxtproj Report -i data/      # run it for every XML file in data/
fxt-cli scenario orders.fxtproj -i data/a.xml        # run the scenario bound to the file
fxt-cli scenario orders.fxtproj --list               # list them
fxt-cli scenario orders.fxtproj --check              # regression check against the expected results
fxt-cli scenario orders.fxtproj Report --accept      # make the current results the expected ones
fxt-cli validate --project orders.fxtproj data/      # bound schema, Schematron, JSON Schema

See scenario and validate --project.

docs.title: Query Console & Query Documents
docs.text: XPath, XQuery and JSONPath queries run either in the Query Console at the bottom of the editor (Ctrl+K) or as query documents (.xq, .xpath) with an input selector.

docs.title: Query Console
docs.text:
Run XPath, XQuery and JSONPath against the open document right from the editor. This is the one place for queries - the Transform panel links here with its Open Query Console button.

The Query Console is a panel that opens along the bottom of the editor. Toggle it with the terminal icon in the editor toolbar or with Ctrl+Shift+X; Ctrl+K (or a click on the header search pill) opens it and focuses the query input. Close it with the ✕ button at its top right. It runs against whichever document is currently active, so it is the fastest way to probe an XML or JSON file while you work.

The same queries run on the command line with fxt-cli query, e.g. fxt-cli query -e 'count(//Position)' data/ for every XML file of a folder.

The Query Console with IntelliSense: typing / in the XPath input opens the completion popup (document elements and axes). The mode toggle and Run are on the left; on the right, the results pane shows the previous run's XML result with syntax highlighting.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Left - the query:
  • An XPath | XQuery mode switch; the active mode is filled in the accent colour. The mode is also named on the Run button (Run XPath / Run XQuery), in the hint below the input (XPath mode · …) and in the empty input's example. While a JSON document is active, the XPath segment reads JSONPath. Next to the switch: the document the query runs against.
  • The query input with IntelliSense (autocomplete): suggestions pop up as you type after /, //, @, [, (, $ and ::, or on demand with Ctrl+Space. It suggests element and attribute names from the active document, XPath/XQuery functions, axes, operators and (in XQuery mode) FLWOR keywords. Use ↑/↓ to navigate and Enter/Tab to accept.
  • The query is syntax-highlighted as you type: keywords, functions, axes, variables, strings, numbers and comments each get their own color.
  • To run: press Ctrl+Enter in either mode (Enter inserts a new line, so queries can span several lines; a hint below the query says so). The Run button works in both modes.
  • Run - Execute the query against the active document.
  • Save - Save the current expression as a reusable snippet (see below).
  • Snippets - A menu of your saved XPath and XQuery snippets; pick one to load it (the console switches to the matching mode automatically).
  • Examples - Inserts a built-in XQuery example: Simple, FLWOR, HTML report or Data-quality check.
  • Right - the results:
  • A read-only, selectable results editor with line numbers showing the query result. XML results are syntax-highlighted (tags, attributes, values, comments), and JSON results (e.g. from JSONPath queries) get JSON highlighting; scalar results and messages stay plain.
  • Copy - Copy the full result to the clipboard.
  • Table - Shows the last XQuery result as a table in the OUTPUT panel (enabled after an XQuery run whose result can be shown as a table).

Like the text editor, every console area zooms with the mouse: hold Ctrl and scroll the mouse wheel over the query input or the results to change that area's font size (Ctrl+0 resets it).

docs.title: Running a Query
docs.text:
1. Open the console (Ctrl+K, the header search pill, the terminal icon, or Ctrl+Shift+X) - it opens focused on the query input.
  2. Choose XPath or XQuery with the mode toggle.
  3. Type your expression, then click Run (in XPath mode, Enter also runs).
  4. The result appears on the right. Use Copy to put it on the clipboard.

The console always runs against the active document. For an XML document it evaluates the expression directly; for a JSON document the toggle reads JSONPath and the input is evaluated as a JSONPath expression. When no document is open, Run is disabled and the results pane shows "No document open."

The map:, array: and math: function namespaces are pre-declared in the console, so XPath 3.1 expressions using map:merge(), array:size(), math:pow() etc. run directly - no namespace prolog needed.

Note

The Query Console is an additional, faster access point - it does not replace the Transform activity. For XSLT transformations, parameters, recent-stylesheet history, watch-and-rerun, and the OUTPUT panel's result table and HTML preview, use the Transform Panel.

docs.title: Showing Results in the Document
docs.text:
When a result contains nodes of the document - elements, attributes or text, as in //Position[TotalPercentage > 30] - the RESULTS header shows a Text | Hits switch and a counter such as 1 of 2. Hits lists every result item; a click on a node (or Enter, or the arrows next to the counter, F3 / Shift+F3 while the console has the focus) shows it in the view you are in, without switching it:

  • Text - every hit is highlighted, the current one is selected.
  • Tree - the node is selected and scrolled into view.
  • Graphic - every hit is highlighted in the grid: a whole table row when the hit is a member of repeating elements, only the cell when it is a node inside one, the row otherwise. The current hit is opened, selected and briefly flashed.

Values that are not nodes of the document - sum(...), strings, numbers, elements an XQuery builds - appear in the list without a link and are not highlighted; a result with no nodes shows no switch at all. After the document changes the hits are stale ("Document changed - run the query again"); running the query again finds the new places. Hits are shown for XPath and XQuery against XML documents (not JSONPath).

docs.title: Saving and Loading Snippets
docs.text:
Reusable XPath and XQuery expressions are saved as snippets:

  • Save - Prompts for a name and stores the current expression. XPath snippets are saved as .xpath files and XQuery snippets as .xquery files.
  • Snippets - Lists every saved snippet, prefixed with its kind (XPath / XQuery). Selecting one loads it into the console and switches to the matching mode.

Snippets are kept in the shared query folder.

Saved snippets can be managed directly from the menu. Each snippet's submenu offers, next to Load into console and Open in editor:

  • Overwrite with current query - Replaces the saved expression with the console's current input of the snippet's kind (an .xpath snippet always takes the XPath input, an .xquery snippet the XQuery input), after a confirmation.
  • Rename… - Prompts for a new name (pre-filled with the current one). Names already in use are refused.
  • Delete… - Deletes the snippet file, after a confirmation.

The entries in the FUNDSXML section (see below) are read-only - they are re-registered from the FundsXML content cache on every start and therefore offer no management actions.

Looking for ready-made queries? The installation's examples/xpath/ folder contains 32 XPath 3.1 examples and examples/xquery/ contains 17 XQuery 3.1 scripts (data-quality checks plus a reporting series producing CSV, ASCII tables/charts, Markdown and JSON), all written for the FundsXML4 sample files in examples/xml/. Paste them into the console, or copy the .xpath files into your query folder to have them appear in the Snippets menu. See the README.md in each folder for details.

When the optional FundsXML extension is enabled, the Snippets menu also shows a FUNDSXML section with the XPath/XQuery example queries shipped with the FundsXML examples (for example fund-summary, top-holdings, look-through, aggregate-by-assettype). Selecting one loads it into the console and switches the XPath/XQuery mode to match. These entries come from the FundsXML content cache and are re-registered automatically on every start.

docs.title: XPath / XQuery Autocomplete
docs.text: The XPath/XQuery inputs of the Query Console offer context-aware autocomplete in both the XPath and XQuery input fields. Suggestions appear automatically after trigger characters (/, [, @, (, $, ::) or on demand with Ctrl+Space. Depending on context it suggests element names, attribute names, XPath axes, functions, and (in XQuery) variables. Navigate with the arrow keys and press Enter or Tab to insert; Escape dismisses the popup. Functions and axes are inserted with their parentheses / :: automatically.

docs.title: Saving, Loading and Examples
docs.text: Saved queries are the Query Console's Snippets menu, and its Examples menu inserts the built-in XQuery examples - see Saving and Loading Snippets.

docs.title: Query Documents & the Input Selector
docs.text:
XPath and XQuery files are first-class editor documents: open a .xq or .xpath file (or any file from examples/xpath/ and examples/xquery/), press Run Query, and read the result in the OUTPUT panel - no console or panel switching required.

An XQuery document from examples/xquery/ with the Input dropdown open: pick an open XML-family document, a file from disk, or Automatic (the most recently active XML document, here checked). Below, the OUTPUT panel shows the query's CSV result.

docs.title: Query documents
docs.text: .xq, .xquery, .xqm, .xqy (XQuery) and .xpath (XPath) files open in a dedicated query editor with XPath/XQuery syntax highlighting and the same context-aware autocomplete as the Query Console. They appear in the Explorer workspace tree, the file choosers and drag & drop like every other supported type.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
• Run Query (the toolbar's Run button, or Ctrl+Enter) runs the active XPath/XQuery document. The Run ▾ arrow menu lists all three run actions explicitly.
  • Run Transform does the same for an active XSLT stylesheet - output format auto-detected from its xsl:output declaration.
  • Run Pipeline covers XProc documents (see XProc Pipelines).

Results appear in the OUTPUT panel docked below the editor, with execution time and result size in the status line. A tabular XQuery result (a sequence of similar elements) additionally offers a Table view; HTML results get a preview, and everything can be opened as an editor tab, opened in the browser, or saved from the panel's header buttons.

docs.title: The Input dropdown
docs.text:
The query, stylesheet or pipeline runs against an XML input document. The Input dropdown in the editor toolbar (its label reads "Input: …" followed by the chosen document) (shown only for query/XSLT/XProc documents) controls which one:

  • Automatic (last active XML document) - the default: the most recently active XML-family document (XML, XSD, XSLT, Schematron, XProc). The active document itself is never chosen - an XSLT stylesheet does not transform itself.
  • An open document - pick any other open XML-family tab. The run uses the tab's live editor text, including unsaved changes.
  • Choose XML from file system… - pick a file without opening it; it is read fresh on every run.

The choice is remembered per document for the session. If a chosen target tab is closed, the run falls back to Automatic. With no XML-family document available at all, Run Query/Run Transform show a short guard message instead of failing.

Tip

Ready-made queries ship in examples/xpath/ (32 expressions) and examples/xquery/ (17 scripts) - open any of them and press Ctrl+Enter against a FundsXML sample from examples/xml/. See Bundled Example Collections.

docs.title: Schema Library
docs.text:
The Schema Library maps namespaces (and JSON $schema URIs) to schema files, so documents that don't carry an explicit reference to their schema can still be validated and get IntelliSense automatically.

Where to find it: click Schema Library in the activity bar. The library opens as a page - a tab named Schema Library in the main editor area, just like Settings - with three tabs: Mappings, Catalogs and Cache. The side panel on the left lists the same three sections: click one to jump to its tab; the tab you are on is highlighted. A shared status line at the bottom of the page reports the outcome of the last action. The Properties inspector is hidden while the page is selected, so the tables get the full width.

docs.title: 1. What the Schema Library is
docs.text:
A mapping connects a namespace - or, for no-namespace XSDs, a root element name - to a schema location: a local file path or an http(s) URL. The library draws mappings from three sources, tried in this order:

  1. Your mappings - entries you added yourself (the Mappings tab, source USER).
  2. XML catalogs - OASIS catalog.xml files you registered (the Catalogs tab).
  3. Bundled standards - 25 well-known W3C/OASIS/industry schemas shipped with the application (see Bundled standards).

The first match wins, and a schema you bind manually in the Validation panel or status bar always takes priority over anything the library resolves.

The status bar's schema indicator shows how the active binding was resolved: a plain XSD: invoice.xsd for a schema the document declared itself, XSD: invoice.xsd (catalog) for one an XML catalog entry redirected to, XSD: invoice.xsd (library) for one a Schema Library mapping supplied, and XSD: invoice.xsd (manual) for one you picked by hand; hover the indicator for the resolved location and, for catalog/library bindings, the matched namespace or catalog target.

The library is consulted whenever a document needs a schema but doesn't say which one:

  • XML auto-binding - a document without xsi:schemaLocation / xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation is looked up by its root element's namespace, or (for no-namespace schemas) by the root element's local name.
  • xs:import / xs:include resolution - during validation, in the XSD editor, and in the legacy schema parser, an import or include that can't be resolved locally is looked up by its namespace or system ID.
  • JSON $schema URIs - a JSON document's $schema member that isn't a plain local/HTTP reference resolves through the library. Meta-schema ids (json-schema.org/...) are not bundled, so a JSON schema document still binds nothing - but you can map one yourself as a USER entry if you want schema documents validated against their dialect.
  • XSLT/XQuery doc() / document() - a system ID the engine can't resolve directly falls back to the library (and catalogs) the same way.

docs.title: 2. Mappings tab
docs.text:
The Mappings tab: namespace → schema entries with status icons, filter and action buttons.

The table has one row per mapping: a status icon, Namespace (or <root> (no namespace) for root-element mappings), Location, Kind (XSD or JSON_SCHEMA), Source (user, catalog or bundled) and an On checkbox to enable/disable the row without deleting it. All columns are visible. The filter field searches namespace, location, description and root element. Bundled rows render in italics and can only be enabled/disabled, never edited or removed.

Icon Status Meaning ✔ Available The schema file exists locally, or its remote copy is already cached ☁ Not downloaded yet A remote schema that hasn't been fetched yet ⚠ File missing A local path that no longer exists on disk ✖ Error The last download/verification attempt failed (hover for the error message)

The labelled buttons above the table: Add mapping… and Edit… open the mapping dialog (namespace, location, kind, description, optional root element); Remove deletes a USER mapping; Enable / disable toggles the On column for the selected row; Add schema of current document prefills a new mapping from the active document's bound schema; and Download / verify materializes a remote entry immediately (also clearing a remembered failure, see Troubleshooting). Double-clicking a row opens the resolved schema file as an editor tab; the context menu offers the same Open schema, Edit…, Remove and a Copy namespace action.

docs.title: 3. XML catalogs
docs.text:
The Catalogs tab: registered OASIS catalog.xml files with their entry count or error.

The Catalogs tab registers OASIS catalog.xml files and supports the core catalog elements: system, public, uri, rewriteSystem, rewriteURI, nextCatalog and xml:base. Catalogs are parsed without any network access - nextCatalog is only followed for local files, with cycle protection and a depth cap of 10.

During validation a reference is looked up by its system identifier first, then by its public identifier (public entries), and finally by namespace. public entries are therefore honoured for schema resolution even though they cannot be imported into the Mappings tab (a public identifier is not a namespace).

The tab's labelled buttons:

  • Add catalog… registers a catalog.xml file; Remove unregisters it (the file itself is untouched); Enable / disable toggles it without removing it; Reload catalogs re-parses every registered catalog (useful after editing one by hand).
  • Each row shows either the parsed entry count or, if the file is missing/invalid, a red error message.
  • Import entries into Mappings… converts the catalog's system/uri entries into regular Mappings-tab entries: a preview dialog lists what would be imported, with entries that already exist (by namespace/kind) shown disabled so you don't create duplicates.
  • Double-click a catalog row to open the catalog.xml file itself as an editor tab.

Example catalog mapping the bundled X3D 4.0 namespace to a local copy:

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<catalog xmlns="urn:oasis:names:tc:entity:xmlns:xml:catalog">
    <uri name="http://www.web3d.org/specifications/x3d-4.0.xsd"
         uri="schemas/x3d-4.0.xsd"/>
</catalog>

docs.title: Try it: the shipped catalog example
docs.text: release/examples/catalog/ contains a complete, self-contained demo: an invoice schema that imports shared types from the non-existent host schemas.example.org, a catalog.xml (with system, rewriteSystem, public and a chained nextCatalog) that maps every such reference to the local schemas/ folder, and three instance documents — one with an unreachable xsi:schemaLocation, one with only a namespace, one with deliberate errors. Register catalog.xml in the Catalogs tab, open the documents and validate; the folder's README.md walks through each step.

docs.title: 4. Schema cache
docs.text:
The Cache tab: remote schemas downloaded and cached under ~/.freeXmlToolkit/cache/schemas.

Every remote schema resolved through the library (or downloaded because a document referenced it directly) is cached under ~/.freeXmlToolkit/cache/schemas. When a schema imports or includes it, a copy is also saved next to that schema under its original name and used from then on (see Automatic Resolution of Imported Schemas). The Cache tab lists URL, Target namespace and file Size by default, with a filter over URL/namespace, plus the Downloaded timestamp and Hits (access count) - all columns are visible. The labelled buttons: Open cached file opens the cached file as an editor tab; Show in system file manager shows the cache folder in your file manager; Re-download fetches the selected entry again; Delete cached file removes one cached file (re-downloaded on next use); Clear entire cache wipes the entire cache. A footer line reports the total file count, total size and the cache hit ratio.

A collapsible "Auto-detected schemas (legacy cache)" group underneath holds the older, separate cache of schemas auto-downloaded from xsi:schemaLocation references (one folder per schema URL, keyed by an MD5 hash). It is read-only except for a Clear auto-detected schema cache button; those files are simply re-downloaded the next time a document references them.

docs.title: 5. Bundled standards
docs.text:
FreeXmlToolkit ships a curated list of 25 well-known namespace → schema mappings so common standards validate out of the box, without you having to hunt down and register the schema yourself. Bundled entries are grouped by family:

  • W3C core - xml (XML namespace attributes), XMLSchema (schema for schemas), xmldsig-core, xmlenc-core, XLink 1.1, XInclude 1.0, XSLT 2.0/3.0 stylesheet schema.
  • Markup - XHTML 1.0 Strict, SVG 1.1, MathML 3.
  • Web services - SOAP 1.1 and 1.2 envelopes, WSDL 1.1.
  • 3D graphics - X3D 3.0 through 4.0. X3D documents carry no namespace (they point at their schema with xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation), so these are no-namespace entries: 4.0 and 3.3 additionally declare the root element X3D and are found by auto-binding (4.0 is listed first and therefore wins); 3.0-3.2 are reached by their location whenever a document or an xs:import names that URL.
  • Finance/industry - FundsXML 4, XBRL 2.1 (instance + linkbase), UBL 2.1 (Invoice, Order, CreditNote), UN/CEFACT Cross Industry Invoice D16B (ZUGFeRD/Factur-X).

The JSON Schema meta-schemas are deliberately not bundled: $schema in a JSON schema document declares its dialect, not a validation binding, and a bundled meta-schema mapping would bind every schema document to it. Add one as your own mapping if you want that.

The list itself lives in src/main/resources/schema-library/bundled.json. Bundled entries are not downloaded at install time - like any remote mapping, the actual schema file is fetched into the cache the first time it's needed, so a bundled entry needs network access once before it shows the ✔ Available status.

Offline rule: a remote library entry is downloaded on first use only when remote downloads are permitted. Starting the application with -Dfxt.schema.namespaceFallback=false turns them off (the test suite does this) - resolution then uses local files and already-cached copies only, and every other entry is simply a miss. Local entries and cached entries always resolve, with or without network access.

docs.title: 6. Settings
docs.text:
The SCHEMA LIBRARY card in Settings (gear icon at the bottom of the activity bar, group Schemas & Validation) holds:

  • "Use the Schema Library to bind schemas automatically" - controls automatic binding in the editor only (default on): the XML root-namespace / root-element lookup and the JSON $schema lookup described in §1. Turning it off means a document without its own schema reference stays unbound. It does not switch the library off: the resolver hooks - xs:import / xs:include resolution, XML catalogs and XSLT/XQuery doc() / document() - keep consulting the library either way, and manual bindings are unaffected.
  • The library file location, ~/.freeXmlToolkit/schema-library.json, shown for reference.
  • A "Manage schema cache…" link that opens the Schema Library page directly on its Cache tab. The same link also appears in the TEMP & CACHE card (group Files & Cache).

docs.title: 7. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
A document isn't binding a schema I expect:

  • Check the namespace actually matches - a typo or a trailing slash difference means no match. For no-namespace XSDs, the library matches by root element name instead.
  • Make sure the mapping's On checkbox is checked; a disabled entry (including a disabled catalog) is skipped during resolution.
  • Confirm the "Use the Schema Library to bind schemas automatically" setting is on (it gates editor auto-binding only, not xs:import/catalog resolution).
  • If the document already has a manually bound schema (or an xsi:schemaLocation), that wins - the library is only consulted when there's no other reference.

A catalog shows a red error: the file is missing, unreadable, or not well-formed XML. Fix the file and click Reload catalogs, or check the nextCatalog chain - only local files are followed, and the depth is capped at 10.

A download keeps failing / the status stays ✖ error: hover the status icon for the error message. A failed download is remembered for 10 minutes to avoid hammering an unreachable server; use Download / verify on the Mappings tab to retry immediately.

A remote mapping never leaves ☁ "Not downloaded yet": remote downloads may be turned off (-Dfxt.schema.namespaceFallback=false); with them off only local and already-cached entries resolve. Use Download / verify to fetch one explicitly.

"URL is not allowed" when adding a mapping: the location resolves to a private or internal network address (loopback, link-local, RFC 1918 ranges, etc.) and is rejected as unsafe - remote schema locations must be reachable public URLs.

docs.title: Schema Support
docs.text: FreeXmlToolkit supports different schema formats for validating your XML and JSON files. This page explains what's supported and what isn't.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Schemas define rules for your XML documents - what elements are allowed, what order they should be in, and what values they can contain.

docs.title: XSD (XML Schema Definition)
docs.text:
The Validation panel - an XML document checked against its bound XSD schema

Full Support - The main schema format used for XML validation.

Feature Description Validation Check if XML files follow schema rules Auto-Completion Get suggestions while typing based on schema Auto-Detection Schema is found automatically from XML files Documentation Generate readable documentation from schemas Sample Data Create test XML files from schema definitions Visual Display See schema structure as diagrams

What You Can Define: - Elements and their order - Required and optional fields - Data types (text, numbers, dates) - Allowed values - Documentation

docs.title: Schematron
docs.text:
A Schematron rules file (.sch) open as a normal document in the editor

Business Rules - For validation rules that go beyond structure.

Feature Description Custom Rules Write your own validation logic Real-time Checking See errors as you edit Clear Messages Define helpful error messages Flexible Rules Apply different rules in different situations

Best For: - "If field A is filled, then field B must also be filled" - "The total must equal the sum of all items" - "Each ID must be unique in the document"

docs.title: JSON Schema
docs.text:
Full Support (for JSON documents) - The standard schema format for validating JSON files.

Feature Description Validation Check if JSON files follow schema rules Auto-Detection A schema referenced by the document's $schema member is bound automatically Manual Binding Bind a schema via the status bar indicator, the Validation panel, or drag & drop Line Numbers Each problem points to the offending line in your document Dialects Draft-07, 2019-09, and 2020-12

JSON Schemas bind and validate the same way XSD schemas do for XML - see the JSON Editor page for details.

docs.title: XML Catalogs (OASIS)
docs.text: Full Support - Register one or more OASIS catalog.xml files in the Schema Library's Catalogs tab to resolve system, public, uri, rewriteSystem, rewriteURI, nextCatalog and xml:base entries when the toolkit looks up an xs:import/xs:include or a schema reference by system ID. During validation the lookup tries the system identifier, then the public identifier (public entries), then the namespace, so public entries resolve schemas too.

docs.title: DTD and RELAX NG
docs.text:
Documents can be validated against a DTD or a RELAX NG schema (XML syntax .rng, compact syntax .rnc). Validation is exact (Xerces for DTDs, Jing for RELAX NG); IntelliSense, the grid's entry helpers and the Properties inspector use an XML Schema translated from the grammar (Trang), which for some RELAX NG constructs is an approximation. There is no graphical editor, diagram or documentation generator for these languages.

Which grammar is used, when no XSD is bound:

The document has It is validated against <!DOCTYPE book SYSTEM "book.dtd"> or PUBLIC "…" "…" that DTD (and the internal subset, if any) <!DOCTYPE book [ … ]> (only an internal subset) the internal subset <?xml-model href="book.rng" schematypens="http://relaxng.org/ns/structure/1.0"?> that RELAX NG schema <?xml-model href="book.rnc" type="application/relax-ng-compact-syntax"?> that compact-syntax schema

An xsi:schemaLocation (XSD) takes precedence. You can also bind a .dtd, .rng or .rnc file like an XSD: click the schema indicator in the status bar, use Change in the Validation panel, or drop the file there. A document's own DOCTYPE wins over a bound DTD.

Where DTDs come from: the XML catalogs and the Schema Library first (public and system identifiers — the way to use DocBook, XHTML or other standard DTDs offline), then local files relative to the document, then — for http/https addresses only — the schema cache, which downloads once through the proxy settings. A DTD that cannot be loaded is reported as a warning and the document is checked for well-formedness only.

Security: external entities (<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "…">) are never read, entity expansion is limited (no "billion laughs"), and DTDs are loaded only as described above. Settings → Network & Security → Validate documents against their DTD switches DTD validation off; administrators can lock it (security.dtd.allowed=false, see Administration).

On the command line, fxt-cli validate -x book.rng … binds a grammar for all files, and declared DOCTYPEs and xml-model instructions are used like xsi:schemaLocation (see Command Line).

docs.title: Loading a Schema
docs.text:
1. Automatic: Open an XML file that references a schema (xsi:schemaLocation / xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation) - it is bound automatically
  2. Manual: Open the Validation panel and click Change on the XSD row - or click the XSD indicator in the status bar and pick an .xsd file
  3. Drag & Drop: Drop an .xsd file onto the Validation panel's XSD row or onto the status bar's XSD indicator

A Schematron rules file binds the same way via the Validation panel's Schematron row. Schematron files themselves (.sch) open as normal documents in the editor.

For JSON documents, a JSON Schema binds the same way: automatically via the document's $schema member, or manually via the status bar's JSON Schema indicator, the Validation panel's JSON Schema row, or drag & drop.

docs.title: Validation Workflow
docs.text:
1. Open your XML file
  2. Bind (or auto-detect) the schema
  3. Click Run Validation in the Validation panel (or press F8) - or enable Validate while typing to check continuously
  4. Problems appear in the PROBLEMS list, each tagged with its source (XSD, Schematron, Well-formed); click one to jump to the problem location
  5. Fix issues and re-validate

docs.title: Using Both XSD and Schematron
docs.text: For the best validation coverage: - Use XSD for structure (elements, order, types) - Use Schematron for business rules (relationships, conditions)

docs.title: Tips
docs.text: Tip Description Start with XSD XSD handles most validation needs Add Schematron later For business rules XSD can't express Use auto-detection Let the app find your schema automatically Check error messages They tell you exactly what's wrong

docs.title: Schematron Quick Fixes (SQF)
docs.text:
FreeXmlToolkit understands Schematron Quick Fix (SQF) definitions — the sqf:* vocabulary (namespace http://www.schematron-quickfix.com/validator/process) that lets Schematron authors attach automatic corrections to their rules. When a document is validated against a Schematron whose asserts/reports reference fixes via sqf:fix="…", the editor offers those fixes right where the problems are reported — and applies them with a single click while preserving the document's formatting.

Try it: the bundled examples include two ready-made demo pairs in examples/schematron/ — quickfix-demo.xml + quickfix-demo.sch (a fully commented Schematron covering every fix type) and funds-quickfix-demo.xml + funds-quickfix-rules.sch (realistic FundsXML business rules, including a fix whose value is computed from elsewhere in the document). Open an XML file, bind the matching .sch file in the Validation panel, and validate: every finding offers a quick fix.

docs.title: Using quick fixes
docs.text:
Bind a Schematron to your XML document as usual (Validation panel → SCHEMATRON source row, or the Explorer's one-click validation bar). After validation, problems that carry fixes can be corrected from three places:

  • Problems lists — right-click a problem row in the Validation panel or the PROBLEMS strip below the editor and pick an entry from the Quick Fix submenu.
  • Editor lightbulb — lines with fixable problems show a yellow lightbulb in the editor gutter. Click it (or press Alt+Enter / Ctrl+. on the line) to open the fix chooser at the caret.
  • Schematron report — the report table has a Fix column with a lightbulb button on fixable findings.

Applying a fix

  • changes only the affected text region — indentation and formatting of the rest of the document stay byte-for-byte untouched,
  • is a single native undo step (Ctrl+Z restores the document),
  • triggers an immediate re-validation, so resolved problems disappear from all lists.

If the document was edited after the last validation, the fix refuses to run and asks for a re-validation instead of guessing.

docs.title: Authoring fixes
docs.text:
The Schematron editor's IntelliSense completes the SQF vocabulary (sqf:fixes, sqf:fix, the four activities, sqf:user-entry, sqf:call-fix, …) including the sqf:fix / sqf:default-fix attributes on sch:assert and sch:report. A minimal example:

<sch:schema xmlns:sch="http://purl.oclc.org/dsdl/schematron" queryBinding="xslt2"
            xmlns:sqf="http://www.schematron-quickfix.com/validator/process">
  <sch:pattern>
    <sch:rule context="person">
      <sch:assert test="@id" sqf:fix="addId">Person must have an id.</sch:assert>
      <sqf:fix id="addId">
        <sqf:description>
          <sqf:title>Add generated id attribute</sqf:title>
        </sqf:description>
        <sqf:add node-type="attribute" target="id">p-1</sqf:add>
      </sqf:fix>
    </sch:rule>
  </sch:pattern>
</sch:schema>

docs.title: Supported SQF features
docs.text:
• The four activities sqf:add, sqf:delete, sqf:replace, sqf:stringReplace — including @match, @node-type (element/attribute/processing-instruction/comment/keep), @target (as attribute value template), @position (first-child/last-child/before/after), @select, @regex/@flags and @use-when conditions.
  • Dynamic content: XSLT instructions inside fix content (xsl:value-of, xsl:choose, attribute value templates, …) are executed natively (Saxon), with the rule's sch:let variables and sch:ns namespaces in scope. sqf:copy-of and sqf:keep are supported in content.
  • sqf:user-entry — the fix prompts for the value(s) in a dialog; the @default XPath is evaluated against the failing node and pre-filled.
  • sqf:call-fix / generic fixes — fixes can call other fixes with sqf:with-param-bound sqf:param parameters (cycles are detected). A fix declaring a parameter without a default is only reachable via sqf:call-fix, never offered directly.
  • Fixes may be defined rule-locally or globally under a schema-level sqf:fixes container (rule-local ids shadow global ones); sqf:group wrappers and sqf:default-fix ordering are honored, as are fixes pulled in via sch:include and same-document abstract rules (sch:extends rule="…").

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• sch:extends with an external href and abstract patterns (is-a) are not resolved for fix discovery — findings from such rules simply show no fixes.
  • $sqf:match inside sqf:stringReplace content is not supported; use regex-group() instead (the replacement content runs inside a native xsl:analyze-string matching-substring context).
  • @use-for-each (generic iteration with $sqf:current) is not supported yet.
  • Text nodes in heavily mixed content (text interleaved with comments/CDATA) may not be addressable for sqf:stringReplace; the fix then reports a clear error instead of guessing.

docs.title: Schematron Validation
docs.text:
Note: The standalone Schematron editor tab has been retired. .sch files open as ordinary editor tabs in the Unified Shell, and validation runs in the Validation activity panel. The Schematron tools — rule check, templates, tester, visual builder, documentation, and the validation report — are labelled rows in the Validation panel's SCHEMATRON AUTHORING and REPORTS & CHECKS sections. The capabilities below are unchanged; they are reached through the shell rather than a dedicated sidebar tab.

Schematron lets you create custom validation rules that go beyond what XSD schemas can check. It's perfect for validating business rules and data relationships.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
While XSD schemas check the structure of your XML (which elements can appear where), Schematron checks the content and relationships:

XSD Checks Schematron Checks Element names Data values Element order Field relationships Required fields Business rules Data types Conditional requirements

docs.title: Example Rules
docs.text:
• "If status is 'approved', an approval date must be present"
  • "The total must equal the sum of all line items"
  • "Each ID must be unique in the document"

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
Schematron files use the shell's single-row editor toolbar. Related actions sit in split buttons with a visible ▾ arrow menu; see Unified Shell - Toolbar for the full reference.

With a .sch file active, the relevant actions are:

Button Shortcut Description New Ctrl+N Open the guided New File dialog (includes Schematron) Open Ctrl+O Open an existing file Save ▾ Ctrl+S Save the current file; the arrow menu holds Save As… (Ctrl+Shift+S) and Save All Undo / Redo Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y Undo / redo the last change (icon buttons) Format ▾ Shift+Alt+F Pretty-print the file. (Note: Ctrl+Shift+F opens Find in Files, not document search.) Validate F8 Check that the Schematron file is well-formed XML (the result appears in the Validation panel's PROBLEMS list). Use Check Rules for a deeper rule-level inspection Query Console Ctrl+Shift+X Toggle the bottom XPath/XQuery console — the place to try out rule expressions

Rule templates, the tester, the visual builder, and Check Rules are reached through the Validation activity panel (see Schematron Tools in the Unified Shell).

docs.title: Editing Schematron Files
docs.text:
A .sch (or .schematron) file opens as a normal file tab in the shell's editor — there is no separate Schematron editor. The document is detected as Schematron by its namespace (http://purl.oclc.org/dsdl/schematron), which enables:

  • Syntax highlighting and IntelliSense for Schematron elements (pattern, rule, assert, report, …) in the Text view
  • A Tree view of the file's patterns, rules, and assertions (switch views in the editor toolbar)
  • Well-formedness checking with Validate (F8); rule-level problems are found with Check Rules (see below)

To create a new Schematron file, use New (Ctrl+N) and pick the Schematron template in the New File dialog. Ready-made rule snippets are inserted from Rule Templates.

docs.title: Testing XPath Expressions
docs.text: To try out a rule's context or test expression, open the XML document you want to check and press Ctrl+Shift+X to show the Query Console. It evaluates XPath (and XQuery) against the active document and lists the matching nodes, so you can refine an expression before putting it into a rule. See Query Console.

docs.title: Schematron Tools in the Unified Shell
docs.text:
The Validation activity panel offers the Schematron tools as labelled rows in two collapsible sections at the top of the panel (both open at first - click a header to collapse it). Each tool opens as a closable tool tab in the editor area:

Tool Section What It Does Rule Templates SCHEMATRON AUTHORING Insert ready-made Schematron rule patterns into the active editor Schematron Tester SCHEMATRON AUTHORING Run the rules against an XML file (pre-loads the bound Schematron, if any) Rule Builder SCHEMATRON AUTHORING Build rules visually Check Rules SCHEMATRON AUTHORING Inspect the Schematron file itself for problems Schematron Documentation SCHEMATRON AUTHORING Generate documentation for the Schematron file Validation Report REPORTS & CHECKS Open a detailed report of the last Schematron validation run

docs.title: Check Rules
docs.text:
Check Rules runs an error detector over your Schematron file and shows the issues it finds in a categorised table, so you can fix mistakes in the rules before relying on them. Issues are grouped into categories:

Category Examples XML syntax Malformed XML, unclosed tags Structural Missing or misplaced patterns, rules, or assertions XPath Invalid XPath expressions in contexts or tests Semantic Rules that can never match, or contradictory conditions Best practice Style and maintainability suggestions

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Schematron Documentation opens the Schematron documentation generator, which produces readable documentation describing the patterns, rules, and assertions in your Schematron file.

docs.title: Validation Report
docs.text:
After validating an XML document that has a Schematron file bound, Validation Report (a row in the Validation panel's REPORTS & CHECKS section) opens a Schematron Report tool tab. It shows the document name, the Schematron file, an error/warning summary, and a table with one row per finding - severity, line, message, the failed rule/test expression, and the failing node's XPath context. Clicking a row jumps to that line in the editor.

The report can be exported with Save Report (HTML) (a self-contained HTML file) or Save SVRL (XML) (the raw SVRL result of the run). See Detailed Schematron Report in the Unified Shell guide.

docs.title: Basic Structure
docs.text:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<schema xmlns="http://purl.oclc.org/dsdl/schematron">
    <title>My Validation Rules</title>

    <pattern name="Invoice Validation">
        <rule context="invoice">
            <assert test="@date">
                Every invoice must have a date attribute.
            </assert>
            <assert test="customer">
                Every invoice must have a customer element.
            </assert>
        </rule>
    </pattern>
</schema>

docs.title: Required Field
docs.text:
<rule context="order">
    <assert test="orderNumber">
        Order number is required.
    </assert>
</rule>

docs.title: Conditional Requirement
docs.text:
<rule context="order">
    <assert test="not(@status='shipped') or shipDate">
        Shipped orders must have a ship date.
    </assert>
</rule>

docs.title: Value Comparison
docs.text:
<rule context="order">
    <assert test="endDate >= startDate">
        End date must be after start date.
    </assert>
</rule>

docs.title: Sum Validation
docs.text:
<rule context="invoice">
    <assert test="sum(item/price) = total">
        Total must equal sum of item prices.
    </assert>
</rule>

docs.title: Unique Values
docs.text:
<rule context="items">
    <assert test="count(item) = count(distinct-values(item/@id))">
        All item IDs must be unique.
    </assert>
</rule>

docs.title: Cross-Reference
docs.text:
<rule context="orderLine">
    <assert test="@productId = //product/@id">
        Product ID must reference an existing product.
    </assert>
</rule>
