docs.title: Test Against XML Files
docs.text:
1. Open the Validation activity and click Schematron Tester in the SCHEMATRON AUTHORING section
  2. Pick the Schematron file with Browse… (the one bound to the active document is pre-loaded) and add the XML file(s) to test with Add XML Files
  3. Click Run Tests and review the results in the Tester tab

For a quick check of many files at once, select the XML files in the Explorer's workspace tree, right-click and choose Validate with <Schematron> - it validates them against the last-used Schematron.

docs.title: Integration with XML Editor
docs.text:
Use Schematron validation directly in the XML Editor:

  1. Open an XML file in the editor
  2. In the Validation panel's SOURCES section, click the Schematron row to select your Schematron file (or pick one from its favorites menu) - or simply drop a .sch / .schematron file from your file manager onto that row
  3. Press Validate (F8) or click Run Validation in the panel; with Validate while typing on, the document is re-checked as you edit
  4. Errors are highlighted in the editor; click a problem to jump to its location

In the PROBLEMS panel below the editor, Schematron findings carry a Schematron source badge (so they are easy to tell apart from XSD errors), and hovering a row shows the full message together with the failed test expression and the failing node's XPath. For a complete overview of a run, open the Validation Report.

If a rule defines Schematron Quick Fixes (SQF), the matching problems can be corrected automatically — from a right-click Quick Fix menu on the problem rows, from a lightbulb in the editor gutter, or from the Validation Report's Fix column. See Schematron Quick Fixes for the full guide, including how to author fixes.

docs.title: Favorites Integration
docs.text:
Save frequently used Schematron files for quick access:

  • Add Favorite (Ctrl+D) - Save current file to favorites
  • Favorites (Ctrl+Shift+D) - Show/hide the favorites panel

docs.title: XPath Reference
docs.text:
Common XPath expressions for Schematron rules:

Expression Description . Current node @attribute Attribute of current node child::element Child element parent::element Parent element //element Any element in document count(element) Count elements string-length(.) Length of text content contains(., 'text') Text contains substring starts-with(., 'text') Text starts with normalize-space(.) Normalized whitespace sum(element) Sum of numeric values distinct-values(element) Unique values

docs.title: Supported Formats
docs.text:
Format Support ISO Schematron (.sch) Full support XSLT-based Schematron Full support

Schematron validation runs on the SchXslt compiler (executed by Saxon), which fully resolves sch:include, sch:extends, and abstract patterns. Schematrons that declare queryBinding="xslt2" or "xslt3" use XPath 2.0/3.0; files without a queryBinding attribute are compiled as xslt2, so existing rule files keep working unchanged.

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text: Shortcut Action Ctrl+N New file (Schematron template available) Ctrl+S Save file Ctrl+Shift+S Save As F8 Validate the active document Ctrl+Shift+X Toggle the Query Console (XPath/XQuery) Alt+Enter / Ctrl+. Open the Quick Fix chooser on the current line Ctrl+D Add to favorites Ctrl+Shift+D Toggle favorites

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Start simple - Begin with basic rules and add complexity
  • Test both ways - Test with valid and invalid sample files
  • Clear messages - Write helpful error messages for users
  • Use patterns - Group related rules into patterns
  • Query Console - Press Ctrl+Shift+X to test XPath expressions against the open document before using them in a rule

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution Rule not firing Check the context XPath matches elements False positives Review your test condition logic Namespace issues Add namespace declarations to schema Performance slow Optimize complex XPath expressions

docs.title: Testing Schematron with XSpec
docs.text: Schematron rules can be unit-tested with XSpec (x:expect-assert, x:expect-report, x:expect-valid): see Testing with XSpec.

docs.title: Supported Versions
docs.text:
Security fixes are provided for the latest release of FreeXmlToolkit. Please update to the latest version before reporting an issue (Help → Check for Updates…).

Version Supported Latest release ✅ Older releases ❌

docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues.

Report them privately via GitHub private vulnerability reporting. If that is not possible, send an e-mail to karl.kauc@gmail.com with the subject [SECURITY] FreeXmlToolkit.

Please include:

  • The affected version and operating system
  • The type of issue (e.g. XXE, path traversal, code execution through a stylesheet, insecure update)
  • Step-by-step instructions and, if possible, a minimal proof-of-concept file
  • The impact you see — what an attacker could achieve

docs.title: What to Expect
docs.text:
• You will receive an acknowledgement within 7 days.
  • We will investigate, keep you informed about the progress and agree on a disclosure date with you.
  • Fixes are published in a new release; with your consent you will be credited in the release notes.

docs.title: Built-in Protections
docs.text: FreeXmlToolkit protects against common XML attacks (XXE, SSRF, path traversal, untrusted XSLT/XQuery extensions, tampered updates). See Security Features in the user guide for details.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Settings open as a full page (a tab in the main editor area) rather than in the narrow left side panel. The options are presented as color-coded cards, sorted into seven groups.

Click the gear icon at the bottom of the activity bar (or press Ctrl+,): the Settings page opens as a tab in the main editor area, where there is room for all options.

The Settings page: groups in the side panel, colour-coded cards in the main area

Finding a setting - the side panel on the left lists the seven groups. Click a group to scroll the page to it; the group you are looking at is highlighted. Type into the search field at the top of the side panel to filter both the group list and the cards on the page down to the matching settings; if nothing matches, the page shows "No settings match the search.".

Managed settings - on a computer where an administrator manages FreeXmlToolkit, some settings may be greyed out and a notice at the top of the page says so; see Administration & Policies.

Saving - a save bar stays fixed at the bottom of the page:

  • Unsaved changes appears as soon as you change an option that has not been saved yet.
  • Save Settings stores and applies your changes.
  • Reset to Defaults… asks for confirmation and then puts the default values into the controls. Nothing is stored until you click Save Settings, so you can still review or adjust the values first. The reset leaves your privacy / usage statistics choices, your user info, your templates, the file associations and the extension settings (FundsXML, Developer) unchanged.
  • The language applies at the next start.
  • A few actions take effect immediately, without Save: switching the theme or the accent colour, registering or unregistering file associations, and creating, editing or deleting templates.
Group Cards and options Appearance Theme - Light, Dark or System (follows the light or dark setting of the operating system, also while the application runs). Accent colour - the colour of buttons, selection, focus and links: eight presets or Own colour; see Accent colour below. Language - the language of the interface: System default, English or Deutsch (takes effect after a restart; the system default is used when it is English or German, otherwise English). Layout - Show toolbar button labels; Show activity bar labels; Use small icons; toolbar icon size (Small / Large); Show left side panel; Show Properties (inspector) panel. Rendering - JavaFX graphics pipeline: Auto / Hardware / Software (takes effect after restart), with the active pipeline and GPU status; see Rendering mode (hardware vs. software) below. Memory - Maximum memory for the application: Automatic (half of the installed memory) or a fixed limit (takes effect after restart); see Memory and large files below. Editor Editor - XML indent and JSON indent (spaces); Auto-format after loading; Pretty-print XSD on save; Pretty-print Schematron on load; Recent files to remember (1–100, default 20) - every file opened in the editor, opened in the background or saved with Save As goes into File → Recent, the Explorer's RECENT list and the Welcome page. Templates - a configurable templates directory, plus a New / Edit / Delete list of your own templates; see Managing your templates below. User Info - Name, Email and Company, used for example when generating documentation or signing. Schemas & Validation XSD - Auto-save (with an interval in minutes); Create backups on save (with the number of versions to keep, and an optional separate backup directory). Schema Library - Use the Schema Library to bind schemas automatically; shows the library file's location and a Manage schema cache… link; see Schema Library. Parser - XML parser engine (Xerces or Saxon); Allow XSLT extension functions. Files & Cache Temp & Cache - Use system temp folder or a custom temp folder; Clear Temp Folder to free disk space; Clear Cache Folder to delete cached files (downloaded schemas etc.); Manage schema cache…. Log Files - Delete old log files automatically at startup (on by default) with Keep for (days) (default 14) and Maximum total size (MB) (default 100; 0 = no limit); Clean Up Now applies the limits at once, Open log folder shows the folder, and the card names the folder with its file count and size. The log file in use is never deleted. File Associations - make FreeXmlToolkit the default application for XML, XSD, XSLT, Schematron and JSON files (per user, no admin rights); see File Associations. Network & Security HTTP Proxy - Connection: System proxy (default, includes automatic configuration via PAC/WPAD), Manual proxy (host and port) or No proxy; No proxy for: hosts connected directly (* wildcard, e.g. *.corp.example, 10.*; local addresses always); Proxy authentication: user (DOMAIN\user or user@domain also work), password (stored encrypted) and NTLM domain, or — without a user — sign-in with the Windows account (NTLM/Kerberos; takes effect after a restart); Timeouts for connecting and reading; Test Connection checks an address with the values shown, saved or not. Every connection uses these settings: schema and catalog downloads, updates, FundsXML, telemetry, doc() in XPath/XQuery, JSON Schema $refs, XProc (incl. p:http-request) and HTML previews. Security - Trust all certificates: accept any TLS certificate for HTTPS downloads (schemas, updates); use with care. Allow JavaScript and remote content in HTML previews (off: previews run no scripts and load nothing from the network). Run XProc pipelines without restrictions (off: pipelines may not run programs, run computed pipelines, send HTTP requests or load documents from the network); see Threat Model. Updates - Check for updates on startup. Privacy Usage Statistics - Enable usage tracking (local, anonymous feature-usage counters shown on the Welcome page) and Clear statistics. Below them: Send anonymous usage statistics and Send anonymous error reports (both on by default) and a What is sent? link that shows the exact data and your anonymous installation ID. See Privacy & Anonymous Telemetry. Extensions FundsXML - Enable FundsXML extensions adds the FundsXML activity to the activity bar. Developer - Record execution statistics collects duration, CPU and memory per XSLT/XQuery/validation run; view them in the Execution Statistics tool tab or via the "last run" item in the status bar. Support the Project - a Sponsor on GitHub link.

docs.title: Accent colour
docs.text:
The accent colour replaces the blue of the primary buttons, selected rows, focus rings, links, active tabs and toggles - in the shell, in dialogs, in the XSD diagram and in the grid. Pick one of the presets (Blue, Indigo, Violet, Green, Teal, Orange, Red, Graphite) or any colour with Own colour. The choice applies at once to every open window, in the light and the dark theme.

You do not have to find a colour that works everywhere: the shades derived from it are adjusted so that texts on and in the accent keep a contrast of at least 4.5:1 (WCAG AA). A very light colour, for example, is darkened for text on white and lightened for text on the dark backgrounds.

Settings → Appearance with the violet accent

The same accent in the dark theme

The workflow colours of the activities (Validation green, Transform orange, ...) stay as they are.

docs.title: Clearing the Cache Folder
docs.text: The Clear Cache Folder button in the TEMP & CACHE section deletes the contents of the application's local cache folder (~/.freeXmlToolkit/cache) - for example downloaded schemas, including schemas fetched automatically for missing xs:import references. Clearing is safe: such schemas are simply re-downloaded the next time they are needed. A confirmation dialog is shown first, because the action cannot be undone. The cache folder itself is kept; only its contents are removed.

docs.title: Memory and large files
docs.text:
The MEMORY card sets how much memory the application may use, so that large files can be opened on machines with plenty of RAM.

The editor keeps a whole document in memory several times over (text, line model, highlighting, structured views), roughly 16 times the file size. The memory limit therefore decides how large a file can be:

Maximum memory Largest file that opens 4 GB about 256 MB 8 GB about 512 MB 16 GB about 1 GB
  • Automatic (default) uses half of the installed memory.
  • A fixed value (2 GB up to the installed memory) applies from the next start; the application restarts itself once with that limit. The card shows the limit of the current session and the installed memory.
  • If the chosen limit cannot be used, the application falls back to Automatic on its own.
  • In a development run (./gradlew run) the setting has no effect; the Gradle task sets the memory.

Opening a file of 50 MB or more asks whether to open it in the editor (editing will be slow) or in the read-only Large File Viewer, which shows files of any size with a few megabytes of memory. A file that does not fit into the current memory limit can only be opened in the viewer; the message names the limit and points to this card.

docs.title: Rendering mode (hardware vs. software)
docs.text:
The RENDERING card lets you choose how JavaFX draws the UI, per machine, without relying on a fixed JVM flag.

JavaFX can render either on the GPU (hardware-accelerated, faster) or purely in software. On machines with only an integrated GPU, hardware rendering can become unstable on very large diagrams/grids, while machines with a dedicated GPU benefit from it. The Mode dropdown controls this:

Mode Behaviour Auto (default) The application detects the graphics adapter at startup and picks hardware rendering on a dedicated GPU (and on macOS), or software rendering on integrated/unknown adapters. The detection result is cached. Hardware Always prefer GPU rendering (with an automatic software fallback if the GPU pipeline cannot start). Use this if Auto does not recognize your dedicated GPU. Software Always use software rendering. Use this if hardware rendering causes display glitches or crashes on your machine.

Below the dropdown the card shows the current run's rendering status:

  • Active pipeline - what JavaFX is actually using right now: Hardware — Direct3D, Hardware — OpenGL ES2, Hardware — Metal, or Software. This is read from the live graphics pipeline, so with Auto you can see at a glance whether you ended up on hardware or software rendering.
  • Detected GPU - the graphics adapter(s) the application found on this machine.

Notes:

  • A restart is required for a change to take effect - the graphics pipeline is chosen once when the application starts. The Active pipeline line always reflects the pipeline of the running session, not an unsaved dropdown change.
  • An explicit -Dprism.order=... JVM flag (command line) still overrides this setting, so power users can force a specific pipeline for troubleshooting.
  • Auto is intentionally conservative: any adapter it cannot confidently identify as a dedicated GPU falls back to software rendering. If your dedicated GPU is not detected, switch the mode to Hardware.

docs.title: Managing your templates
docs.text:
The TEMPLATES card lets you keep your own starting templates, which then show up (filtered by file type) in the New File dialog.

  • Templates directory - Use Browse… to point the application at the folder where your templates live. Leave it empty to use the default location. Changing the directory takes effect immediately, without restarting the application.
  • Your templates - The card lists your own (non-built-in) templates. Use:
    • New - Create a template. A dialog asks for its Name, Category, Description, File type, and Content.
    • Edit - Change the selected template.
    • Delete - Remove the selected template.

Each template is stored as a .template file in the templates directory. Once saved, your templates appear in the New File dialog whenever their file type is selected. For the wider template and XPath-snippet system, see Template Management.

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text: FreeXmlToolkit is built using modern Java technologies and libraries to provide a robust, cross-platform XML and JSON processing environment.

docs.title: Java Platform
docs.text:
• Java Version: Java 25 with preview features enabled
  • Build System: Gradle 9.x with Kotlin DSL
  • Application Framework: JavaFX 25 (included in Liberica Full JDK)

docs.title: UI Framework
docs.text:
• JavaFX: 25 for cross-platform desktop GUI (bundled with Liberica Full JDK)
  • FXML: Declarative UI layout with MVC architecture
  • RichTextFX: 0.11.7 - Advanced text editing component with syntax highlighting
  • ControlsFX: 11.2.6 - Extended JavaFX controls

docs.title: XML Processing
docs.text:
• Saxon HE: 12.10 - XSLT 3.0, XPath 3.1 and XQuery processing engine
  • XML Calabash: 3.0.54 - XProc 3.0 pipeline engine (Run Pipeline for .xpl/.xproc files)
  • ph-schematron: 10.3.1 - Schematron validation (pure, XSLT and SchXslt engines)
  • Jakarta XML Bind API: 4.0.5 - XML binding and marshalling
  • Apache Xerces: 2.12.2 (exist-db fork) - XSD 1.1 validation with assertions support

docs.title: JSON Processing
docs.text:
• Gson: 2.15.0 - JSON parsing and serialization
  • JSONPath: 3.0.0 (Jayway) - JSONPath query language support
  • JSON Schema Validator: 3.0.9 (NetworkNT) - JSON Schema validation (Draft-07, 2019-09, 2020-12)

docs.title: PDF Generation
docs.text:
• Apache FOP: 2.12 - XSL-FO to PDF transformation
  • Apache PDFBox: 3.0.8 - PDF manipulation
  • Apache Batik: 1.20 - SVG processing and rendering

docs.title: Digital Signatures
docs.text:
• Apache Santuario: 4.0.4 - XML Security (XML-DSig)
  • BouncyCastle: 1.86 - Cryptographic operations for XML digital signatures
  • Java Cryptography Architecture (JCA): Native Java crypto support

docs.title: Office Integration
docs.text: • Apache POI: 6.0.0 - Excel export for validation results

docs.title: Utilities
docs.text:
• Apache Commons Lang3: 3.21.0 - String manipulation and utilities
  • Apache Commons IO: 2.22.0 - File and IO utilities
  • Apache Commons Text: 1.15.0 - Text algorithms

docs.title: Testing Framework
docs.text:
• JUnit Jupiter: 6.1.3 - Unit and integration testing
  • TestFX: 4.0.18 - JavaFX application testing framework
  • Mockito: 5.24.0 - Mocking framework for unit tests

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
• Log4j2: 2.26.1 - Comprehensive logging framework
  • SLF4J: Logging facade for library compatibility (routed into Log4j2)

docs.title: UI Enhancements
docs.text:
• IconifyIcon: In-house icon control rendering bundled Iconify Bootstrap Icons SVG data (no external icon library)
  • CSSFX: 11.5.1 - CSS hot-reloading for development
  • Thymeleaf: 3.1.5 - Template engine for documentation generation

docs.title: Model-View-Controller (MVC)
docs.text:
• Controllers: JavaFX controllers handling UI logic and user interactions
  • Services: Business logic layer for XML operations
  • Domain Models: Data transfer objects and entity representations
  • FXML Views: Declarative UI definitions

docs.title: XSD Editor V2 Architecture (MVVM Variant)
docs.text: The XSD Editor V2 uses a sophisticated MVVM variant: - Model Layer: Pure XsdNode tree with PropertyChangeSupport - Command Pattern: All editing operations for undo/redo (46 XSD commands in controls/v2/editor/commands, 16 XML-instance commands in controls/v2/xmleditor/commands) - Observable Properties: Reactive UI updates without tight coupling - Incremental Rendering: Only changed nodes re-render

docs.title: XmlService
docs.text:
• XML parsing, validation, and transformation
  • XPath and XQuery execution with context-aware autocomplete
  • Schema validation (XSD 1.0 and 1.1)
  • Document manipulation operations

docs.title: XsdDocumentationService
docs.text:
• Schema analysis and documentation generation

docs.title: Privacy & Anonymous Telemetry
docs.text: FreeXmlToolkit sends anonymous usage statistics and anonymous error reports to help improve the application. Both are switched on by default (opt-out) and can be turned off at any time. Nothing is sent before you have seen the one-time notice that appears after the first start.

docs.title: What is collected
docs.text:
Every request contains a small envelope describing the environment:

Field Example Meaning install_id 9b2d… A random UUID created on the first launch. It is not derived from your computer, user name or network and can be reset at any time. session_id 4f1c… A random UUID per application launch. app_version 2.2.0 FreeXmlToolkit version. os_name Windows Operating-system family only: Windows, macOS, Linux or Other. os_arch x64 CPU architecture family: x64, arm64 or other. java_major 25 Java feature release. locale de UI language only (no country / region).

Each usage event describes one action:

Field Meaning event_type, category, status Which feature was used (e.g. validate, xslt_transform) and whether it succeeded, failed, was cancelled, … client_event_at When it happened (UTC). doc_kind Coarse document type derived from the file extension: xml, xsd, xslt, schematron, json or other. file_count, input_bytes, element_count, error_count, duration_ms Counts, sizes and timings. is_first_run Whether this is the first launch of the installation (on the app_start event). meta A few flat technical attributes such as the view mode (text, tree, graphic).

Each error event additionally contains:

Field Meaning error_code The exception class, e.g. java.lang.NullPointerException. error_detail A stack signature: the chain of exception classes plus up to 20 code locations (class#method:line), mainly from FreeXmlToolkit's own code. If the stack contains no FreeXmlToolkit code at all, its first and last locations are kept (where it failed and what triggered it). error_hash A 16-character fingerprint of that signature, used to group identical problems. meta.where Where in the app it happened, e.g. uncaught (an exception no code handled), executor (a background task), dialog.<title> (an error dialog was shown; a dialog without a known cause carries the fixed code ui.error_dialog or ui.action_failed), or log.<class> / logwarn.<class> (the application logged an exception as an error / warning; the log message itself is never sent). The same exception is counted once, however many of these paths it passes.

A failed XSLT transformation event (xslt_transform) carries only the processor's standard error code in error_code (e.g. XTSE0010 = invalid stylesheet element, XPST0003 = XPath syntax error, SXXP0003 = input XML not well-formed) and the failure phase in meta.phase (compile, input or runtime) — never the error message, which may contain file names. A stylesheet that does not compile or an input that is not well-formed is a problem with the user's files, not with the app: those runs have status invalid_input. So do runtime failures with a serialization error code (SESU*, SEPM*, SERE*, e.g. an xsl:output version the serializer does not support); only other runtime failures have status error. The error dialog of a failed run is not reported a second time as an app error. input_bytes is the size of the source document in characters.

A failed XSD generation (xsd_generate) carries the exception class in error_code, or not_well_formed with status invalid_input when the sample XML is not well-formed. A failed update check (update_check) names a fixed reason in meta.reason: network (no response), http_<status> (e.g. http_403), empty, parse, no_version or exception.

Every feature action records why it failed the same way: the processor's error code or the exception class in error_code, a stack signature (error_detail, error_hash) for an app failure, and status invalid_input when the user's document, stylesheet, schema or environment was the cause (not well-formed input, a missing or unreadable file, an unreachable host). This applies to xslt_transform, sign, verify_signature, create_certificate, encrypt (target kind, data algorithm family, key methods, number of recipients, whether a legacy algorithm was used - never keys, passwords or content), decrypt (key source, number of decrypted elements), inspect_encryption, schema_analysis, xsd_generate, sample_generate, spreadsheet_convert, format (meta.mode = format or minify), schematron_check, quick_fix (a fix that does not apply to the document is invalid_input, a skipped one cancelled with meta.reason), replace (meta.kind = xpath/text, meta.scope = document/files), file_search (meta.kind, files searched and files that could not be read), debug_run (meta.language = xslt/xquery/schematron, meta.stage = start/run, a stopped run is cancelled), xsd_flatten, type_usages, schema_library (meta.action), template_insert and update_apply. A dialog that belongs to such an action is not counted a second time.

A PDF generation (fop_pdf) names the stage that ran last in meta.stage (transform = the XSLT run that produces the XSL-FO, render = Apache FOP rendering it) and, for a failure, the processor's error code or the exception class in error_code. A stylesheet that does not compile or an XSL-FO document FOP rejects (ValidationException) is a problem with the user's files and has status invalid_input; the error dialog of such a run is not reported a second time. A schema documentation run (schema_doc) records the format (meta.format), the duration and, for a failure, the exception class in error_code; a schema that does not parse (SAXParseException) has status invalid_input.

The spreadsheet converter (spreadsheet_convert) records the direction in meta.direction (to_spreadsheet or to_xml), the format in meta.format (xlsx, xls or csv), the duration, the size of the exported document in characters (input_bytes) and, for a failure, the exception class in error_code. A document that is not well-formed has status invalid_input; one with more rows than a sheet holds, or too large for the memory limit, has status unsupported.

Identical errors are sent only once per session (with a repeat counter), and at most 30 error events are sent per session.

docs.title: Launch, session and performance information
docs.text: Event What it contains app_start Startup time in ms, is_first_run, meta.channel (release or dev), meta.days_since_install (whole days since the anonymous ID was created), meta.package (installer, portable or none — only the kind of installation, never its folder), meta.install_source (distribution channel: standalone for a direct download, winget, scoop, homebrew or flatpak; a winget install is recognised from the second start on) and a snapshot of a few UI settings (meta.set_theme, set_toolbar_labels, set_toolbar_icons, set_activity_labels, set_rendering, set_update_check, set_xml_autoformat, set_xsd_autosave, set_schema_autobind — on/off values and fixed options only). app_exit Session length, number of opened files, actions, side panels and the maximum number of open tabs, plus the peak (sampled while the app runs) and maximum Java heap rounded to 64 MB. prev_session_crashed Sent at the next start when the previous session ended without a clean exit (crash, forced close). Contains only that session's anonymous ID and app version. The detection uses small marker files in ~/.freeXmlToolkit/sessions/. If the Java runtime itself crashed, it leaves a crash file (hs_err_pid<pid>.log) behind; the app then adds meta.jvm_crash with three fixed pieces read from that file's header: the signal (crash_signal, e.g. EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION), the faulting library or Java method (crash_frame, e.g. C fontmanager.dll) and the thread name (crash_thread). Paths, addresses, registers and the rest of the file are never read or sent, and the file is left in place. file_open, view_mode, validate, schema_analysis, schema_bind How long opening a document, switching to the Text/Tree/Graphic view, validating or analyzing took, and the document size. schema_bind tells how a schema was found for an opened document (declared, library, catalog, manual or none); when a referenced schema could not be bound, it names the source that was tried and the reason in meta.failure (unresolved = the reference could not be resolved or reached, unloadable = the schema was found but could not be loaded) and the form of the reference in meta.ref_kind (http, file, relative, urn or other) — never the location itself. A relative or file reference that cannot be resolved names a local file that does not exist (next to the document, or at an absolute path, e.g. one written on another machine) and is sent with status invalid_input. A file that cannot be read is recorded as file_open with status invalid_input (missing, unreadable or not decodable: the exception class in error_code) or error (an app failure, with its stack signature); a file that cannot be written is file_save with the same classification. An opened file and a failed write carry the name of the document's character encoding in meta.charset when it is not UTF-8 (for example windows-1252). A validation that could not run — the schema or Schematron does not load, or the validator itself failed — is validate with status invalid_input or error and the error code; problems in the document are error_count on a status ok event. A file that is not opened because of its size is recorded as file_open with status cancelled (the user declined the large-file warning) or unsupported (it does not fit into the memory limit), its size, meta.reason=too_large and the memory limit (meta.heap_max_mb). ui_stall The user interface did not respond for at least two seconds: the duration, the side panel and view mode that were active, a stack signature of the blocked code (code locations only, as for errors), and the shape of the active document: its size in characters (input_bytes), its number of lines (meta.lines) and the length class of its longest line (meta.max_line_len: <1k, <10k, <100k, >=100k; unknown above 50,000 lines, which are not scanned) — never its content. Also the garbage-collection time during the block in ms (meta.gc_ms), the heap usage at its end in percent of the memory limit (meta.heap_pct) and meta.cause=gc when collections took at least half of the block (the memory was nearly full). Pauses of the whole application (system sleep) and waits in the operating system's own loops (window dragging or live resizing, native file dialogs, showing a native popup window) are not reported. At most 10 per session. ui_freeze The user interface has not responded for ten seconds and is still blocked. Sent right away, while the freeze lasts, so that a freeze ending in a forced close is not lost: the time blocked so far, the side panel, view mode and document type, a stack signature of the blocked code (code locations only), and the memory load (meta.gc_ms, meta.heap_pct, meta.cause=gc) as for ui_stall. The document shape is not included. If the interface recovers, the regular ui_stall follows. At most 3 per session. ui_command, panel_action Which toolbar button, keyboard shortcut (e.g. mod+s), Welcome page card or side-panel action was used (fixed identifiers). edit_summary Counts per session of editing commands in the structured editors (e.g. add_element: 12, undo: 3) and of IntelliSense suggestions shown/accepted — command names only, never element names, values or text.

docs.title: What is never collected
docs.text:
• File names, folder names or paths
  • Document content, XPath/XQuery expressions, schema or element names
  • Exception messages (they often contain paths or content — only class names and code locations are used)
  • User names, e-mail addresses, the "User Info" from the settings, license or machine identifiers
  • Your IP address: the server derives only the country from it and never stores or logs the IP

docs.title: Error reports you send yourself
docs.text: Error dialogs, the About dialog and the Help menu offer Send error report… / Report a problem…. There you describe the problem in your own words and may optionally leave a contact address if you would like a reply. The checkbox Include technical details attaches the exception class, fingerprint and stack signature described above. A collapsible Preview shows exactly the JSON that will be sent.

docs.title: How to see what is sent
docs.text: Settings → Privacy → USAGE STATISTICS → What is sent? shows a sample of the exact payload (built from the events currently waiting to be sent) together with your anonymous installation ID.

docs.title: How to switch it off
docs.text:
Open Settings → Privacy → USAGE STATISTICS and clear

  • Send anonymous usage statistics and/or
  • Send anonymous error reports,

then click Save Settings. Events of the disabled kind that are still waiting to be sent are deleted immediately.

docs.title: Switching it off for every user (administrators)
docs.text:
Telemetry is switched off completely - nothing is recorded, queued or sent, and the first-start notice is not shown - when any of these is set:

Switch Value Typical use Environment variable FXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED 1, true or yes machine-wide, e.g. by group policy or a software-distribution script Environment variable DO_NOT_TRACK 1, true or yes the cross-tool Console Do Not Track convention Java system property -Dfxt.telemetry.disabled=true true a custom launcher or start script fxt.telemetry.disabled=true in the policy file true machine-wide, together with the other managed settings, see Administration & Policies

Setting the environment variable machine-wide:

  • Windows (elevated prompt): setx FXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED 1 /M. With group policy: Computer Configuration → Preferences → Windows Settings → Environment, a system variable FXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED with the value 1.
  • macOS: sudo launchctl setenv FXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED 1 (until the next restart), or a LaunchAgent that runs this command at login for a permanent setting.
  • Linux: add FXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 to /etc/environment.

The application reads the switch at start-up; restart it after setting the variable.

A single user can also switch both kinds off in ~/.freeXmlToolkit/FreeXmlToolkit.properties:

telemetry.usage.enabled=false
telemetry.errors.enabled=false

docs.title: How to reset the installation ID
docs.text: Settings → Privacy → USAGE STATISTICS → What is sent? → Reset ID replaces the anonymous installation ID with a new random one. Data sent afterwards can no longer be linked to data sent before.

docs.title: Where the data goes
docs.text: Events are sent over HTTPS to https://telemetry.status20.net, a self-hosted server operated by the FreeXmlToolkit author in the EU (Helsinki, Finland). The data is not shared with third parties and is used only to understand which features are used and which errors occur. Individual events are deleted automatically after 90 days; long-term, only anonymous, aggregated daily totals (counts per feature, version and operating system) are kept. Error reports you send yourself via Send error report… are kept until they have been reviewed. The country is derived from your IP address using the free DB-IP country database (IP Geolocation by DB-IP, CC BY 4.0); the IP address itself is never stored or logged.

docs.title: Offline use and proxies
docs.text:
Events are queued locally in ~/.freeXmlToolkit/telemetry-queue.jsonl (at most 5000 events and 14 days, oldest dropped first) and sent in small batches about every five minutes. Requests use the proxy configured in Settings → Network & Security → HTTP PROXY. If the server cannot be reached, sending is retried later with increasing pauses (up to six hours); the application is never slowed down.

The command line (fxt-cli) sends no telemetry at all.

docs.title: Template Management
docs.text:
Reusable XML snippets and document skeletons: insert them into the document you are editing, or start a new file from one. Templates can carry ${parameter} placeholders that you fill in when the template is used.

Templates power the New File dialog

Templates also appear in the guided New File dialog (filtered to the matching file type), so a brand-new document can start from a template instead of a blank page. You manage your own templates in the Settings → Editor → TEMPLATES card. See Creating templates for the New File dialog.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Templates in the Unified Shell: the Insert Template dialog and the TEMPLATES settings card

Templates let you keep document structures you type again and again - a SOAP envelope, a Maven POM, a CDATA section, a Schematron rule - and drop them into the editor with a few clicks. The parts written as ${name} are parameters: when you use a template that has parameters, FreeXmlToolkit asks for their values first and then inserts the finished text.

There are two places where templates are used:

Where What it does Insert Template (Edit → Insert Template… or Ctrl+T) Inserts a template at the caret of the active document New File dialog (toolbar New or Ctrl+N) Creates a new document from a template of the selected file type

docs.title: Inserting a Template
docs.text:
1. Open (or create) the document you want to edit and place the caret where the snippet should go.
  2. Press Ctrl+T or choose Edit → Insert Template… in the menu bar.
  3. The Insert Template dialog lists all templates as name — category; select one to see its content in the Preview box. OK is enabled once a template is selected.
  4. If the template has parameters, a second dialog asks for each value (defaults are pre-filled where the template defines them). Cancelling this dialog inserts nothing.
  5. The rendered text is inserted at the caret. Undo (Ctrl+Z) removes it again in one step.

The dialog is only available while a document is open; with no active document the shortcut does nothing.

docs.title: Built-in Templates
docs.text:
FreeXmlToolkit ships with a set of ready-made templates, grouped by category, for example:

Category Examples Basic simple-element, element-with-attributes, cdata-section, xml-comment Web services soap-envelope, rest-response, wsdl-service Build & configuration spring-config, maven-pom, api-documentation Industry financial-transaction, patient-record, vehicle-information, government-form Schema xsd-schema Testing XSpec test (XSLT), XSpec test (XQuery), XSpec test (Schematron) — a new file from one of these is saved as .xspec (see Testing with XSpec)

Built-in templates cannot be edited, but you can create your own with the same content and change it freely.

docs.title: Managing Your Own Templates
docs.text: Your templates are managed in Settings (gear icon at the bottom of the activity bar), in the TEMPLATES card (group Editor in the Settings side panel). Template changes are saved right away - you do not need to click Save Settings.

docs.title: Set the templates folder
docs.text:
1. In the TEMPLATES card, use Browse… next to Templates directory to choose the folder where your templates are kept (leave it empty for the default location, ~/.freeXmlToolkit/templates, or the bundled examples/templates folder when it exists).
  2. The change takes effect right away - no restart needed.

docs.title: Add or change a template
docs.text:
Below the folder you find the list Your templates with three buttons:

Button Action New Opens the New Template dialog. Fill in Name, Category, Description, File type and Content. Edit Opens the selected template in the Edit Template dialog to change any of its fields. Delete Removes the selected template.

Each template is saved as a .template file in the templates folder, so you can copy those files to another machine or share them with colleagues. The File type you pick decides where the template shows up in the New File dialog: it appears only when that same file type is selected.

docs.title: Creating templates for the New File dialog
docs.text:
1. Click New on the toolbar (Ctrl+N), or New file in the Explorer panel.
  2. Choose the File type that matches your template.
  3. Open the Template list - your templates appear alongside the built-in ones.
  4. Select it; if it has parameters, you are prompted to fill them in.
  5. Optionally choose a Save to location, then confirm to create the document.

See New File dialog for the other options of that dialog.

docs.title: Placeholders and Parameters
docs.text:
Write placeholders as ${name} anywhere in the template content:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<${rootElement}>
    <header>
        <title>${documentTitle}</title>
        <version>${version}</version>
    </header>
</${rootElement}>

When the template is used, every ${name} is replaced by the value you enter. A placeholder can be used several times (${rootElement} above appears twice and is filled in once).

Templates created with the built-in library or programmatically can declare typed parameters (string, integer, decimal, boolean, date, email, URL, or a list of allowed values); the parameter dialog validates the input accordingly and offers default values where defined.

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text: Shortcut Action Ctrl+T Insert Template into the active document Ctrl+N New File dialog (choose a template there)

docs.title: Tips
docs.text: Tip Description Keep it simple Smaller templates are more reusable Clear names Use descriptive parameter names such as ${customerId} instead of ${x} Use categories The Insert Template dialog shows name — category, so consistent categories make long lists scannable One file type per template Pick the File type carefully - it controls where the template is offered in the New File dialog

docs.title: Threat Model
docs.text: This page is for security reviewers and administrators. It lists what an attacker can try with the files FreeXmlToolkit opens, which defaults protect against it, which settings change them, and where the protection ends. The user-facing description of the protections is on Security Features; every network connection is listed on Operation without internet.

docs.title: Scope and assumptions
docs.text:
FreeXmlToolkit is a desktop application. It runs with the rights of the signed-in user and has no server component, no listening port and no account system. The assets to protect are the user's files, the credentials the application stores (proxy password) and the machine's network position (it may reach intranet hosts that an attacker cannot).

Untrusted input is any file the user opens or a document refers to: XML instances, XSD, XSLT, XQuery, Schematron, XProc pipelines, JSON, HTML previews and the URLs inside them (xsi:schemaLocation, xs:import, doc(), $ref). Running a stylesheet, query or pipeline is running code: treat them like scripts.

Trusted: the application package itself (signed on macOS; checksums and an SBOM with every release, see Licenses) and the update server (GitHub releases, see below).

docs.title: Threats and mitigations
docs.text: Threat Mitigation (default) Setting XXE: an XML document reads local files or URLs through external entities Parsers are created by one factory with external general and parameter entities off, external DTD loading off and JAXP secure processing on. In the editor, internal entities are not expanded. A DOCTYPE is allowed (internal subsets are common in real files). Signature trust checks and every document read for XML encryption or decryption reject any DOCTYPE. The parser Saxon reads documents with (XPath, XQuery, XSLT, grid formulas and filters) gets the same settings. – Entity expansion ("billion laughs") The parsers for documents and schemas run in secure-processing mode, which stops a document after 100,000 entity expansions; this also holds when Saxon reads a document (XPath, XQuery, XSLT, grid formulas and filters). The editor keeps internal entities as references; the StAX parsers do not read DTDs. – DTDs named by schemas Resolved to an empty document; never downloaded. – DTD validation of documents with a DOCTYPE External general entities stay off (no XXE); the DTD and its parameter-entity modules load only from XML catalogs, the Schema Library, local files, or http(s) through the schema cache (proxy settings, internal addresses refused); entity expansion is limited to 100,000. One validation or translation never mixes local files and downloads: once a DTD has read a local file other than the DOCTYPE's own DTD it downloads nothing more, and the other way round (entity text could otherwise carry a local file's contents into a URL); catalog and Schema Library entries are exempt. file: URLs naming another host (Windows network shares) are refused. RELAX NG schemas and the documents checked against them are read with external entities and DTD loading off, also when they are translated to XSD for IntelliSense; a RELAX NG schema with a DOCTYPE is not translated. The DTD setting also stops the translation of DTDs bound by a project. security.dtd.allowed=false Remote schemas (schemaLocation, xs:import) Downloaded over http/https only from public addresses: loopback, private (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), link-local, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) and multicast addresses are refused, at most 5 redirects. Downloads are checked to be a schema before they are cached. -Dfxt.schema.namespaceFallback=false, -Dfxt.schema.localCopies=false; Schema Library / OASIS catalogs map URLs to local files Stylesheets calling Java Saxon-HE has no reflexive extension calls; external functions are switched off in the transformation engine. security.xslt.allow.extensions (Settings, default off) Stylesheets and queries reading the network In XSLT, XQuery and XPath (Query Console, grid formulas and filters), doc(), document(), unparsed-text() and unparsed-text-lines() refuse http, https and ftp (URLs mapped by the Schema Library or a catalog excepted); collection() serves only the files selected for the run. – XSL-FO reading or writing remote resources FOP's resource resolver refuses remote reads and writes. – Schematron reading local files or the network The document is read by the application's secure parser and the Schematron with external entities resolved to nothing; the compiled rules run in a Saxon configuration with the same parser settings and without remote doc(), document() or unparsed-text(). – XProc pipelines running programs or reaching the network Pipelines that use p:os-exec, p:run (a pipeline computed at run time) or p:http-request, also in imported libraries, are refused before they run. Documents, imports and doc() targets may only be local files: XML Calabash's resolver allows only file: and jar: URIs, and its HTTP client is sent to an address where nothing listens. Pipelines can still read and write local files (p:store, p:file-*). security.xproc.unrestricted (Settings → Network & Security, default off) HTML previews running scripts or loading remote content Previews of HTML files, XSLT output and generated documentation run no JavaScript, open no popups, load images, styles and fonts only from data: URIs or local files (a Content-Security-Policy is added to the page) and do not follow links to remote pages. security.htmlPreview.allowActiveContent (Settings → Network & Security, default off) Forged or weak XML signatures Verification uses the JDK's XML DSig with its secure-validation default; SHA-1 is rejected; references resolve only to plain file names in the signature's own folder. – Attacks through encrypted documents (padding / Bleichenbacher oracles, oversized or crafted structures, CipherReference to other files) Decryption runs Santuario with secure validation; RSA-1_5, TripleDES and CBC modes are marked legacy, warned about and can be blocked by policy (xmlenc.legacyAlgorithms.allowed=false); AES-GCM and RSA-OAEP are the defaults. At most 10,000 EncryptedData, 64 EncryptedKeys each and 10 million PBKDF2 iterations; a CipherReference only to a file next to the document (512 MB at most). Decrypted documents open unsaved. Error messages say only that no key fits, not why. Man in the middle on updates The update check, the update download and the SHA-256 digest it is checked against always validate the server certificate, also when "Trust all certificates" is on. update.requireChecksum=true refuses updates without a published digest Man in the middle on other downloads TLS certificates are validated unless the user switches on "Trust all certificates" (meant for proxies that re-sign traffic); it applies per connection, never to the JVM defaults. ssl.trustAllCerts (default off) Code opening its own connections (proxy, TLS settings bypassed) All HTTP goes through one service; a build test fails when any other class opens a connection. – Stored proxy password Encrypted with AES-256-GCM; the key is derived (PBKDF2-SHA256) from machine identifiers, so the properties file alone does not reveal it on another machine. This protects against casual disclosure, not against code running as the same user on the same machine. – YAML that expands or loops (alias bombs, recursive aliases) when converting to JSON or XML YAML is read with the core schema only (no Java objects are created from tags); at most 50 aliases per collection, the expanded document may hold at most twice as many values as the text has characters (at least one million), duplicate keys and recursive aliases are refused. – Project files writing elsewhere (a .fxtproj from a repository or a download) The output of a scenario must be a relative path inside the project folder; ../… and absolute paths are refused before the scenario runs. – Path traversal in file names from documents Paths are validated (parent traversals, system directories, encoded sequences, null bytes, symlink escapes). – Telemetry leaking data Anonymous counts and error reports without file contents; documented on Privacy & Telemetry. FXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1 (machine-wide), Settings

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
These are not covered by the protections above. Keep them in mind when files come from untrusted sources:

  • XProc pipelines can read and write local files (p:store, p:file-copy, p:file-delete, …) with the user's rights, like a script. Run only pipelines you trust; with security.xproc.unrestricted they can also run programs and reach the network.
  • Stylesheets write files. xsl:result-document writes to any path the user may write to, as in every XSLT 2.0+ processor; this also holds for the stylesheet of a project scenario and for the stylesheet under test in an XSpec run. Only the debugger keeps such results in memory. Run only stylesheets you trust.
  • Opening a document downloads its schema. An xsi:schemaLocation with an http(s) URL is fetched when the file is opened (from public addresses only; the Schema Library and catalogs are asked first). The download reveals to that server that the file was opened.
  • Host names that do not resolve on the client are not refused by the private-address check; the connection is left to fail on its own.
  • Same-user attacks (malware running as the signed-in user) are out of scope: it can read the settings, caches and the derived key like the application itself.

docs.title: Hardened configuration
docs.text:
For machines that process untrusted files or must not contact the internet:

Goal How Users cannot change the settings below Put them into the machine-wide policy file, see Administration & Policies No telemetry Environment variable FXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 (machine-wide), or fxt.telemetry.disabled=true in the policy file No update check update.check.enabled=false in the properties file (Settings → Updates); update.allowed=false in the policy file also removes manual checks and installs Schemas only from local files Schema Library entries or an OASIS catalog for every schema; -Dfxt.schema.namespaceFallback=false Nothing written next to schemas -Dfxt.schema.localCopies=false Certificate checks everywhere Leave "Trust all certificates" off No Java from stylesheets Leave security.xslt.allow.extensions off (default) XProc without programs and network Leave security.xproc.unrestricted off (default); lock it with security.xproc.unrestricted=false in the policy file HTML previews without scripts and remote content Leave security.htmlPreview.allowActiveContent off (default); lock it in the policy file

The -D… options are Java options; the policy file takes them as fxt.…=value lines, and Operation without internet shows where else to set them for an installed application, and lists every connection and cache.

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text: See the Security Policy.

docs.title: Transform Panel
docs.text:
The panel is organized into collapsible sections (STYLESHEET, INPUT, OUTPUT METHOD, PARAMETERS) with a single primary Run Transform button and a Run automatically checkbox next to it. Results do not open as an editor tab - they appear in the OUTPUT panel docked below the editor. The run options (checkboxes) and the advanced tools share the OPTIONS & TOOLS section at the top of the panel.

The Transform panel (open it from the Transform icon in the activity bar on the left) runs XSLT transformations. XPath, XQuery and JSONPath queries against the open document live in the Query Console - the panel shows a short hint with an Open Query Console button for them. The panel header reads TRANSFORM; the run options and tools are in the OPTIONS & TOOLS section (see OPTIONS & TOOLS below). Each section header is clickable to collapse or expand that section.

Tip

For a quick transform without opening this panel, right-click XML files in the Explorer and choose Transform with …. It shares the same recent-stylesheet list and shows its result in the same OUTPUT panel.

docs.title: SCENARIO
docs.text: Shown only while a project is open: pick one of the project's saved transformation scenarios to fill stylesheet, input, parameters and output method in one step, run it with Run Scenario (writes its output file), save the current settings as a scenario (disk button) or remove one (trash button). For a scenario with an expected result, Check compares the run's result with it; after a failed check, Differences opens both in the Compare view and Accept makes the current result the expected one. See Projects and Transformation Scenarios and Regression checks.

docs.title: STYLESHEET
docs.text:
• Shows the name of the chosen XSLT stylesheet on its own line below the icon, the favorites/browse controls and Change (long names are shortened in the middle; hover for the full path). While no stylesheet is set, the row reads "No stylesheet — choose or drop a file" - clicking it works like Change.
  • Change - pick an .xsl / .xslt file from disk (it is also loaded into the editor).
  • The clock icon opens the recent stylesheets menu: reapply a recently used stylesheet in a single click (it is also loaded into the editor), or choose Clear recent to empty the list.
  • The star icon opens your XSLT favorites - see Browsing favorites with ◀ / ▶ below. A picked stylesheet is also loaded into the editor.
  • Drag & drop: drop an .xsl / .xslt file from your file manager straight onto the STYLESHEET row - it becomes the current stylesheet and is loaded into the editor, exactly as if you had picked it from a favorite. While dragging, the row glows green when the file can be loaded and red when it has the wrong extension (a red drop is rejected). As with favorites, the transform runs automatically as soon as both a stylesheet and an input are ready (while Run automatically is checked).

docs.title: INPUT
docs.text:
The INPUT section shows which document the transform will use as its input (the name on its own line, the full path as tooltip; "No input — open a document or drop a file" while there is none):

  • By default the input follows the active editor document: switch to another tab and the next run transforms that document (the shown input name updates live).
  • Change opens a small menu with two options:
    • Select XML file… - transform a fixed XML file from disk instead, regardless of which editor tab is active.
    • Use active editor - go back to following the active tab.
  • The star icon opens your XML favorites - see Browsing favorites with ◀ / ▶ below. A picked input is also opened in the editor and becomes the active tab.
  • Drag & drop: drop an .xml file from your file manager straight onto the INPUT row to transform that file - exactly like picking a favorite: it becomes the input and opens as the active editor tab. The same green (loadable) / red (rejected) drag-over feedback applies, and the transform runs automatically as soon as both a stylesheet and an input are ready (while Run automatically is checked).

docs.title: Browsing favorites with ◀ / ▶
docs.text:
Pick stylesheets and input files straight from your Favorites and page through them, so you can run the same stylesheet over many files, or many stylesheets over one file, without ever opening a file chooser.

Both the STYLESHEET and the INPUT rows carry a star icon, a pair of ◀ / ▶ navigation buttons, and a small "i / n" position label. The ◀ / ▶ buttons and the label only appear once the browse list holds at least two entries.

  • The star menu lists the favorites of the matching type - XSLT favorites for STYLESHEET, XML favorites for INPUT - grouped by their folder (category). An "All … favorites" entry at the top selects the whole list at once.
  • Picking a favorite (or an "All"/folder entry) does three things: it sets the current file, it builds a browse list from that selection, and it loads the file into the editor. An input comes to the front as the active tab. A stylesheet opens behind the active tab while the input follows the active document (otherwise the stylesheet would become its own input); with a fixed input file it comes to the front too. The same happens on every ◀ / ▶ step.
  • The ◀ / ▶ buttons then step backward and forward through that browse list. Browsing is cyclic: pressing ▶ on the last entry wraps to the first, and ◀ on the first wraps to the last. The "i / n" label shows your position (for example, 3 / 12).
  • Each ◀ / ▶ step runs the transformation automatically (while Run automatically is checked) - but only once both sides are ready: a stylesheet is selected and an input is available (either a chosen input file or the active editor document). Until both are present, stepping just loads the file without transforming.

This supports two common workflows:

  1. Fix the input, step through stylesheets. Keep one XML file as input, then page through several data-quality or reporting stylesheets with ▶ to see each result in turn.
  2. Fix the stylesheet, step through inputs. Choose one XSLT stylesheet, then page through many XML input files with ▶ to apply the same transformation to each.

The existing Change file chooser, the clock (recent stylesheets) menu, and Use active editor all keep working exactly as before.

docs.title: OUTPUT METHOD
docs.text: A single dropdown with Auto, XML, HTML, XHTML, Text, JSON. Auto (the default) detects the output format from the stylesheet's xsl:output declaration; pick a concrete format to override the detection.

docs.title: PARAMETERS
docs.text:
Define XSLT parameters as name = value rows:

  • Add parameter adds a new row.
  • Each row has its own remove button.
  • The values are passed to the stylesheet on every run.

docs.title: Running a Transformation
docs.text:
1. Choose a stylesheet (STYLESHEET → Change, or pick one from the recent menu).
  2. Check the INPUT section shows the document you want to transform.
  3. Click Run Transform.

The Run automatically checkbox next to Run Transform (on by default) controls the automatic run that starts when you drop a stylesheet or input, pick one from your favorites, or browse with ◀ / ▶. Uncheck it to only set the file and run with Run Transform yourself.

The result appears in the OUTPUT panel below the editor - see The OUTPUT Panel below.

docs.title: Debugging a Stylesheet
docs.text:
Debug (next to Run Transform) runs the same stylesheet over the same input as Run Transform (the INPUT file when one is set by dropping, a favorite or ◀ / ▶ browsing, otherwise the active document) in the interactive XSLT debugger. The other ways in are Tools → Debug with XSLT…, the Transform ▾ → Debug with XSLT… toolbar entry, Run ▾ → Debug Transform for an active XSLT document (against the toolbar's Input target), the PDF / FOP panel's Debug stylesheet…, and Shift+F5 whenever a document is open.

What happens:

  1. The stylesheet opens as a document. The debugger runs its editor text - unsaved changes included, also of open included modules - under the file's location, so relative xsl:include / xsl:import hrefs resolve (a new stylesheet must be saved once). Every saved XSLT document already has a breakpoint gutter: click the slot left of a line to toggle a red breakpoint, before or during a session (the click does not move the caret). Breakpoints are remembered per file across sessions and restarts, including those set in included modules.
  2. The DEBUG dock opens below the editor, so the stylesheet stays visible while you step. The dock shares its space with OUTPUT; a small OUTPUT | DEBUG strip switches between them, and a result that arrives while DEBUG is in front marks the OUTPUT toggle.
  3. The run starts and pauses at the first instruction when there are no breakpoints (Pause on entry, a toggle in the dock's header), otherwise at the first breakpoint. The paused line is tinted in the editor and marked with a green arrow in the gutter (a yellow arrow on a breakpoint line). When Saxon pauses inside an included module, that file opens, with its own breakpoints in its gutter.

The dock's header holds the controls - Continue (F5), Pause (F6, breaks into a running transformation), Run to Cursor (Ctrl+F10; also gutter right-click → Run to Here, and it starts the debugger when none runs), Step Into (F7), Step Over (F8), Step Out (Shift+F8), Restart (runs again from the start with the same breakpoints, reading the stylesheet again from the editor), Stop, Pause on entry, Mute (all breakpoints off, steps still work), Show in editor, Show input (the paused context node in the input XML, which is tinted blue there), Evaluate (Alt+F8: any XPath in the selected frame, with a history on Up/Down) and ✕ (ends the session). Below it, two tab groups show the paused state - Variables | Watch on the left, Call Stack | Messages | Breakpoints | Output on the right, with a draggable divider whose position is remembered. Messages and Breakpoints carry a count badge; a failed run brings Messages to the front. The panels:

Panel Shows Variables The context item (.), position() / last(), the XSLT context (mode, current-group() / current-grouping-key(), regex-group(n), tunnel parameters, accumulator values), every local variable in scope and every global variable that has been evaluated so far - with real values and XDM types, as a tree: nodes unfold into attributes and children, sequences, maps and arrays into their items; each row's XPath can be watched. While paused, the stylesheet also shows each variable's value at the end of its declaration line (details), and resting the mouse on a $variable (or a selected XPath) shows its value in a popup. Click a value to open it in a window with the full, highlighted value, Copy, and an XPath field that runs against it (details) Watch Your XPath expressions, evaluated against the paused context item with the variables in scope (count(item), $total, position()); re-evaluated at every pause. Add / Remove sit above the table (or Variables → right-click → Add to Watches); Delete removes, F2 / double-click edits an expression; click a value to open the full result. Watches are saved per stylesheet Call Stack Template and function frames (instructions nested inside them are dimmed), each with its module and line; loops show their current item, e.g. ForEach (3 of 222); double-click jumps there, also into an include. Selecting a frame switches Variables and Watch to that frame (its context item, own locals and the globals). Enter / Open Value… opens the frame's context item, with XPath over that frame's own variables Messages xsl:message output and Saxon warnings as they happen, with their stylesheet location; double-click jumps to the line. Filter by level and text, Copy, Clear Breakpoints All breakpoints of the session, grouped by file (checkbox = enabled · file · line · condition · hit rule · hits of this run; after a completed run, breakpoints it never reached are flagged and drawn amber in the gutter) with Remove / Edit… / Template… (break whenever a template rule, named template, function or mode is entered, at any line) / Clear all / Break on ▾ (dynamic errors - pausing at the failing instruction with its variables -, terminating or all xsl:message) above the list (Delete removes the selected one); double-click jumps to the line; right-click an entry for per-file Enable / Disable / Remove and Export / Import Breakpoints…. Right-click a gutter slot for a conditional breakpoint (XPath, pauses only when true), a logpoint (writes item {@id}-style messages to Messages, optionally without pausing) or a hit count rule (exactly / from / every N-th hit) - details Output The output written so far, refreshed at every pause; the complete result once the run finishes. Secondary results (xsl:result-document, kept in memory) are selectable; Documents lists and opens what doc() / document() / collection() loaded

When the run ends, the status reads Finished · N ms and the result lands in the OUTPUT panel (the OUTPUT toggle lights up; DEBUG stays in front so the messages remain readable). A failed run shows the error with its location in Messages. The debugger runs on its own Saxon processor, so a normal Run Transform during a paused session is unaffected. Tools → Debug Configuration… saves per stylesheet the input (Run target or a file), parameters, output format and pause on entry; Re-run Last Debug (Ctrl+Shift+F5) repeats the last debug run with its input read again. Details and stylesheet tips: XSLT Developer → Interactive Live Debugger.

docs.title: Queries (XPath, XQuery, JSONPath)
docs.text: The Transform panel no longer has its own XPATH and XQUERY sections. Below the run controls, a short hint and an Open Query Console button take you to the Query Console, which runs XPath, XQuery and JSONPath queries against the open document and offers the saved queries (Snippets menu) and the XQuery Examples.

docs.title: OPTIONS & TOOLS
docs.text:
The collapsible OPTIONS & TOOLS section at the top of the panel (open by default - click its header to collapse it) holds everything secondary. First the run options, as checkboxes:

Option What it does Live preview Re-runs the transform automatically (debounced) while you edit the input document. Watch stylesheet file Re-runs the transform whenever the chosen stylesheet changes on disk - handy while editing the stylesheet in another tool. Profile run The transform runs under the XSLT profiler and opens a Profile tab: hot spots by self time, call tree, flame graph and time per line (see XSLT Developer → Performance and Profiling). Trace run A transform also opens a Trace tool tab (template matches + xsl:message output). Auto-open result tab Additionally opens every successful result as a regular editor tab (HTML/XHTML results open rendered in the Preview view). Off by default.

Below the options, the advanced tools are labelled rows (icon + name):

Row What it does Debug XSLT… Same as the Debug button next to Run Transform: opens the stylesheet (with the breakpoints set in its gutter) and the DEBUG dock below the editor - see Debugging a Stylesheet. Batch Transform… Runs the chosen stylesheet - or, when no stylesheet is set, the active XQuery document - over many XML files, with per-file results and "Save All". Execution Statistics Opens the Execution Statistics tool tab (duration, CPU and memory per XSLT/XQuery/validation run). Runs are only recorded while Record execution statistics is enabled in the Settings page's DEVELOPER card.

XSLT version selection (1.0/2.0/3.0) is intentionally not offered: Saxon HE auto-detects the version from the stylesheet's version attribute, so an explicit selector would be cosmetic.

docs.title: The OUTPUT Panel (Results)
docs.text:
Transform and query results appear in an OUTPUT panel docked below the editor instead of opening editor tabs and a separate HTML-preview tool tab.

All Transform-panel results - XSLT transforms, XPath/JSONPath queries, and XQuery runs - appear in an OUTPUT panel that docks below the editor: the source document stays on top and the result shows underneath, while the Properties inspector keeps its full height. The panel persists across activity switches, so the last result stays visible while you work elsewhere.

The OUTPUT panel header shows:

  • A format badge (XML, HTML, …) for the result.
  • A status: a green check with Transformed · N ms · M chars on success (how long the run took and how large the output is), or a red error icon with the error message on failure.
  • View toggles - Preview | Text | Table:
    • Text - the result in a read-only code editor (the default): line numbers, syntax highlighting matching the result format (XML or JSON; plain text otherwise), and font zoom with Ctrl+mouse wheel (Ctrl+0 resets). A very large result (over 2 million characters) shows only its start with a note; Open as Tab, Browser and Save… use the whole result.
    • Preview - the result rendered as a web page; available for HTML/XHTML results only.
    • Table - available for XQuery results that return a sequence of items (auto-selected when applicable). Each item becomes a row, and the columns are taken from each item's child elements (or, if an item has no child elements, its attributes). A sequence of plain values is shown in a single value column.
  • Actions:
    • Open as Tab (Open result as editor tab) - opens the result as a regular document (Transform-Result.xml / .html / .json / .txt) that you can edit and save. An HTML/XHTML result opens as an HTML document rendered in the Preview view (switch to Text to see the markup); re-running the transform updates the open result tab, re-rendering the preview if it is showing. An XML result gets a schema for validation and IntelliSense like an opened file: the xsi:schemaLocation / xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation it declares (a relative location resolves against the input's folder), else a Schema Library entry, else the schema of the transform's input - if that schema declares the result's root element (e.g. a stylesheet that only adds or removes annotations).
    • Browser (Open in browser) - opens the result (typically HTML) in your system web browser.
    • Save… (Save result…) - writes the result straight to a file.
    • ✕ - hides the OUTPUT panel; it reappears automatically on the next run.

Note

In earlier versions, every transform opened a Transform-Result.* editor tab, and HTML output additionally opened an "HTML Preview" tool tab. Both were replaced by the OUTPUT panel: an editor tab now opens only via the panel's Open result as editor tab action or the Auto-open result tab option in OPTIONS & TOOLS, and HTML is rendered inline via the panel's Preview view.

docs.title: Unified Shell
docs.text: The application opens directly into the Unified Shell - one workspace that combines XML, XSD, XSLT, XProc, Schematron and JSON editing with all the validation, transformation, signing and documentation tools. The separate legacy tabs have been consolidated here.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Unified Shell is the single workspace for everything FreeXmlToolkit does. Instead of switching between separate editor pages, you open files as tabs in the central editor host and reach every tool through the activity bar on the left. You can work with an XML file next to its XSD schema, XSLT stylesheets and Schematron rules at the same time.

The Unified Shell: activity bar (left), Explorer side panel, editor host with an XML file (Text/Tree/Graphic view toggle), the Properties inspector (right) and the status bar.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Area Purpose Activity bar (far left) Switch tools / side panels: Explorer, Search, Favorites, Validation, Transform, Schema, Schema Library (its label wraps onto two lines), PDF/FOP, Sign & Encrypt, Settings - plus a FundsXML activity when the optional FundsXML extension is enabled (see FundsXML Panel). Always visible - it cannot be collapsed. (Settings, Schema Library and Sign & Encrypt open as a full page in the editor area - see Settings Page, Schema Library Page and Sign & Encrypt Page. Help is not an activity - it is the Help menu, see Help Menu & About.) Menu bar (very top) File / Edit / View / Tools / Help - every action of the toolbar, the Activity Bar and the keyboard shortcuts in one place (see Menu Bar). On macOS it is the system menu bar at the top of the screen. Header bar (top) The breadcrumb (application / active file), a centered search pill ("Run XPath / XQuery…", shortcut Ctrl+K) that opens the bottom Query Console when clicked, the star button (Favorites quick access - every favorite, from any activity or page), the ? button (opens the Help menu as a popup - same as F1) and the Theme button. Side panel The panel for the selected activity (e.g. the Transform panel, the Validation panel). Resizable and collapsible (see Resizing and collapsing the side panels). Editor host (center) Tabs of open documents, each with the Text, Tree and Graphic view modes - plus a rendered Preview for HTML documents (see View Modes). Inspector (right) View and edit the selected node's properties from any view. Resizable and collapsible (see Resizing and collapsing the side panels). Hidden automatically while a page without a document (Settings, Schema Library, Signature, reports, tool tabs) is selected. Status bar (bottom) Caret position (Ln/Col), character count, file type, the XSD / IntelliSense indicator, the encoding label (the charset the file was read in and is saved in, e.g. UTF-8 or ISO-8859-1), the last recorded run (Developer feature), a memory indicator and the active file's path (see Status Bar).

docs.title: Resizing and collapsing the side panels
docs.text:
Both the left side panel and the right Properties inspector can be resized and collapsed to give the editor more room - the activity bar always stays visible.

Resizing - the panels are not fixed-width:

  • Drag the thin divider line between a panel and the editor to make the panel wider or narrower (the mouse pointer turns into a horizontal resize arrow over the divider). Widen the panel when file names, validation messages, or property values get truncated.
  • Each panel keeps a minimum width of 200 px, and the editor in the middle always keeps at least 320 px - you cannot drag a panel so far that the editor disappears.
  • The chosen widths are remembered across restarts (per user).
  • When you resize the window, the panels keep their pixel width - only the editor column grows or shrinks (the same behavior as VS Code).

Collapsing - each panel can also be hidden completely:

  • Collapse / re-open: click the matching toggle button in the editor toolbar (left-most toggle, a sidebar icon, for the side panel; right-most toggle, a mirrored sidebar icon, for the inspector) - the same mechanism on both sides. Selecting any activity from the activity bar also re-opens the left side panel. A re-opened panel comes back at its last dragged width. The toolbar toggles (or Ctrl+L / Ctrl+Shift+P) are the only way to collapse a panel - there is no collapse button on the panels themselves.
  • Collapsing one panel leaves the other alone: hiding the side panel does not resize the Properties inspector (and the other way round) - only the editor gets the freed space.
  • The collapsed/expanded state is remembered across restarts and can also be changed under Settings → Appearance → LAYOUT ("Show left side panel" / "Show Properties (inspector) panel").
  • The inspector only appears next to documents. When you switch to a tab that is not a document - Settings, Schema Library, Sign & Encrypt, a report or another tool tab - the inspector hides automatically, so the page gets the full width. Its toggle button is greyed out on such tabs. As soon as you select a document tab again, the inspector comes back. Your own show/hide choice is not changed by this - if you had hidden the inspector, it stays hidden.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Multi-tab editing - Open multiple files of different types in one view
  • Automatic file type detection - Files are recognized by extension (.xml/.wsdl, .xsd, .xsl/.xslt, .xpl/.xproc, .xq/.xquery/.xqm/.xqy, .xpath, .sch/.schematron, .json/.jsonc/.json5, .html/.htm/.xhtml); anything else opens as plain text
  • View modes per document - Text, Tree and Graphic, all over one shared model, plus a rendered Preview for HTML documents (see View Modes)
  • Inspector editing everywhere - edit node properties from the Text, Tree and Graphic views, not just one
  • Type picker with explanations - the inspector's Type field and Change Type… in the diagram and tree context menus list the schema's own types and every XSD built-in datatype, and a side pane explains the highlighted one (see Choosing a type)
  • Integrated XPath/XQuery - a bottom Query Console queries the active XML/JSON file right from the editor (Ctrl+Shift+X)
  • Editor toolbar actions - run Validate, Transform, Run, Generate Documentation and the Type Editor for the active document without switching activities
  • Search & Replace - Ctrl+F / Ctrl+H across the editor, in every view mode: the Text view searches the raw text, the Tree and Graphic views search the nodes themselves (names, documentation, attributes, enumeration and facet values, comments)
  • Find in Files & XPath search - the Search activity (Ctrl+Shift+F) searches and replaces across all files of a folder, by plain text or by XPath expression (see Search Panel)
  • Resizable side panels - drag the divider lines to give the side panel or the Properties inspector more room; the widths are remembered across restarts (see Resizing and collapsing the side panels)
  • Favorites - Quick access to frequently used files

docs.title: Colours: workflows and actions
docs.text:
