An XSLT stylesheet open in the editor, the Transform panel on the left with the stylesheet and input selected, and the transformation result in the OUTPUT panel below the editor

XSLT/XQuery development in the Unified Shell provides:

  • Full code editors for XML, XSLT, and XQuery — every file opens as a normal editor tab
  • Live preview and watch modes for instant feedback while you edit
  • XSLT Parameters for reusable stylesheets
  • Multi-file batch processing for XSLT and XQuery
  • Performance metrics, profiling, and tracing
  • An interactive debugger with breakpoints, stepping, and variable inspection
  • Favorites integration for quick access to stylesheets and input files

docs.title: Where Everything Lives
docs.text: Capability Where to find it Edit the stylesheet / query Open the .xsl / .xq file — it is a normal editor tab with syntax highlighting Choose stylesheet & input The Transform panel (activity bar → Transform): STYLESHEET and INPUT rows, each with a Change link, a star (favorites) menu, and ◀ / ▶ browse buttons Run a transformation The panel's Run Transform button (with Run automatically checked, dropping or browsing a stylesheet/input runs it right away) — or, with the XSLT file active, the toolbar's Run button (Ctrl+Enter / F5). From an XML document, the toolbar's Transform with XSLT… opens the Transform panel and runs it there See the result The OUTPUT panel docked below the editor (Text / Preview / Table views, open-in-browser, save) Parameters, output method The Transform panel's PARAMETERS and OUTPUT METHOD sections XPath / XQuery queries The bottom Query Console (Ctrl+Shift+X, or the Transform panel's Open Query Console button) Debugger The Debug button next to Run Transform (also Tools → Debug with XSLT…, Shift+F5) - see Interactive Live Debugger Batch, profile, trace The Transform panel's OPTIONS & TOOLS section (at the top of the panel, open by default; it lists Debug XSLT… again)

docs.title: Step 1: Choose Your Files
docs.text:
1. Open the Transform panel from the Transform icon in the activity bar.
  2. In the STYLESHEET section, click Change to pick an .xsl / .xslt file — or pick one from the clock (recent) or star (favorites) menu, or drop a stylesheet file onto the row.
  3. Check the INPUT section: by default it follows the active editor document, so simply open the XML you want to transform. Change → Select XML file… fixes the input to a file from disk instead.

docs.title: Step 2: Transform
docs.text: Click Run Transform. (With the stylesheet itself as the active document, the toolbar's Run button or Ctrl+Enter runs it against the document selected in the Input dropdown.)

docs.title: Step 3: View Results
docs.text: The output appears in the OUTPUT panel docked below the editor. The header shows a format badge and the run status (Transformed · N ms · M chars). For HTML output, switch the panel to the Preview view to see the rendered page, or click Open in browser.

docs.title: Live Preview and Watch Mode
docs.text:
Two checkboxes in the Transform panel's OPTIONS & TOOLS section re-run the transformation automatically:

  • Live preview — re-runs (debounced) whenever you edit the input document.
  • Watch stylesheet file — re-runs whenever the chosen stylesheet changes on disk, which is handy while editing the stylesheet in another tab or tool.

This is ideal for developing and debugging stylesheets: make a change, and the OUTPUT panel updates by itself.

docs.title: Using XSLT Parameters
docs.text: XSLT stylesheets can accept parameters to make them more flexible. The PARAMETERS section of the Transform panel lets you define these values.

docs.title: Defining Parameters in XSLT
docs.text:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="1.0"
                xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">

  <!-- Define a parameter with a default value -->
  <xsl:param name="title" select="'Default Title'"/>
  <xsl:param name="show-prices" select="true()"/>
  <xsl:param name="currency" select="'EUR'"/>

  <xsl:template match="/">
    <html>
      <head><title><xsl:value-of select="$title"/></title></head>
      <body>
        <h1><xsl:value-of select="$title"/></h1>
        <xsl:if test="$show-prices">
          <!-- Show prices in the specified currency -->
        </xsl:if>
      </body>
    </html>
  </xsl:template>

</xsl:stylesheet>

docs.title: Setting Parameter Values
docs.text:
1. Expand the PARAMETERS section in the Transform panel
  2. Click Add parameter to create a new row
  3. Enter the parameter name (e.g., title)
  4. Enter the value (e.g., My Custom Report)

Each row has its own remove button, and the values are passed to the stylesheet on every run.

docs.title: XQuery Development
docs.text:
XQuery is powerful for querying and transforming XML data. There are two ways to work with it:

  • XQuery documents — open (or create) a .xq / .xquery file; it gets its own editor with highlighting and autocomplete. Press the toolbar's Run button (Ctrl+Enter) to run it against the selected Input; the result appears in the OUTPUT panel.
  • The Query Console — switch it to XQuery mode and run a query against the active document.

docs.title: Basic XQuery Example
docs.text:
for $book in /books/book
where $book/price > 30
order by $book/title
return <result>{$book/title}</result>

docs.title: Built-in XQuery Examples
docs.text:
The Query Console's Examples menu inserts sample queries:

Example Description Simple Basic element selection FLWOR For-Let-Where-Order-Return HTML report Generate HTML output Data-quality check Validate data completeness

Tip

The installation ships 17 ready-to-run XQuery scripts in examples/xquery/ and 32 XPath expressions in examples/xpath/ — open any of them and press Ctrl+Enter. See Bundled Example Collections.

docs.title: Multi-File Batch Processing
docs.text:
Batch Transform… (Transform panel, OPTIONS & TOOLS section) runs the chosen stylesheet over many XML files at once - or, when no stylesheet is set, the active XQuery document.

  1. Open the stylesheet (or XQuery file) you want to apply, then pick OPTIONS & TOOLS → Batch Transform… — a Batch tool tab opens.
  2. Add the XML files to process (each file is transformed/queried independently).
  3. Run the batch: the table shows one row per file with its status, and selecting a row shows that file's RESULT.
  4. Save All… writes every result to a folder you choose.

The Explorer offers an even faster route: select several XML files in the workspace tree (Ctrl/Shift+click), right-click and choose Transform with <stylesheet> — the Batch tool tab opens pre-loaded with those files and starts automatically.

docs.title: XSLT 3.0 Examples
docs.text: FreeXmlToolkit supports XSLT 3.0 via Saxon HE. Here are some advanced patterns:

docs.title: For-Each-Group (XSLT 2.0/3.0)
docs.text:
Group items without the Muenchian method:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="3.0"
                xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">

  <xsl:output method="html" indent="yes"/>

  <xsl:template match="/">
    <html>
      <body>
        <h1>Books by Author</h1>
        <xsl:for-each-group select="books/book" group-by="author">
          <xsl:sort select="current-grouping-key()"/>
          <h2><xsl:value-of select="current-grouping-key()"/></h2>
          <ul>
            <xsl:for-each select="current-group()">
              <li><xsl:value-of select="title"/></li>
            </xsl:for-each>
          </ul>
        </xsl:for-each-group>
      </body>
    </html>
  </xsl:template>

</xsl:stylesheet>

docs.title: Using Maps and Arrays (XSLT 3.0)
docs.text:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="3.0"
                xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform"
                xmlns:map="http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-functions/map">

  <xsl:output method="text"/>

  <xsl:variable name="config" select="map {
    'title': 'Report',
    'format': 'detailed',
    'max-items': 100
  }"/>

  <xsl:template match="/">
    <xsl:text>Title: </xsl:text>
    <xsl:value-of select="map:get($config, 'title')"/>
  </xsl:template>

</xsl:stylesheet>

docs.title: JSON Output (XSLT 3.0)
docs.text:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="3.0"
                xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">

  <xsl:output method="json" indent="yes"/>

  <xsl:template match="/">
    <xsl:map>
      <xsl:map-entry key="'books'">
        <xsl:array>
          <xsl:for-each select="books/book">
            <xsl:map>
              <xsl:map-entry key="'title'" select="string(title)"/>
              <xsl:map-entry key="'author'" select="string(author)"/>
              <xsl:map-entry key="'price'" select="number(price)"/>
            </xsl:map>
          </xsl:for-each>
        </xsl:array>
      </xsl:map-entry>
    </xsl:map>
  </xsl:template>

</xsl:stylesheet>

docs.title: Text Value Templates (XSLT 3.0)
docs.text:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="3.0"
                xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform"
                expand-text="yes">

  <xsl:output method="html" indent="yes"/>

  <xsl:template match="/">
    <html>
      <body>
        <xsl:for-each select="books/book">
          <p>{title} by {author} - ${price}</p>
        </xsl:for-each>
      </body>
    </html>
  </xsl:template>

</xsl:stylesheet>

docs.title: Performance and Profiling
docs.text:
Every run shows compact statistics in the OUTPUT panel's status line: Transformed · N ms · M chars — the execution time and the output size.

For a deeper look, enable Profile run in the Transform panel's OPTIONS & TOOLS section: the next transformation runs under the XSLT profiler and opens a Profile: tab that shows where the time goes.

Tab Shows Hot Spots Every template rule (with its mode), named template and function: calls, Self time and its share of the run, Total time, average per call. Sorted by self time: the top rows are what to optimize. Call Tree Who called whom: the whole run at the top, below it the templates and functions each one called, with calls, total time and its share, and self time. The slowest path is expanded. Flame Graph The call tree as bars; the width is the total time. Click a bar to zoom in (it fills the width), click it again or Reset Zoom to go back; hover for the numbers. Right-click to export it as PNG, SVG or PDF or to copy it as an image (Exporting a Graphical View). Lines Self time per stylesheet line, with the line's text: the expressions and instructions that cost the most.

Total is the time from entering a template or function until leaving it, including everything it calls; a recursive function counts only its outermost calls, so no time is counted twice (in the call tree its recursive calls are folded into one node). Self is the total without the templates and functions it calls. Double-click a row or bar to open the stylesheet (also an included or imported module) at that line.

The run is measured with Saxon's tracing on, so the absolute times are higher than in a normal transformation; compare the parts with each other. The first run of a stylesheet also includes the warm-up of Java's JIT compiler: Profile Again measures once more after a warm-up run, which gives steadier numbers. Export writes the profile as JSON (with the call tree) or as a text report.

docs.title: Profiling an XQuery
docs.text:
An XQuery is profiled the same way: open the .xq file and choose Run ▾ → Profile Query. The query runs against the selected Input (or without a context item when none is chosen), its result goes to the OUTPUT panel, and a Profile: tab opens with the same four views. The components are the query's user functions (declare function); the time outside them belongs to the root of the call tree, (query body). Saxon may move an expression that does not depend on a loop out of it, so a function called in a loop can show fewer calls than iterations.

On the command line, fxt-cli transform --profile report.json … profiles a stylesheet or a query run (see Command Line).

docs.title: Testing with XSpec
docs.text:
XSpec tests are part of FreeXmlToolkit (XSpec 4, bundled): unit tests for XSLT stylesheets, XQuery modules and Schematron, written as .xspec files.

<x:description xmlns:x="http://www.jenitennison.com/xslt/xspec" xmlns:f="urn:f" stylesheet="price.xsl">
  <x:scenario label="net price of 120">
    <x:call function="f:net"><x:param select="120"/></x:call>
    <x:expect label="is 100" select="100"/>
  </x:scenario>
  <x:scenario label="item template">
    <x:context><item name="pen"/></x:context>
    <x:expect label="upper-case line"><line>PEN</line></x:expect>
  </x:scenario>
</x:description>

To start one, choose File → New…, type XML, and one of the templates XSpec test (XSLT), XSpec test (XQuery) or XSpec test (Schematron); the file is saved as .xspec. Open the .xspec file and choose Tools → Run XSpec Tests. The tests run with the text in the editor (also unsaved changes); the file must be saved once, because the stylesheet, query or Schematron it names is found relative to it. What is tested follows the description: stylesheet="…" an XSLT stylesheet, query="…" with query-at="…" an XQuery module, schematron="…" a Schematron (with x:expect-assert, x:expect-report, x:expect-valid).

The XSpec tab shows the summary (passed, failed, pending) and every scenario with its tests; scenarios with a failed test are expanded and the first failure is selected. Expected and Actual below show what the test expected and what the code returned. Run Again runs the tests again (after you changed the stylesheet or the tests), HTML Report opens XSpec's own report as a preview, Export JUnit… writes a JUnit XML report for CI servers. Scenarios marked pending="…" are listed but not run.

On the command line: fxt-cli xspec tests/price.xspec -r junit.xml (see Command Line).

Ready-to-run examples are in the examples/xspec/ folder of the installation: tests for an XSLT stylesheet (functions and template rules), an XQuery library module and a Schematron, plus 05-failing-demo.xspec, which fails on purpose so you can see Expected and Actual.

docs.title: Tracing and Messages
docs.text:
Enable Trace run in OPTIONS & TOOLS to open a Trace tool tab with the next run. It shows the sequence of template matches and all xsl:message output:

<xsl:message>Processing book: <xsl:value-of select="title"/></xsl:message>

docs.title: Tips for Debugging
docs.text:
1. Use <xsl:message> to output debug information and read it in the Trace tab
  2. Enable Trace run to see which templates actually fire, and in what order
  3. For stepping through the stylesheet interactively, use the debugger (below)

docs.title: Interactive Live Debugger
docs.text: Debug in the Transform panel, Tools → Debug with XSLT… or Shift+F5 start the interactive debugger for XSLT, XQuery and Schematron: breakpoints, stepping, variables, watches, call stack and coverage - see the Debugger page.

docs.title: Output Format
docs.text:
The Transform panel's OUTPUT METHOD section is a single dropdown with Auto, XML, HTML, XHTML, Text, JSON. Auto (the default) detects the format from the stylesheet's xsl:output declaration; pick a concrete format to override the detection.

XSLT version selection (1.0/2.0/3.0) is intentionally not offered: Saxon HE auto-detects the version from the stylesheet's version attribute.

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text:
The complete list is on the Keyboard Shortcuts page (and in the app under Help → Keyboard Shortcuts).

For stylesheet and query work:

Shortcut Action Ctrl+Enter / F5 Run the active XSLT / XQuery / XPath / XProc document against the selected Input Shift+F5 Debug the active XSLT / XQuery / Schematron document (or the Transform / PDF panel's stylesheet) F9 Toggle a breakpoint on the caret line F5 / F7 / F8 / Shift+F8 While paused: Continue / Step Into / Step Over / Step Out - see Debugger Ctrl+Shift+X Toggle the Query Console

docs.title: Data Extraction
docs.text:
(: Extract all customer emails :)
for $customer in /customers/customer
return <email>{$customer/email/text()}</email>

docs.title: Transformation
docs.text:
(: Transform to HTML table :)
<table>
  <tr><th>Name</th><th>Email</th></tr>
  {
    for $c in /customers/customer
    return <tr>
      <td>{$c/name/text()}</td>
      <td>{$c/email/text()}</td>
    </tr>
  }
</table>

docs.title: Aggregation
docs.text:
(: Calculate statistics :)
let $orders := /orders/order
return <stats>
  <count>{count($orders)}</count>
  <total>{sum($orders/amount)}</total>
  <average>{avg($orders/amount)}</average>
  <min>{min($orders/amount)}</min>
  <max>{max($orders/amount)}</max>
</stats>

docs.title: Conditional Logic
docs.text:
(: Categorize items :)
for $item in /items/item
return <categorized>
  <name>{$item/name/text()}</name>
  <category>{
    if ($item/price > 100) then "Premium"
    else if ($item/price > 50) then "Standard"
    else "Budget"
  }</category>
</categorized>

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Start with Live preview off for large files to avoid slow updates
  • Use the Examples menu to insert working XQuery templates
  • Enable Profile run if transformations are slow — the per-template timings show where
  • Star your stylesheets as favorites, then page through them with the STYLESHEET row's ◀ / ▶ buttons
  • Use Batch Transform for processing multiple files efficiently
  • Enable Trace run when troubleshooting complex stylesheets
  • Only process trusted stylesheets - see Security Features for details on XSLT extension security

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution No output Check the STYLESHEET row shows a stylesheet and the INPUT row shows the XML you expect Syntax error Read the red error status in the OUTPUT panel header Slow transformation Enable Profile run (OPTIONS & TOOLS) and check the per-template timings Batch results empty Ensure files were added to the Batch tab and the run has finished Parameters not working Verify parameter names match exactly Java extension function not found Java extensions are disabled by default for security. See Security Features

docs.title: XSLT Viewer
docs.text:
Note: The standalone XSLT Viewer tab has been retired. Quick XSLT transformations now live in the Unified Shell's Transform panel (set a stylesheet, transform, preview the result, open in browser). Parameters, live preview, debugging, profiling, and batch processing sit in the same panel - the XSLT Developer page covers those advanced tools.

This page shows how to quickly transform XML documents using XSLT stylesheets. Simply select your files and view the results immediately.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Transform panel is designed for quick transformations where you want to see results immediately. Open it in the Unified Shell from the Transform icon in the activity bar. For advanced features like the debugger, profiling, and batch processing, see the XSLT Developer guide.

Quick XSLT/XQuery transformations now live in the Unified Shell's Transform panel

docs.title: What is XSLT?
docs.text:
XSLT (Extensible Stylesheet Language Transformations) is a language for transforming XML documents. Think of it like a recipe that tells the computer how to convert your XML data into a different format such as HTML, text, or another XML structure.

XML input + XSLT rules = Output: the examples/xslt/FundsXML_Factsheet.xslt stylesheet rendered as HTML in the OUTPUT panel below the editor

Common uses:

  • Convert XML data to HTML for web display
  • Transform XML between different schemas
  • Generate reports from XML data
  • Extract and restructure data

docs.title: Step 1: Select Your Files
docs.text:
1. Open your XML source file in the editor host so it is the active document - the panel's INPUT section follows the active tab by default (use Change → Select XML file… to transform a fixed file from disk instead, or drop an .xml file from your file manager onto the INPUT row)
  2. In the STYLESHEET section, click Change to choose an XSLT stylesheet (the clock icon offers your recently used stylesheets) - or simply drop an .xsl / .xslt file from your file manager onto the STYLESHEET row

docs.title: Step 2: Run and View the Results
docs.text:
Click Run Transform. The result appears in the OUTPUT panel that docks below the editor - the source stays on top, the result shows underneath. The panel header shows a format badge, a success/error status with timing (Transformed · N ms · M chars), and view toggles:

View Description Text The result in a read-only code editor with line numbers and syntax highlighting (the default) Preview For HTML/XHTML output: the result rendered as a web page Table For XQuery results that return a sequence: the items shown as a table

The OUTPUT METHOD defaults to Auto: the format (XML, HTML, XHTML, Text, JSON) is detected from the stylesheet's xsl:output declaration. Pick a concrete format in the dropdown to override the detection.

docs.title: Transform Panel Actions
docs.text:
Control Description Run Transform Runs the transformation with the current stylesheet and input Run automatically (Checkbox next to Run Transform, on by default) Runs as soon as a stylesheet or input is dropped, picked from favorites or browsed with ◀ / ▶ Debug (Next to Run Transform, also Shift+F5) Runs the stylesheet in the interactive debugger - breakpoints (toggle them in the saved stylesheet's gutter at any time, before or during a session; they are remembered per file), stepping, variables - in a DEBUG dock below the editor; see XSLT Developer Transform with XSLT… (Editor toolbar / Tools menu, XML documents) Opens this panel on the active document, asks for a stylesheet if none is set, and runs it Open result as editor tab (OUTPUT panel) Opens the result as an editable, savable document. HTML/XHTML results open as an HTML document rendered in the editor's read-only Preview view; re-running the transform updates the open tab Open in browser (OUTPUT panel) Opens the result in your default web browser Save result… (OUTPUT panel) Writes the result straight to a file Watch stylesheet file (OPTIONS & TOOLS checkbox) Re-runs automatically when the stylesheet changes on disk Live preview (OPTIONS & TOOLS checkbox) Re-runs automatically (debounced) while you edit the input document Auto-open result tab (OPTIONS & TOOLS checkbox) Also opens every successful result as an editor tab (off by default)

The OPTIONS & TOOLS section sits at the top of the panel and is open by default - click its header to collapse it.

docs.title: XSLT Examples
docs.text: FreeXmlToolkit includes example XSLT stylesheets in the examples/ folder. Here are some common XSLT patterns:

docs.title: Example 1: Basic XML to HTML
docs.text:
Transform a simple XML list to an HTML table:

<!-- Input XML -->
<books>
    <book>
        <title>XML for Beginners</title>
        <author>Jane Smith</author>
        <price>29.99</price>
    </book>
    <book>
        <title>Advanced XSLT</title>
        <author>John Doe</author>
        <price>49.99</price>
    </book>
</books>

<!-- XSLT Stylesheet -->
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="1.0"
                xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">

  <xsl:output method="html" indent="yes"/>

  <xsl:template match="/">
    <html>
      <head><title>Book List</title></head>
      <body>
        <h1>Available Books</h1>
        <table border="1">
          <tr>
            <th>Title</th>
            <th>Author</th>
            <th>Price</th>
          </tr>
          <xsl:for-each select="books/book">
            <tr>
              <td><xsl:value-of select="title"/></td>
              <td><xsl:value-of select="author"/></td>
              <td><xsl:value-of select="price"/></td>
            </tr>
          </xsl:for-each>
        </table>
      </body>
    </html>
  </xsl:template>

</xsl:stylesheet>

Output: An HTML page with a table listing all books.

docs.title: Example 2: Filter and Sort Data
docs.text:
Filter items based on a condition and sort the results:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="1.0"
                xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">

  <xsl:output method="xml" indent="yes"/>

  <xsl:template match="/">
    <expensive-books>
      <!-- Select books over $30, sorted by price descending -->
      <xsl:for-each select="books/book[price > 30]">
        <xsl:sort select="price" data-type="number" order="descending"/>
        <book>
          <xsl:copy-of select="title"/>
          <xsl:copy-of select="price"/>
        </book>
      </xsl:for-each>
    </expensive-books>
  </xsl:template>

</xsl:stylesheet>

docs.title: Example 3: Using Templates for Modular Code
docs.text:
Use templates to organize complex transformations:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="1.0"
                xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">

  <xsl:output method="html" indent="yes"/>

  <!-- Main template -->
  <xsl:template match="/">
    <html>
      <body>
        <xsl:apply-templates select="books/book"/>
      </body>
    </html>
  </xsl:template>

  <!-- Template for each book -->
  <xsl:template match="book">
    <div class="book">
      <h2><xsl:value-of select="title"/></h2>
      <p>By: <xsl:value-of select="author"/></p>
      <xsl:call-template name="format-price">
        <xsl:with-param name="amount" select="price"/>
      </xsl:call-template>
    </div>
  </xsl:template>

  <!-- Named template for price formatting -->
  <xsl:template name="format-price">
    <xsl:param name="amount"/>
    <p class="price">
      <xsl:text>Price: $</xsl:text>
      <xsl:value-of select="format-number($amount, '#,##0.00')"/>
    </p>
  </xsl:template>

</xsl:stylesheet>

docs.title: Example 4: XML to JSON-like Structure
docs.text:
Convert XML to a JSON-friendly text format:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="1.0"
                xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">

  <xsl:output method="text"/>

  <xsl:template match="/">
    <xsl:text>[</xsl:text>
    <xsl:for-each select="books/book">
      <xsl:if test="position() > 1">,</xsl:if>
      <xsl:text>{"title":"</xsl:text>
      <xsl:value-of select="title"/>
      <xsl:text>","author":"</xsl:text>
      <xsl:value-of select="author"/>
      <xsl:text>","price":</xsl:text>
      <xsl:value-of select="price"/>
      <xsl:text>}</xsl:text>
    </xsl:for-each>
    <xsl:text>]</xsl:text>
  </xsl:template>

</xsl:stylesheet>

docs.title: Example 5: Conditional Formatting
docs.text:
Apply different styles based on data values:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="1.0"
                xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">

  <xsl:output method="html" indent="yes"/>

  <xsl:template match="/">
    <html>
      <head>
        <style>
          .low-price { color: green; }
          .high-price { color: red; font-weight: bold; }
        </style>
      </head>
      <body>
        <xsl:for-each select="books/book">
          <p>
            <xsl:value-of select="title"/>:
            <span>
              <xsl:attribute name="class">
                <xsl:choose>
                  <xsl:when test="price < 30">low-price</xsl:when>
                  <xsl:otherwise>high-price</xsl:otherwise>
                </xsl:choose>
              </xsl:attribute>
              $<xsl:value-of select="price"/>
            </span>
          </p>
        </xsl:for-each>
      </body>
    </html>
  </xsl:template>

</xsl:stylesheet>

docs.title: Example 6: Grouping with Keys (XSLT 1.0 Muenchian Grouping)
docs.text:
Group items by a common value:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="1.0"
                xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">

  <xsl:output method="html" indent="yes"/>

  <!-- Key for grouping books by author -->
  <xsl:key name="books-by-author" match="book" use="author"/>

  <xsl:template match="/">
    <html>
      <body>
        <h1>Books by Author</h1>
        <!-- Select first book of each author group -->
        <xsl:for-each select="books/book[count(. | key('books-by-author', author)[1]) = 1]">
          <xsl:sort select="author"/>
          <h2><xsl:value-of select="author"/></h2>
          <ul>
            <!-- List all books by this author -->
            <xsl:for-each select="key('books-by-author', author)">
              <li><xsl:value-of select="title"/></li>
            </xsl:for-each>
          </ul>
        </xsl:for-each>
      </body>
    </html>
  </xsl:template>

</xsl:stylesheet>

docs.title: Included Example Files
docs.text:
FreeXmlToolkit includes example XSLT stylesheets in the examples/xslt/ folder, for example:

Stylesheet Description FundsXML_Factsheet.xslt Fund factsheet as an HTML page FundsXML_DataQualityReport_HTML.xsl Data quality report (HTML) FundsXML_CompleteDQReport_HTML.xsl Complete data-quality report (HTML) FundsXML_AssetAnalysis_HTML.xsl Asset analysis with tables (HTML) FundsXML_to_JSON.xslt Export a FundsXML document as JSON FundsXML_Positions_to_CSV.xslt Export positions as CSV Check_FundsXML_File.xslt Consistency checks with a text report

Use these with the example XML file examples/xml/FundsXML_422_Bond_Fund.xml.

The stylesheets in examples/xsl/ (FundsXML_Factsheet.xsl, FundsXML_RiskReport.xsl, …) are XSL-FO stylesheets for PDF output - use them with the PDF Generator (FOP), not with the XSLT transform.

docs.title: Performance Statistics
docs.text:
After each transformation, the OUTPUT panel's status line shows compact statistics in the form Transformed · N ms · M chars:

  • Execution time - How long the transformation took (milliseconds)
  • Output size - Size of the generated output (characters)

For detailed per-template timings, enable Profile run in the Transform panel's OPTIONS & TOOLS section - the next run also opens a read-only Profile tool tab.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Validate first - Make sure your XML and XSLT files are valid before transformation
  • Check the OUTPUT panel status - If a transformation fails, the red error status in the OUTPUT panel header shows the error message
  • Use the Preview view - For HTML output, the OUTPUT panel's Preview toggle shows you exactly how it will look
  • Try the example files - Learn from the included examples in the examples/ folder
  • Need more features? - See the XSLT Developer guide for parameters, the interactive debugger, profiling/tracing, and batch processing (all in the Transform panel and its OPTIONS & TOOLS section)
